Should the court grant the motion and suppress the store owner's trial testimony identifying the defendant as the robber?

一名警探向一名珠宝店最近被抢劫的店主出示了被告的照片，该被告此前曾犯下其他类似罪行。店主查看了照片，然后询问警探警方是否认为照片中的男子就是抢劫犯。在警探说“我们很确定”之后，店主陈述照片中的男子就是抢劫她的人。

被告因抢劫罪被起诉。其律师申请排除店主在庭审中指认被告为抢劫犯的任何证词。

法院是否应批准该动议，并排除店主指认被告为抢劫犯的庭审证词？
options:
A. No, because suppression of in-court testimony is not a proper remedy, even though the out-of-court identification was improper.
不应批准，因为排除庭审证词并非适当的救济措施，即使庭外指认不当。

B. No, because the out-of-court identification was not improper.
不应批准，因为庭外指认并无不当。

C. Yes, because the improper out-of-court identification has necessarily tainted any in-court identification.
应批准，因为不当的庭外指认必然污染了任何庭审中的指认。

D. Yes, unless the prosecution demonstrates that the in-court identification is reliable.
应批准，除非控方证明庭审中的指认是可靠的。
data.explanation:
Due process requires the suppression of unreliable testimony identifying the defendant as the perpetrator of the charged crime (ie, identification testimony) since it may inhibit the defendant's right to a fair trial. In-court identification testimony may be unreliable if it stems from unnecessarily suggestive out-of-court identification procedures arranged by police. Therefore, such in-court identification testimony is only admissible if the prosecution demonstrates that it is sufficiently reliable and poses no substantial likelihood of misidentification.

Here, the police detective showed the store owner a photograph of the defendant and explained that the police were "pretty sure" that the defendant was the robber. After this unnecessarily suggestive out-of-court identification procedure, the store owner identified the defendant as the robber (Choice B). As a result, the court should suppress the store owner's in-court testimony identifying the defendant as the robber unless the prosecution proves that her testimony is reliable despite the improper identification procedure.

(Choice A) Suppression of in-court identification testimony is a proper remedy if (1) that testimony stems from an unnecessarily suggestive out-of-court identification procedure and (2) the prosecution cannot prove that the in-court testimony is reliable.

(Choice C) An improper out-of-court identification does not always taint an in-court identification - eg, a witness's in-court testimony may be reliable despite a suggestive identification procedure if he/she could accurately describe the perpetrator before that procedure. Therefore, in-court identification testimony will only be suppressed if it is rendered unreliable by an improper out-of-court identification.

Educational objective: Due process requires the suppression of in-court identification testimony that was rendered unreliable (ie, substantially likely to result in misidentification) by an unnecessarily suggestive out-of-court identification procedure.



选项正确率统计：A选项 18%，B选项 10%，C选项 24%，D选项 47%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

Due process 要求排除指认被告为被控罪行作案人的不可靠证词（即指认证词），因为这可能会妨碍被告获得公平审判的权利。如果庭审指认证词源于警方安排的不必要的暗示性庭外指认程序，则该证词可能不可靠。因此，只有当控方证明此类庭审指认证词足够可靠，且不会造成错误指认的重大可能性时，该证词才可被采纳。

在本案中，警探向店主出示了被告的照片，并解释说警方“很确定”被告就是抢劫犯。在这个不必要的暗示性庭外指认程序之后，店主指认被告为抢劫犯（选项B）。因此，法院应排除店主在庭审中指认被告为抢劫犯的证词，除非控方能证明，尽管存在不当的指认程序，其证词仍然是可靠的。

（选项A） 如果（1）庭审指认证词源于不必要的暗示性庭外指认程序，且（2）控方无法证明该庭审证词是可靠的，那么排除该证词是一种适当的救济措施。

（选项C） 不当的庭外指认并不总是会污染庭审中的指认——例如，如果证人在该暗示性指认程序之前能够准确描述作案人，那么尽管存在该程序，其庭审证词也可能是可靠的。因此，庭审指认证词只有在因不当的庭外指认而变得不可靠时才会被排除。

教学目标：Due process 要求排除因不必要的暗示性庭外指认程序而变得不可靠（即，极有可能导致错误指认）的庭审指认证词。

References

U.S. Const. amends. V & XIV (due process).

Neil v. Biggers, 409 U.S. 188, 197 (1972) (holding that unnecessarily suggestive identification procedures violate due process if they create a substantial likelihood of misidentification).

Perry v. New Hampshire, 565 U.S. 228, 240 - 244 (2012) (stating that the reliability of identification testimony stemming from improper identification procedures must be assessed before admitting that testimony at trial).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Constitutional Protection
正确答案：D 应批准，除非控方证明庭审中的指认是可靠的。
Yes, unless the prosecution demonstrates that the in-court identification is reliable.
⚖️ 核心法律规则 (Legal Rule)
本题考察的是正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause) 对警方指认程序 (Identification Procedures) 的限制。

最高法院确立了处理“暗示性指认”的两步测试法 (Two-Prong Test)：
  • 1
    程序是否具有不必要的暗示性？
    (Was the procedure unnecessarily suggestive?)
    在本案中，警方只出示了一张照片（而不是一组照片），并且警探明确表示“我们很确定”就是此人。这具有极强的暗示性。
  • 2
    尽管存在暗示，指认是否仍然可靠？
    (Is the identification reliable despite the suggestiveness?)
    如果第一步成立，庭审指认（In-court identification）并不自动被排除。控方有机会证明，证人的指认有“独立来源” (Independent Source)，即指认是基于案发时的观察，而非警方的暗示。
参考判例：Manson v. Brathwaite (1977); Neil v. Biggers (1972)
🔍 案情分析 (Analysis)

1. 警方的错误：警探的行为（单张照片+确认性语言）构成了 unnecessarily suggestive 的程序。这违反了正当程序的基本要求。

2. 救济措施：被告律师申请排除庭审指认。由于庭外程序不当，举证责任转移给控方 (Prosecution)。

3. 结论：法院应当批准排除动议，除非控方能证明店主的指认是可靠的（例如：店主在抢劫时看清了罪犯的脸，且记忆清晰，不受照片影响）。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A 错：排除庭审证词是标准的救济措施。如果指认不可靠且源于非法程序，必须排除。
选项 B 错：只给看一张照片并告诉证人“就是他”，这是教科书级别的“不当暗示” (Improper)。
选项 C 错：这是最强的干扰项。不当的庭外指认并不必然 (Necessarily) 污染庭审指认。如果证人本身记忆深刻（可靠性高），庭审指认依然可以被采纳。法律采用的是“综合考量” (Totality of the Circumstances) 标准，而非“本身违法” (Per Se) 规则。
💡 MBE 考试技巧
在处理 Identification 问题时，记住这是一个“平衡测试”：
警方的不当行为 vs. 证人记忆的可靠性。

看到绝对化的词汇（如选项 C 中的 "Necessarily tainted"）要警惕，因为最高法院通常允许控方通过证明“可靠性”来补救警方的程序瑕疵。

questions.question:
A man was charged with murder. Several witnesses testified that the crime was committed by a person of the man's general description who walked with a severe limp. The man in fact walks with a severe limp. He objected to a prosecution request that the court order him to walk across the courtroom in order to display his limp to the jury to assist it in determining whether the man was the person that the witnesses had seen.
How should the court respond to the man's objection?

choices.a: Overrule the objection, because a criminal defendant has no legitimate expectation of privacy.
choices.b: Overrule the objection, because the order sought by the prosecution is a legitimate part of a proper courtroom identification process.
choices.c: Sustain the objection, because the order sought by the prosecution would constitute an illegal search and seizure.
choices.d: Sustain the objection, because the order sought by the prosecution would violate the man's privilege against self-incrimination.

一名男子被控犯有谋杀罪。多名证人作证称，罪行是由一名与该男子体貌特征相似且严重跛行的人所为。事实上，该男子确实严重跛行。他反对检方的一项请求，该请求要求法院命令他在法庭上行走，以便向陪审团展示其跛行，从而帮助陪审团确定该男子是否就是证人所见到的人。

法院应如何回应该男子的反对意见？
options:
A. Overrule the objection, because a criminal defendant has no legitimate expectation of privacy.
驳回反对意见，因为刑事被告没有合法的隐私期待。

B. Overrule the objection, because the order sought by the prosecution is a legitimate part of a proper courtroom identification process.
驳回反对意见，因为检方所请求的命令是正当的法庭身份识别程序的合法组成部分。

C. Sustain the objection, because the order sought by the prosecution would constitute an illegal search and seizure.
支持反对意见，因为检方所请求的命令将构成非法搜查与扣押。

D. Sustain the objection, because the order sought by the prosecution would violate the man's privilege against self-incrimination.
支持反对意见，因为检方所请求的命令将侵犯该男子的反对自证其罪特权。
data.explanation:
Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination


Testimonial communications
(privileged)		Real or physical evidence
(not privileged)
  • Oral testimony
  • Act of producing documents
  • Fingerprints
  • Handwriting samples
  • Voice tests
  • Photographs
  • Physical characteristics & clothing
  • Movements or gestures
  • Blood, DNA, urine samples
The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination protects defendants from being compelled to provide incriminating evidence - evidence that could be used, or lead to other evidence that might be used, against a person in a criminal prosecution. However, this privilege only applies to testimonial communications (eg, oral testimony, act of producing documents) - not real or physical evidence (eg, movements, gestures, blood test).

Here, several witnesses testified that the murderer walked with a severe limp (same as the man), so the prosecution requested that the court order him to walk across the courtroom to show the jury his limp. Since the privilege against self-incrimination does not apply to physical evidence (eg, a limp), the order sought is a legitimate part of a proper courtroom identification process (Choice D). Therefore, the man's objection should be overruled.

(Choices A & C) The Fourth Amendment protects a person's legitimate expectation of privacy by prohibiting unreasonable searches and seizures. However, a person has no legitimate expectation of privacy in his/her physical characteristics because they are exposed to the public. Therefore, an order compelling the man to display his limp would not constitute an illegal search and seizure or otherwise violate the Fourth Amendment.

Educational objective: The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination prohibits the government from compelling a defendant to provide incriminating testimonial communications - not real or physical evidence.

选项正确率统计：A选项 5%，B选项 69%（正确选项），C选项 0%，D选项 25%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

Fifth Amendment 反对自证其罪特权


证言通讯
（受特权保护）		实物证据
（不受特权保护）
  • 口头证词
  • 出示文件的行为
  • 指纹
  • 笔迹样本
  • 声音测试
  • 照片
  • 体貌特征与衣着
  • 动作或手势
  • 血液、DNA、尿液样本
Fifth Amendment 的反对自证其罪特权保护被告免于被强迫提供罪证——即在刑事诉讼中可能被用来指控某人，或可能引出其他可被用来指控某人的证据。然而，此特权仅适用于证言通讯（例如，口头证词、出示文件的行为）——而不适用于实物证据（例如，动作、手势、血液测试）。

在本案中，多名证人作证称凶手严重跛行（与该男子相同），因此检方请求法院命令他在法庭上行走以向陪审团展示其跛行。由于反对自证其罪特权不适用于实物证据（例如，跛行），检方所请求的命令是正当的法庭身份识别程序的合法组成部分（选项B）。因此，该男子的反对意见应被驳回。

（选项A和C） Fourth Amendment 通过禁止不合理的搜查与扣押来保护个人的合法隐私期待。然而，个人对其体貌特征没有合法的隐私期待，因为这些特征是向公众暴露的。因此，强迫该男子展示其跛行的命令不构成非法搜查与扣押，也没有以其他方式违反 Fourth Amendment。

教学目的： Fifth Amendment 的反对自证其罪特权禁止政府强迫被告提供具有罪证性质的证言通讯，但不包括实物证据。

References

U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).

Schmerber v. California, 384 U.S. 757, 764 (1966) (recognizing that self-incrimination does not apply to real or physical evidence).

Missouri v. Proctor, 535 S.W.2d 141, 144 - 45 (Mo. Ct. App. 1976) (holding that a compelled walk in the courtroom does not violate privilege against self-incrimination).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Constitutional Law
正确答案：选项 B
驳回反对意见，因为这是合法的法庭身份识别程序。
⚖️ 核心考点：第五修正案的适用范围
本题的核心在于区分“证言性证据” (Testimonial Evidence) 与 “实物/展示性证据” (Real/Physical Evidence)。
美国宪法第五修正案 (Fifth Amendment) 规定的反对自证其罪特权 (Privilege Against Self-Incrimination) 仅保护被告免受政府强迫其提供具有“证言性质”的交流。
受保护 (Protected)
证言性 (Testimonial)		 不受保护 (Not Protected)
实物性 (Physical)
涉及被告的思想过程或知识。

例如：
  • 口头供述
  • 书面陈述
  • 被强迫回答“你在哪里”
 仅涉及被告的身体特征。

例如：
  • 在法庭上行走 (本题考点)
  • 提供指纹 (Fingerprints)
  • 提供笔迹样本 (Handwriting)
  • 提供声音样本 (Voice exemplar)
  • 穿戴特定衣物
  • 抽血 (Blood sample)
🔍 案情深度解析
在本案中，检方要求被告在法庭上行走，目的是展示其身体特征（跛行，Limp），以便陪审团将其与证人描述的凶手特征进行比对。
这不涉及被告的思想、知识或信念。 被告并没有被要求“承认”他就是凶手，只是被要求展示他的身体状况。根据最高法院的判例（如 Schmerber v. California），这种强迫性的身体展示不属于“证言”，因此不违反第五修正案。
因此，法院应驳回（Overrule）被告的反对意见，允许检方的请求。选项 B 正确描述了这一行为是合法的身份识别程序。
❌ 为什么其他选项是错误的？
选项 D (Self-Incrimination): 这是最强的干扰项。错误原因如上所述，跛行属于实物证据，不受第五修正案保护。
选项 C (Illegal Search): 第四修正案 (Fourth Amendment) 禁止不合理的搜查。但是，观察一个人的公开身体特征（如走路姿势）并不构成“搜查” (Search)，因为一个人对向公众展示的身体特征没有合理的隐私期待。
选项 A (Privacy): 虽然结论（驳回反对）是对的，但理由太绝对。刑事被告在某些方面（如体内异物、私人文件）仍有隐私期待。但在本题语境下，展示走路姿势不侵犯隐私，选项 B 的理由在法律程序上更为精准。
💡 MBE 解题锦囊 遇到涉及“强迫被告做某事”的题目时，请使用“身体 vs. 大脑”测试法：
  • 如果政府想要的是被告大脑里的东西（记忆、想法、承认事实）👉 受第五修正案保护。
  • 如果政府想要的是被告身体上的东西（声音、长相、走路姿势、DNA）👉 不受保护，可以强迫提供。

questions.question:
Federal agents had a hunch that a local man was engaged in illegal gambling activities. An agent decided to enter the man's house while he was not at home and see what he could find. The agent discovered an envelope containing $5,000 in cash and an executive's business card. Returning the envelope to its place, the agent located and interviewed the executive, who admitted that he had paid the man $5,000 to settle a gambling debt; the executive also disclosed that the man regularly took illegal bets from the executive and several of his acquaintances. The agent then interviewed the acquaintances, who confirmed what the executive had told him. The agent then arranged to be introduced to the man at a local bar. After a few drinks, the man, unaware of the agent's identity, boasted that he was one of the biggest bookmakers in the state.
The agent testified to all of his investigation's discoveries before a grand jury, which returned an indictment against the man for illegal gambling activities, based solely on the agent's testimony. The man's attorney then filed a motion to dismiss the indictment, claiming that it rested on violations of the man's constitutional rights.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.a: No, because dismissal of the indictment is not the appropriate remedy.
choices.b: Yes, because much of the agent's testimony before the grand jury was inadmissible hearsay.
choices.c: Yes, because of the agent's unlawful search of the man's home.
choices.d: Yes, because of the agent's violation of the man's right to counsel.

联邦探员怀疑一名当地男子从事非法赌博活动。一名探员决定在该男子不在家时进入其住所，看看能发现什么。探员发现了一个信封，内含5000美元现金和一张高管的名片。探员将信封放回原处后，找到并询问了该高管。该高管承认他曾支付给该男子5000美元以了结一笔赌债；该高管还透露，该男子经常接受他本人及其几位熟人的非法投注。随后，探员询问了这些熟人，他们证实了该高管的说法。然后，探员安排在一家当地酒吧与该男子结识。几杯酒下肚后，该男子在不清楚探员身份的情况下，吹嘘自己是该州最大的庄家之一。

探员在大陪审团面前就其调查的所有发现作证，大陪审团仅根据该探员的证词，便以非法赌博活动为由对该男子提出起诉。该男子的律师随后提出动议，要求驳回起诉，理由是该起诉基于对该男子宪法权利的侵犯。

法院应否批准该动议？
options:
A. No, because dismissal of the indictment is not the appropriate remedy.
不应批准，因为驳回起诉并非适当的救济措施。

B. Yes, because much of the agent's testimony before the grand jury was inadmissible hearsay.
应批准，因为探员在大陪审团面前的大部分证词是不可采纳的传闻证据。

C. Yes, because of the agent's unlawful search of the man's home.
应批准，因为探员对该男子住所的搜查是非法的。

D. Yes, because of the agent's violation of the man's right to counsel.
应批准，因为探员侵犯了该男子获得律师帮助的权利。
data.explanation:
Grounds for dismissing indictment
  • Fails to charge actual crime
  • Omits elements of crime
Deficient indictment
  • Statute of limitations has run
  • Improper venue or jurisdiction
Defective grand jury proceedings
  • Admission of unqualified grand juror
  • Exclusion of grand juror based on race/gender
  • Prosecutorial misconduct
Constitutional violation
  • Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause
  • Sixth Amendment right to speedy trial
  • Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment due process clauses
Grand jury proceedings are investigatory in nature since they are used to determine whether probable cause exists to bring a criminal charge (ie, issue an indictment) against an individual. To help the grand jury in its investigation, the prosecutor can present any evidence that may be relevant to the grand jury's decision - even if that evidence was obtained in violation of the Fourth Amendment. And since these are not traditional judicial proceedings, the exclusionary rule (used to suppress illegally obtained evidence at trial) does not apply.

Here, the man filed a motion to dismiss the indictment, claiming that it was based on violations of his constitutional rights. Although the man's Fourth Amendment rights were violated when the agent conducted a warrantless search of the man's home, the agent's testimony regarding that search was relevant to the man's illegal gambling charge. Therefore, that testimony was properly presented to the grand jury, so the indictment should not be dismissed. Instead, the appropriate remedy will be to suppress any evidence obtained from the unlawful search at trial.

(Choice B) Hearsay is an out-of-court statement offered into evidence to prove the truth of the matter asserted. Although hearsay is generally inadmissible at trial, it can be presented at a grand jury proceeding where the rules of evidence do not apply. Therefore, though much of the agent's testimony would be inadmissible hearsay if offered at trial, it was properly considered by the grand jury.

(Choice C) A Fourth Amendment search is unlawful when it is conducted without a warrant and no exception to the warrant requirement applies (as seen here). But the exclusionary rule only prohibits the use of illegally obtained evidence at trial - not at a grand jury proceeding. Therefore, since the evidence from the unlawful search was relevant to the grand jury's probable cause determination, it was properly presented to the grand jury.

(Choice D) The Fifth Amendment right to counsel is not triggered unless the defendant is subjected to a custodial interrogation. And the Sixth Amendment right to counsel does not attach until judicial proceedings have commenced (eg, indictment issued). But neither right was violated here because the man met with the agent voluntarily (no custody) and was interviewed before judicial proceedings began.

Educational objective: The exclusionary rule prohibits the use of illegally obtained evidence at trial - not grand jury proceedings. Therefore, evidence from an unlawful Fourth Amendment search can be presented to the grand jury if that evidence may be relevant to the grand jury's probable cause determination.

选项正确率统计：A选项 66%（正确选项），B选项 1%，C选项 31%，D选项 1%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

驳回起诉的理由
  • 未能指控实际罪行
  • 遗漏犯罪构成要件
有缺陷的起诉书
  • 诉讼时效已过
  • 审判地或管辖权不当
有缺陷的大陪审团程序
  • 接纳了不合格的大陪审团成员
  • 因种族/性别排除大陪审团成员
  • 检察官不当行为
违反宪法
  • Fifth Amendment 禁止双重危险条款
  • Sixth Amendment 快速审判权
  • Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment 正当程序条款
大陪审团程序本质上是调查性的，因为其用于确定是否存在相当理由（probable cause）对某人提起刑事指控（即发出起诉书）。为协助大陪审团进行调查，检察官可以提交任何可能与大陪审团决定相关的证据——即使该证据是通过违反 Fourth Amendment 的方式获得的。而且，由于这并非传统的司法程序，证据排除规则（用于在审判中排除非法获得的证据）在此不适用。

在本案中，该男子提出动议要求驳回起诉，声称其起诉建立在侵犯其宪法权利的基础上。尽管当探员对该男子住所进行无证搜查时，该男子的 Fourth Amendment 权利确实遭到了侵犯，但探员关于该次搜查的证词与该男子的非法赌博指控相关。因此，该证词被恰当地提交给了大陪审团，故该起诉不应被驳回。相反，适当的救济措施是在审判中排除从该次非法搜查中获得的任何证据。

（选项B）传闻证据（Hearsay）是指在庭外作出的、为证明其所述事项真实性而提交的陈述。尽管传闻证据在审判中通常不被采纳，但在不适用证据规则的大陪审团程序中可以提交。因此，尽管探员的大部分证词如果在审判中提出将是不可采纳的传闻证据，但大陪审团恰当地考量了这些证词。

（选项C）当搜查在没有搜查令且没有任何搜查令要求之例外情况适用的情况下进行时（如本案所示），该 Fourth Amendment 搜查即为非法。但是，证据排除规则仅禁止在审判中使用非法获得的证据，而不适用于大陪审团程序。因此，由于来自非法搜查的证据与大陪审团的相当理由（probable cause）判定相关，该证据被恰当地提交给了大陪审团。

（选项D）Fifth Amendment 中的律师帮助权，仅在被告人受到羁押讯问时才被触发。而 Sixth Amendment 中的律师帮助权，直到司法程序已经启动（例如，发出起诉书）后才生效。但在本案中，这两种权利均未被侵犯，因为该男子是自愿与探员会面的（无羁押），并且是在司法程序开始之前接受询问的。

教学目标：证据排除规则禁止在审判中使用非法获得的证据，但不禁止在大陪审团程序中使用。因此，如果来自非法 Fourth Amendment 搜查的证据可能与大陪审团的相当理由（probable cause）判定相关，则可以将其提交给大陪审团。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Calandra, 414 U.S. 338, 351 - 52 (1974) (explaining that the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings).

MBE 刑诉法考点解析

大陪审团程序与宪法权利

正确答案：A 法院不应批准该动议，因为驳回起诉（Dismissal of Indictment）并不是针对非法取证的适当救济措施。
核心考点解析
证据排除规则的局限性

证据排除规则 (Exclusionary Rule) 是一项旨在威慑警察非法行为的规则，它禁止在刑事审判 (Trial) 中使用非法获得的证据。

然而，最高法院明确裁定，该规则不适用于大陪审团程序 (Grand Jury Proceedings)。

United States v. Calandra (1974)
大陪审团的性质

大陪审团的职能是调查性的，用于确定是否存在相当理由 (Probable Cause) 进行起诉，而非判定有罪或无罪。

  • 大陪审团可以听取在审判中不可采纳的证据（如传闻证据 Hearsay、非法搜查得来的证据）。
  • 基于非法证据作出的起诉书 (Indictment) 仍然是有效的。
被告应如何救济？

虽然起诉书不能被驳回，但被告的宪法权利确实受到了侵犯（非法的无证搜查）。

正确的做法是：在审判开始前，提出排除证据动议 (Motion to Suppress)。

如果动议成功，检察官将不能在审判中使用那个信封、现金以及由此衍生的证人证词（毒树之果），但这并不影响起诉本身的效力。

干扰项排除技巧
选项 B 错误（传闻证据）：
虽然探员的证词包含大量传闻 (Hearsay)，但联邦证据规则 (Federal Rules of Evidence) 不适用于大陪审团。大陪审团完全可以基于传闻证据提起公诉。
选项 C 错误（非法搜查）：
这是最具迷惑性的选项。搜查确实是非法的（违反 Fourth Amendment），但这只能导致证据在审判时被排除，而不能导致起诉被撤销。
选项 D 错误（律师权）：
  1. Fifth Amendment (Miranda): 被告在酒吧喝酒吹牛时并未处于“羁押讯问” (Custodial Interrogation) 状态，且不知道对方是警察，因此无 Miranda 权利问题。
  2. Sixth Amendment: 律师权在司法程序启动（如起诉）后才附着。此时起诉尚未发生。
MBE 考试策略

遇到此类题目，请遵循以下逻辑链条：

  1. 确认是否存在宪法违规（本题中有非法搜查）。
  2. 确认当前的程序阶段（本题是大陪审团/起诉阶段，而非审判阶段）。
  3. 关键判断：非法取证不影响大陪审团起诉的有效性。
  4. 结论：救济措施是“排除证据”，而非“驳回起诉”。

questions.question:
A public defender was appointed by the court to represent an indigent defendant on trial for felony theft. The defendant was offended when the public defender suggested that the defendant consider pleading guilty in light of the evidence against her and the generous plea bargain offered by the prosecution. As a result, the defendant asked the court to appoint another attorney. The court refused but explained that the defendant had the right to dismiss the public defender and proceed pro se. The defendant chose to continue being represented by the public defender. The defendant was subsequently convicted and received a one-year prison sentence that was suspended in full.
Has the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel been violated?

choices.a: No, because a defendant has no right to counsel when a sentence of imprisonment is not actually imposed.
choices.b: No, because the court complied with the defendant's right to the appointment of counsel.
choices.c: Yes, because the defendant was entitled to counsel of her own choosing.
choices.d: Yes, because the defendant's conviction shows that she was denied competent counsel.

questions.question:
An elementary school teacher detained a student after school. A state prosecutor, alleging that the detention was improper, filed an information charging the teacher with false imprisonment. At trial, the jury rendered a not-guilty verdict.
The student later revealed that on the day of the incident, the teacher had hidden the student in a closet to prevent him from being found. The state prosecutor then filed an information charging the teacher with kidnapping, which requires all of the elements required to establish false imprisonment as well as the movement or hiding of the victim. The teacher, contending that his constitutional rights were violated, has filed a motion to dismiss the charge.
Should the court grant this motion?

choices.a: No, because kidnapping requires proof of an additional element that false imprisonment does not.
choices.b: No, because the teacher was not previously subject to punishment for his behavior.
choices.c: Yes, because both crimes are based on the teacher's conduct at a single event.
choices.d: Yes, because the teacher was previously found not guilty of false imprisonment.

questions.question:
United States customs officials received an anonymous tip that heroin would be found inside a distinctively marked red package mailed from a foreign country to a particular address in the United States. Pursuant to this tip, United States customs officers intercepted and opened the red package and found heroin inside. They then resealed the package and left the heroin inside it. The FBI was notified and, as agents watched, the package was delivered to the address.
The FBI then secured a warrant to search the house for the package. About two hours after the package was delivered, agents executed the warrant at the house. The man who opened the door was arrested, and the agents found the package, unopened, in an upstairs bedroom closet. After seizing the package, the agents looked through the rest of the house. They found a machine gun in a small footlocker in the basement.
The man was charged with unlawful possession of the machine gun, among other crimes. He moved to suppress the use of the gun as evidence.
Should the court grant the motion to suppress the machine gun?

choices.a: No, because, having found the package, the agents had probable cause to believe that more narcotics could be located in the house and the gun was found in a proper search for narcotics.
choices.b: No, because narcotics dealers are often armed and the search was justified to protect the agents.
choices.c: Yes, because the initial search by the customs officers was without probable cause.
choices.d: Yes, because the search exceeded the authority granted by the warrant.

美国海关官员收到一条匿名举报，称从外国邮寄至美国一个特定地址的、标记独特的红色包裹内藏有海洛因。根据这条举报，美国海关官员拦截并打开了该红色包裹，在其中发现了海洛因。他们随后将包裹重新密封，并将海洛因留在其内。FBI接到了通知，在探员们的监视下，该包裹被投递至上述地址。

随后，FBI获得了一份搜查该房屋以寻找此包裹的搜查令。在包裹投递约两小时后，探员们在该房屋执行了搜查令。开门的男子被逮捕，探员们在楼上一个卧室的壁橱里找到了那个未开封的包裹。在扣押该包裹后，探员们搜查了房屋的其余部分。他们在地下室的一个小脚箱里发现了一支机关枪。

该男子被指控非法持有机关枪及其他罪行。他提出动议，要求排除该枪支作为证据的使用。

法院是否应批准排除该机关枪证据的动议？
options:
A. No, because, having found the package, the agents had probable cause to believe that more narcotics could be located in the house and the gun was found in a proper search for narcotics.
不应批准，因为在找到包裹后，探员有合理依据相信房屋内可能藏有更多毒品，而该枪支是在对毒品的合法搜查中发现的。

B. No, because narcotics dealers are often armed and the search was justified to protect the agents.
不应批准，因为毒贩通常持有武器，为了保护探员的安全，该搜查是正当的。

C. Yes, because the initial search by the customs officers was without probable cause.
应批准，因为海关官员的初次搜查缺乏合理依据。

D. Yes, because the search exceeded the authority granted by the warrant.
应批准，因为该搜查超出了搜查令授予的权限。
data.explanation:
Generally, a Fourth Amendment search or seizure must be authorized by a warrant that particularly describes the place to be searched and the items to be seized. Officers may seize illegal items discovered during the authorized search but cannot exceed the warrant's authority. Therefore, once items specified in the warrant are seized, the search must end unless another warrant is obtained or an exception to the warrant requirement applies. But if the search instead continues, any items seized during that illegal search should be suppressed.

Here, federal agents obtained a warrant to search the man's house for a red package (item specified in the warrant). Once they seized that package, their search should have ended. Instead, the agents exceeded the warrant's authority by continuing to search the house. And since the machine gun was discovered during that unreasonable search, it should be suppressed at trial.

(Choice A) Seizure of items specified in the warrant may provide police with probable cause to believe that other illegal items are in the searched location, but it does not allow police to continue their search. Instead, they must obtain a warrant or establish an exception to the warrant requirement.

(Choice B) Police do not need a warrant to conduct a protective sweep of the premises if:
  • they have reasonable suspicion that someone on the premises may pose a threat to their safety and
  • the sweep is limited to a cursory inspection of places where a person may be found (eg, a closet).
Here, though narcotics dealers are often armed (reasonable suspicion of threat), the agents could not search the small footlocker since a person could not fit inside.

(Choice C) Under the special government purpose exception to the warrant requirement, customs officials may conduct border searches and search international packages without a warrant or probable cause. Therefore, this is not a basis to grant the man's motion.

Educational objective: When police conduct a search pursuant to a warrant, they must end their search once the items specified in that warrant are seized. They can only continue their search if they obtain another warrant or establish an exception to the warrant requirement. But if they continue without doing so, any seized items should be suppressed.



选项正确率统计：A选项 12%，B选项 3%，C选项 4%，D选项 79%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

通常，美国宪法第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）所规定的搜查或扣押必须由搜查令授权，该搜查令需明确说明要搜查的地点和要扣押的物品。执法人员可以扣押在授权搜查期间发现的非法物品，但不能超出搜查令的权限。因此，一旦搜查令中指定的物品被扣押，搜查必须停止，除非获得另一份搜查令或有搜查令要求的例外情况适用。但如果搜查仍然继续，则在该非法搜查期间扣押的任何物品都应被排除。

在本案中，联邦探员获得搜查令，以搜查该男子房屋内的一个红色包裹（搜查令中指定的物品）。一旦他们扣押了那个包裹，他们的搜查就应该停止。然而，探员们继续搜查房屋，超出了搜查令的权限。并且，由于机关枪是在那次不合理的搜查中发现的，因此它在审判中应被排除。

(选项 A) 扣押搜查令中指定的物品可能会为警方提供合理依据，使其相信被搜查地点存在其他非法物品，但这并不允许警方继续搜查。他们必须获得一份新的搜查令或证明存在搜查令要求的例外情况。

(选项 B) 在以下情况下，警方无需搜查令即可对场所进行保护性巡视（protective sweep）：
  • 他们有合理怀疑（reasonable suspicion），认为场所内的某人可能对其安全构成威胁，并且
  • 巡视仅限于对可能藏人之处（例如壁橱）的粗略检查。
在本案中，尽管毒贩通常持有武器（构成威胁的合理怀疑），但探员不能搜查那个小脚箱，因为一个人无法藏身其中。

(选项 C) 根据搜查令要求的政府特殊目的例外原则，海关官员可以在没有搜查令或合理依据（probable cause）的情况下进行边境搜查和搜查国际包裹。因此，这不能作为批准该男子动议的依据。

教学目标：当警方根据搜查令进行搜查时，一旦搜查令中指定的物品被扣押，他们必须停止搜查。只有在获得另一份搜查令或证明存在搜查令要求的例外情况时，他们才能继续搜查。但如果他们未这样做而继续搜查，任何被扣押的物品都应被排除。

References

U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).

Marron v. United States, 275 U.S. 192, 196 (1927) (limiting the scope of a search and seizure to what is described in the warrant).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

刑事诉讼法 (Criminal Procedure)

搜查令的范围 (Scope of Warrant)

⚖️ 核心法则：搜查令的终止 根据第四修正案 (Fourth Amendment)，搜查令必须明确描述“搜查地点”和“扣押物品”。

一旦警方找到了搜查令中指定的全部物品，搜查令授予的权限即刻终止。继续搜查即视为无证搜查 (Warrantless Search)，除非有其他例外情况适用。

🔍 案情逻辑链

1
搜查令范围：仅针对“红色包裹” (The red package)。
2
执行过程：探员在楼上卧室壁橱找到了该包裹。
3
法律后果：此时，搜查令的目标已达成。搜查权限必须停止。
4
越界行为：探员继续搜查地下室并打开小脚箱 (Footlocker)，发现了机关枪。
✅ 正确答案：D

法院应批准排除该证据。

因为探员在找到包裹后继续搜查，超出了搜查令授予的权限 (Exceeded the authority of the warrant)。既然没有搜查令，且没有其他例外情况适用，该机关枪属于非法搜查的产物（毒树之果），必须被排除。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？

陷阱 A：合理根据 (Probable Cause) 不等于搜查权 虽然找到毒品可能给警方提供了相信屋内有更多违禁品的“合理根据”，但这不能免除搜查令要求 (Warrant Requirement)。警方应该停下来，基于新发现去申请第二张搜查令，而不能直接继续搜。
陷阱 B：保护性扫视 (Protective Sweep) 的限制 这是MBE常见的干扰项。警方确实可以在逮捕时进行“保护性扫视”以确保安全，但范围仅限于“人可能藏身的地方”。
题目特意强调机关枪是在“小脚箱” (Small footlocker) 里发现的。一个人显然无法藏在小箱子里，因此这不属于合法的保护性扫视。
陷阱 C：边境搜查 (Border Search) 的时效 海关最初的搜查是合法的（边境搜查例外），但这只证明了包裹里的海洛因证据合法。它不能为两小时后FBI在私人住宅内进行的、超出搜查令范围的地下室搜查提供正当性。
💡 MBE 提分技巧 在处理搜查令题目时，请像激光一样聚焦于“搜查令上写了什么”。
  • 如果是找“大象”，就不能打开“火柴盒”搜查。
  • 一旦找到了“大象”，搜查必须立即结束。
本题中，找到包裹的那一刻，就是合法与非法的分界线。
© MBE 备考助手 | Constitutional Law & Criminal Procedure

questions.question:
The police suspected that a 15-year-old high school student had committed a series of burglaries. One day, two officers went to the student's high school and asked the principal to call the student out of class and to search his backpack. While the officers waited, the principal took the student into the hall where she asked to look in his backpack. When the student refused, the principal grabbed it from him and found jewelry that she turned over to the officers.
The officers believed that the jewelry had been taken in one of the burglaries. They arrested the student, took him to the station, and gave him Miranda warnings. The student then asked to see a lawyer. The police called the student's parents to the station. When the parents arrived, the police asked them to speak with the student. The officers put the student and his parents in a room and secretly recorded their conversation with a concealed electronic device. The student immediately broke down and confessed to his parents that he had committed the burglaries.
The student was charged with the burglaries.
If the student moves to suppress the use of the statement he made to his parents, what is the student's best argument for exclusion?

choices.a: Once the student had invoked his right to counsel, it was improper for the police to listen to any of his private conversations.
choices.b: The meeting between the student and his parents was arranged by the police to obtain an incriminating statement.
choices.c: The police did not comply with the student's request for a lawyer.
choices.d: The student was in custody at the time the statement was recorded.

警方怀疑一名15岁的高中生犯下了一系列入室犯法罪。一天，两名警官前往该学生所在的高中，要求校长将该学生叫出教室并搜查其背包。在警官等待期间，校长将该学生带到走廊，要求查看其背包。当学生拒绝时，校长从他手中抢过背包，并发现了珠宝，随后将其交给了警官。

警官认为这些珠宝是在其中一起入室犯法罪中被盗的。他们逮捕了这名学生，将他带到警察局，并向他宣读了Miranda警告。该学生随后要求见律师。警方将该学生的父母叫到警察局。当父母到达后，警方要求他们与学生交谈。警官将学生及其父母安排在一个房间里，并用隐蔽的电子设备秘密录下了他们的对话。该学生立即情绪崩溃，并向其父母承认他犯下了那些入室犯法罪。

该学生被指控犯有入室犯法罪。

如果该学生动议排除使用其向父母所作的陈述，那么他主张排除的最佳论据是什么？
options:
A. Once the student had invoked his right to counsel, it was improper for the police to listen to any of his private conversations.
一旦该学生行使其律师权，警方再监听其任何私人对话都是不当的。

B. The meeting between the student and his parents was arranged by the police to obtain an incriminating statement.
警方安排该学生与其父母的会面，旨在获取一份致其入罪的陈述。

C. The police did not comply with the student's request for a lawyer.
警方未遵守该学生见律师的要求。

D. The student was in custody at the time the statement was recorded.
在陈述被录音时，该学生处于被羁押状态。
data.explanation:
The Fifth Amendment protects defendants from compelled self-incrimination. To safeguard this privilege, police must give a suspect Miranda warnings before a custodial interrogation (suspect in custody and subjected to interrogation). Police conduct amounts to an interrogation if that conduct is reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response based on the totality of the circumstances. Such circumstances include:
  • the suspect's personal characteristics (eg, age, mental capacity, religion)
  • whether police asked a close relative to speak with the suspect
  • whether police concealed that they were recording the suspect's conversations
  • other coercive tactics
A custodial interrogation must stop once a suspect invokes the Fifth Amendment right to counsel. If the interrogation continues, any statements made during that interrogation will be suppressed (ie, excluded) at trial.

Here, the student was arrested and taken to police headquarters (custody). Once he asked to see a lawyer, no interrogation should have occurred. However, the totality of the circumstances suggests that an interrogation took place since:
  • the student was only 15 years old
  • the police asked his parents to speak with him and
  • the police secretly recorded their conversation.
Therefore, the student's best argument for exclusion is that the police arranged the meeting with his parents to elicit an incriminating statement in violation of his Fifth Amendment rights.

(Choice A) Although police cannot conduct an interrogation once the Fifth Amendment right to counsel is invoked, they can still listen to a suspect's private conversations for safety or security purposes (eg, to thwart escape plans).

(Choice C) Police need only comply with a request for an attorney if they intend to conduct a custodial interrogation. Therefore, the officers' disregard of the student's request does not justify exclusion unless the student also shows that he was subsequently interrogated.

(Choice D) The Fifth Amendment excludes incriminating statements obtained when the defendant was in custody and subject to interrogation. Therefore, the fact that the student was in custody does not, by itself, trigger Fifth Amendment protections.

Educational objective: Police conduct amounts to an interrogation when that conduct is reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response under the totality of the circumstances, including the suspect's personal characteristics and coercive tactics.

正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

宪法第五修正案保护被告免于被迫自证其罪。为保障此特权，警方在进行羁押讯问（嫌疑人被羁押并接受讯问）前，必须向嫌疑人发出Miranda警告。如果根据整体情况，警方的行为被合理认为可能引出致其入罪的回应，那么该行为即构成讯问。这些情况包括：
  • 嫌疑人的个人特征（例如，年龄、心智能力、宗教信仰）
  • 警方是否要求近亲与嫌疑人交谈
  • 警方是否隐瞒了他们正在录制嫌疑人对话的事实
  • 其他胁迫性策略
一旦嫌疑人行使宪法第五修正案的律师权，羁押讯问必须停止。如果讯问继续，讯问期间所作的任何陈述将在审判中被排除。

在本案中，该学生被逮捕并带到警察总部（羁押）。一旦他要求见律师，就不应再进行任何讯问。然而，整体情况表明讯问已经发生，因为：
  • 该学生年仅15岁
  • 警方要求其父母与他交谈并且
  • 警方秘密录制了他们的对话。
因此，该学生主张排除的最佳论据是，警方安排其与父母的会面，旨在引出致其入罪的陈述，这侵犯了其宪法第五修正案的权利。

（选项A）尽管一旦嫌疑人行使宪法第五修正案的律师权，警方就不能进行讯问，但出于安全或安保目的（例如，挫败越狱计划），他们仍然可以监听嫌疑人的私人对话。

（选项C）只有在打算进行羁押讯问时，警方才需要遵守见律师的要求。因此，除非该学生同时证明他随后遭到了讯问，否则警官无视其要求本身并不足以成为排除证据的理由。

（选项D）宪法第五修正案排除的是在被告被羁押并且接受讯问时获取的致其入罪的陈述。因此，该学生被羁押这一事实本身并不会触发第五修正案的保护。

教学目标：当警方的行为在整体情况下，包括考虑嫌疑人的个人特征和胁迫性策略，被合理认为可能引出致其入罪的回应时，该行为即构成讯问。

References

U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).

Arizona v. Mauro, 481 U.S. 520, 526 - 28 (1987) (evaluating whether police conduct amounted to interrogation).

MBE 解析

Miranda 权利与“讯问”的定义

Constitutional Protection & Criminal Procedure

✅ 正确答案解析

最佳论据是 B：警方安排该学生与其父母的会面，旨在获取一份致其入罪的陈述。

核心考点：什么是“讯问” (Interrogation)？

根据 Miranda v. Arizona，警方在“羁押讯问” (Custodial Interrogation) 前必须给予警告。一旦嫌疑人要求律师 (Right to Counsel)，讯问必须立即停止。

本题的关键在于：警方没有直接提问，是否构成了“讯问”？

根据最高法院在 Rhode Island v. Innis 案中的定义，“讯问”不仅指明确的提问，还包括“警方的任何言行（除正常逮捕程序外），如果警方应当知道该言行合理可能引出致罪回应 (Reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response)”，即构成讯问的功能性对等物 (Functional equivalent)。

⚖️ 法律逻辑推演

在本案中，虽然是父母在和孩子说话，但存在以下关键事实：

  • 嫌疑人是 15 岁的未成年人，心理防线较弱。
  • 是警方主动要求父母与学生交谈（Police asked them to speak）。
  • 警方进行了秘密录音。

警方利用父母作为“代理人” (Agents) 或工具，创造了一种心理胁迫环境。警方应当知道，安排父母去劝说一个刚被捕的 15 岁少年，合理可能 (Reasonably likely) 会导致少年崩溃并坦白。

因此，警方的行为构成了功能性讯问。由于此时嫌疑人已要求律师，警方的这种“变相讯问”违反了第五修正案。

❌ 为什么其他选项不够好？

选项 A (隐私权/监听)：
这是错误的。在监狱或羁押场所，嫌疑人通常没有合理的隐私期待 (Expectation of Privacy)。警方为了安全目的监听对话本身并不违宪。违宪的关键在于警方“策划”了这次谈话来规避律师权，而不仅仅是“监听”。

选项 C (未提供律师)：
这是一个较弱的论点。警方没有立即变出一个律师并不自动导致证据排除。排除证据的触发点是：在嫌疑人要求律师后，警方继续进行讯问。重点必须落在“讯问行为”上。

选项 D (羁押状态)：
这是不完整的。Miranda 保护仅适用于“羁押”加“讯问”。仅证明在羁押状态 (In custody) 并不足以排除自愿供述（例如自发的供述）。必须证明存在讯问行为。

💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在处理 Miranda 考题时，务必检查两个要素：

  1. Custody (羁押)： 嫌疑人是否感到自由受限？
  2. Interrogation (讯问)： 警方是否在提问，或者是否在做一些“故意引诱”嫌疑人说话的事情？

如果警方利用第三方（如父母、狱友卧底）来获取供词：

  • 如果是警方安排/指使的 -> 视为警方讯问 (State Action)。
  • 如果是第三方主动要求的（如 Arizona v. Mauro 案中妻子坚持要见丈夫）且警方仅是被动记录 -> 通常不视为讯问。

questions.question:
A man held up a drugstore at 10:30 at night and drove away. His car broke down in an isolated area just outside the small city in which the crime occurred. The man walked to the nearest house and asked a farmer if he could stay until the next morning, explaining that he had been searching for his sister's home and had run out of gas. The farmer agreed to let him sleep on a couch in the basement.
During the course of the night, the farmer began to doubt the story the man had told him. Early the next morning, the farmer called the police for help and said he was suspicious and frightened of a stranger whom he had allowed to stay the night. The police went immediately to the house to assist the farmer and walked through the open front door. They found the man and the farmer drinking coffee in the kitchen. When they saw the man, they realized he matched the description of the drugstore robber. They arrested the man and found drugs taken during the robbery in the jacket he was wearing.
The man moves to suppress the evidence of the drugs at trial. Assume that the court finds that the police did not have probable cause to believe the man was the robber until they saw him inside the farmer's house and realized he matched the description.
How should the court rule on the man's motion to suppress?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the man had no ownership or other possessory interest in the premises.
choices.b: Deny the motion, because the police had the permission of the farmer to enter his house.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because, as a guest, the man has sufficient standing to contest the entry of the house without a warrant.
choices.d: Grant the motion, because, as a guest, the man has sufficient standing to contest the lack of probable cause at the time of the entry.

When they saw the man, they realized he matched the description of the drugstore robber. They arrested the man and found drugs taken during the robbery in the jacket he was wearing.

The man moves to suppress the evidence of the drugs at trial. Assume that the court finds that the police did not have probable cause to believe the man was the robber until they saw him inside the farmer's house and realized he matched the description.

How should the court rule on the man's motion to suppress?

一名男子在晚上10:30持械抢劫了一家药店后驾车逃离。他的车在犯罪发生地的小城外一个偏僻地区抛锚了。该男子走到最近的房子，询问一位农民是否可以让他留宿到第二天早上，并解释说他一直在寻找他妹妹的家，而且汽油用完了。农民同意让他睡在地下室的沙发上。

在夜里，农民开始怀疑该男子告诉他的故事。第二天一早，农民报警求助，称他对允许留宿的陌生人感到可疑和害怕。警察立即前往该房屋协助农民，并从敞开的前门进入。他们在厨房里发现该男子和农民正在喝咖啡。当他们看到该男子时，他们意识到他与药店劫匪的体貌特征相符。他们逮捕了该男子，并在他穿着的夹克中发现了抢劫时取得的毒品。

该男子在审判中动议排除毒品证据。假设法院认定，在进入农民家中看到该男子并意识到他与描述相符之前，警方没有相当理由相信该男子就是劫匪。

法院应如何裁定该男子的排除动议？
options:
A. Deny the motion, because the man had no ownership or other possessory interest in the premises.
驳回动议，因为该男子对该处所没有所有权或其他占有权益。

B. Deny the motion, because the police had the permission of the farmer to enter his house.
驳回动议，因为警察获得了农民进入其房屋的许可。

C. Grant the motion, because, as a guest, the man has sufficient standing to contest the entry of the house without a warrant.
支持动议，因为作为一名留宿客人，该男子有充分的资格对无证进入房屋的行为提出异议。

D. Grant the motion, because, as a guest, the man has sufficient standing to contest the lack of probable cause at the time of the entry.
支持动议，因为作为一名留宿客人，该男子有充分的资格对进入时缺乏相当理由的情况提出异议。
data.explanation:
To prevail on a motion to suppress, the defendant must first establish that he/she has standing to contest the allegedly unlawful Fourth Amendment search or seizure. Standing exists when the defendant has:
  • an ownership or possessory interest in the place or property searched or
  • a reasonable expectation of privacy in that place or property.
In Minnesota v. Olson , the Supreme Court held that an overnight guest has a reasonable expectation of privacy in the host's home and therefore has standing to contest a government search of that home. The search will be found unlawful if it is conducted without a warrant and no exception to the warrant requirement (eg, consent) applies.

Here, though the man had no ownership or other possessory interest in the farmer's home, he did have a reasonable expectation of privacy in the premises because he was an overnight guest (Choice A). This status gave him standing to contest the police entry of the house without a warrant based on probable cause (Choices C & D). However, the police did not need a warrant since the farmer (who owned the home) consented to their entry when he called the police for help.

Once the police entered the farmer's home, they noticed that the man matched the description of the robber. Since this observation gave them probable cause to believe that the man committed the robbery (a felony), they could - and did - arrest him without a warrant. As part of this arrest, the police properly conducted a warrantless search of the man's body (ie, a search incident to a valid arrest). Therefore, the drugs found in his jacket should be admitted at trial.

Educational objective: A defendant has standing to challenge a Fourth Amendment search when he/she has an ownership or possessory interest, or a reasonable expectation of privacy, in the place or property searched. Since an overnight guest has a reasonable expectation of privacy in the host's home, the guest has standing to contest a search of that home.



选项正确率统计：A选项 15%，B选项 75%（正确选项），C选项 5%，D选项 3%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

要在排除动议中获胜，被告必须首先证明其拥有对据称非法的第四修正案搜查或扣押提出异议的资格。当被告对被搜查的地点或财产拥有：
  • 所有权或占有权益或
  • 合理的隐私期望
时，即具备资格（standing）。在 Minnesota v. Olson 案中，最高法院裁定，留宿客人对主人的家享有合理的隐私期望，因此有资格对政府搜查该房屋的行为提出异议。如果搜查是在没有搜查令的情况下进行的，并且没有任何搜查令要求的例外情况（例如，同意）适用，则该搜查将被认定为非法。

在本案中，尽管该男子对农民的家没有所有权或其他占有权益，但他对该处所确实有合理的隐私期望，因为他是一名留宿客人（选项A）。这一身份赋予他资格，可以对警方在没有搜查令的情况下进入房屋的行为提出异议（选项C和D）。然而，警方并不需要搜查令，因为农民（房屋所有者）在报警求助时已经同意他们进入。

警察进入农民家后，注意到该男子的体貌特征与劫匪相符。由于这一观察为他们提供了相当理由（probable cause），相信该男子实施了抢劫（一项重罪），他们可以在没有逮捕令的情况下逮捕他——他们也确实这样做了。作为此次逮捕的一部分，警方合法地对该男子进行了无证搜查（即，合法逮捕附带的搜查）。因此，在他夹克中发现的毒品应在审判中被采纳为证据。

教学目标：当被告对被搜查的地点或财产拥有所有权、占有权益或合理的隐私期望时，他/她便有资格对第四修正案的搜查提出异议。由于留宿客人对主人的家有合理的隐私期望，因此该客人有资格对搜查该房屋的行为提出异议。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Minnesota v. Olson, 495 U.S. 91, 99 - 100 (1990) (holding that an overnight guest has a reasonable expectation of privacy in the host's home).
  • United States v. Robinson, 414 U.S. 218, 235 (1973) (explaining the search incident to a lawful arrest exception to the warrant requirement).

MBE 刑诉法考点解析

Fourth Amendment Search & Seizure
正确答案：B 驳回动议，因为警察获得了农民进入其房屋的许可。
⚖️ 法律推理逻辑

本题考察的是第四修正案中关于资格 (Standing) 与 同意 (Consent) 的交叉点。解题需要分两步走：

  • 1
    第一步：被告是否有资格提出异议？(Standing)
    是的。根据最高法院判例 Minnesota v. Olson，留宿客人 (Overnight Guest) 在主人的家中享有合理的隐私期望 (Reasonable Expectation of Privacy)。
    因此，被告有权挑战警方的搜查。
  • 2
    第二步：警方的进入是否合法？(Validity of Entry)
    是的。虽然无证搜查通常被推定为不合理，但同意 (Consent) 是一个主要的例外。房屋的主人（农民）主动报警并邀请警察进入。
    主人的有效同意使得警方进入房屋的行为合法。
  • 3
    第三步：证据是否可采？(Admissibility)
    警方合法进入后，看到被告符合劫匪描述（一目了然法则, Plain View），产生了相当理由 (Probable Cause) 进行逮捕。随后的搜查是合法逮捕附带的搜查 (Search Incident to Lawful Arrest)。
    结论：搜查合法，动议应被驳回。
❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 A (错误)
错误地认为被告没有资格 (Standing)。虽然他没有所有权，但他作为留宿客人拥有隐私权。如果选 A，意味着警察即使非法闯入，他也不能投诉，这违背了 Minnesota v. Olson。
选项 C & D (错误)
这两个选项虽然正确识别了被告拥有资格 (Standing)，但得出了错误的结论（支持动议）。
关键点：拥有“资格”只是让你能够走进法庭大门进行辩论，并不意味着你自动获胜。因为警方的搜查基于有效的“同意”，所以被告虽然有资格挑战，但挑战会失败。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧

在处理第四修正案题目时，请遵循以下思维导图：

1. 政府行为？ (Yes, Police)
2. 被告有 Standing 吗？ (Yes, Overnight Guest)
3. 有搜查令吗？ (No)
4. 有例外情况吗？ (Yes, Consent by owner)

陷阱提示：不要看到被告是“客人”就立刻认为他赢了（选项C/D），也不要认为他没房子就没权利（选项A）。要综合判断搜查本身的合法性。

MBE Criminal Procedure Review

questions.question:
A defendant was charged with attempted murder. At the preliminary hearing, the presiding judge heard the testimony of four prosecution witnesses and found that the prosecution had failed to establish probable cause that the defendant had committed any offense. Accordingly, she dismissed the charge.
The prosecutor then called the same four witnesses before a grand jury. The grand jury indicted the same defendant for attempted murder.
The defendant has moved to quash the indictment on the ground of double jeopardy.
How should the court proceed?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the defendant has not yet been in jeopardy of conviction on the attempted murder charge.
choices.b: Deny the motion, because the protection of the double jeopardy clause does not come into play until there has been a conviction or an acquittal.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because the dismissal of the first charge on the merits, whether correct or incorrect, bars any further prosecution.
choices.d: Grant the motion, unless the prosecution has evidence that was not presented in the first case.

data.questionStem:
Q85011

A defendant was charged with attempted murder. At the preliminary hearing, the presiding judge heard the testimony of four prosecution witnesses and found that the prosecution had failed to establish probable cause that the defendant had committed any offense. Accordingly, she dismissed the charge.

The prosecutor then called the same four witnesses before a grand jury. The grand jury indicted the same defendant for attempted murder.

The defendant has moved to quash the indictment on the ground of double jeopardy.

How should the court proceed?

一名被告被指控犯有谋杀未遂罪。在预审听证会上，主审法官听取了四名控方证人的证词，并认定控方未能建立被告犯有任何罪行的合理依据。因此，她驳回了该指控。

随后，检察官将同样的四名证人传唤至大陪审团面前。大陪审团以谋杀未遂罪对同一被告提起了公诉。

被告以“一事不再理”（double jeopardy）为由，请求撤销该公诉。

法院应如何处理？
options:
A. Deny the motion, because the defendant has not yet been in jeopardy of conviction on the attempted murder charge.
驳回该动议，因为被告尚未就谋杀未遂罪的指控陷入被定罪的危险境地。

B. Deny the motion, because the protection of the double jeopardy clause does not come into play until there has been a conviction or an acquittal.
驳回该动议，因为“一事不再理”条款的保护，在有定罪或无罪判决之前，尚不生效。

C. Grant the motion, because the dismissal of the first charge on the merits, whether correct or incorrect, bars any further prosecution.
批准该动议，因为第一次指控基于实体理由的驳回，无论其正确与否，都禁止任何进一步的起诉。

D. Grant the motion, unless the prosecution has evidence that was not presented in the first case.
批准该动议，除非控方拥有在第一次案件中未曾出示的证据。
data.explanation:
An indictment should be quashed (ie, dismissed) if it violates the Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause. Double jeopardy protects criminal defendants from undue harassment and expense by forbidding multiple punishments and a second prosecution for the same offense. This protection attaches once the defendant is in jeopardy of a conviction - ie:

when the jury is impaneled and sworn (jury trial) or when the judge begins to hear evidence (bench trial).

But if a criminal charge is dismissed before the defendant is put on trial before a trier of fact (judge or jury), then jeopardy does not attach and the prosecution can later prosecute the offense.

Here, the defendant was charged with attempted murder. But the charge was dismissed at the preliminary hearing - a pretrial hearing where the judge determines if there is probable cause to believe that the defendant committed the charged offense and should stand trial - so double jeopardy protections did not attach. The prosecution was therefore free to pursue a grand jury indictment for the same offense, and the court should deny the motion to quash that indictment.

(Choice B) Double jeopardy protections are triggered as soon as the defendant is put on trial - before a conviction or acquittal. Therefore, an indictment can be quashed on double jeopardy grounds even though the defendant has not been convicted or acquitted of the offense.

(Choice C) The dismissal of the first charge on the merits for lack of probable cause, whether correct or incorrect, does not bar further prosecution for this offense since jeopardy has not yet attached.

(Choice D) Jeopardy does not attach at preliminary hearings, so the prosecution can pursue charges for the same offense and use the same evidence to do so (eg, the prosecutor can use the same witnesses at the preliminary hearing and the grand jury proceeding) - new evidence is not required. But once jeopardy attaches, the prosecutor cannot pursue a second prosecution even if he/she has evidence that was not presented in the first case.

Educational objective: Fifth Amendment double jeopardy protections attach when a jury is impaneled and sworn (jury trial) OR a judge begins to hear evidence (bench trial). But if a criminal charge is dismissed before trial, jeopardy does not attach and the prosecution can later prosecute the offense.



选项正确率统计：A选项 53%（正确选项），B选项 32%，C选项 8%，D选项 5%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

如果一项公诉违反了第五修正案的“一事不再理”条款，则应予以撤销（即驳回）。一事不再理原则 (Double jeopardy) 通过禁止对同一罪行进行多重处罚和再次起诉，来保护刑事被告免受不当的骚扰和费用。此项保护在被告面临定罪危险时生效——即：

在陪审团组成并宣誓后（陪审团审判）或在法官开始听取证据时（法官审判）。

但是，如果一项刑事指控在被告交由事实审理者（法官或陪审团）审判之前被驳回，那么危险尚未生效，控方可以在之后就该罪行提起诉讼。

在本案中，被告被控犯有谋杀未遂罪。但该指控在预审听证会——一个审前听证会，由法官在此确定是否有合理依据相信被告犯有所指控的罪行并应接受审判——上被驳回，因此“一事不再理”的保护并未生效。因此，控方可以自由地就同一罪行寻求大陪审团的公诉，法院应驳回撤销该公诉的动议。

（选项B） “一事不再理”的保护在被告一经受审时即被触发——即在定罪或宣告无罪之前。因此，即使被告尚未被定罪或宣告无罪，一项公诉仍可能因“一事不再理”的理由被撤销。

（选项C） 基于缺乏合理依据这一实体理由而驳回第一次指控，无论正确与否，都不禁止就此罪行进行进一步起诉，因为危险尚未生效。

（选项D） 在预审听证会上，危险并未生效，因此控方可以就同一罪行提起诉讼，并可使用相同的证据（例如，检察官可以在预审听证会和大陪审团程序中使用相同的证人）——并不需要新的证据。但是，一旦危险生效，即使检察官拥有在第一次案件中未曾出示的证据，也不能进行第二次起诉。

教学目标：第五修正案的“一事不再理”保护在陪审团组成并宣誓（陪审团审判）或法官开始听取证据（法官审判）时生效。但是，如果一项刑事指控在审判前被驳回，则危险尚未生效，控方可以在之后就该罪行提起诉讼。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. V (prohibition against double jeopardy).
  • Serfass v. United States, 420 U.S. 377, 388 (1975) (explaining when jeopardy attaches).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Double Jeopardy
✅ 正确答案：A

法院应驳回被告的动议，因为被告尚未陷入被定罪的危险境地 (Jeopardy has not attached)。

⚖️ 核心法律规则

一事不再理 (Double Jeopardy) 保护被告免受对同一罪行的多次起诉。但这个保护只有在“危险生效” (Jeopardy Attaches) 之后才适用。

危险何时生效？(When does Jeopardy attach?)

  • 陪审团审判 (Jury Trial)： 当陪审团被选定并宣誓 (empanelled and sworn) 时。
  • 法官审判 (Bench Trial)： 当第一位证人宣誓并开始作证 (first witness is sworn) 时。

⚠️ 关键例外： 在审判前的程序（如大陪审团程序、预审听证会）中，无论结果如何，危险通常不生效。

🔍 案情深度解析
1
程序性质： 本案发生在 预审听证会 (Preliminary Hearing)。这是一个审前程序，目的是确定是否有“合理依据” (Probable Cause) 进行审判，而不是判定被告是否有罪。
2
法官的行为： 虽然法官听取了证人证词并驳回了指控，但这并不是对被告“有罪或无罪”的实质性审判 (Trial on the merits)。
3
结论： 因为从未进入正式审判阶段，Jeopardy 从未生效 (Did not attach)。因此，检察官可以重新组织证据，通过大陪审团 (Grand Jury) 再次提起公诉，这不违反第五修正案。
❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 B 错误： 它混淆了生效时间。Double Jeopardy 在审判开始时（陪审团宣誓或首位证人宣誓）就生效了，不需要等到最终判决（定罪或无罪）。如果审判中途无故终止，被告也可能受保护。
选项 C 错误： 预审听证会的驳回 (Dismissal) 并不等同于无罪释放 (Acquittal)。只有在危险生效后的无罪判决才绝对禁止再次起诉。
选项 D 错误： 是否有“新证据”不是关键。只要危险未生效（如本案），控方甚至可以用完全相同的证据再次起诉。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理 Double Jeopardy 问题时，第一步永远是问自己：“危险生效了吗？” (Did jeopardy attach?)

  • 如果是大陪审团拒绝起诉 ➡️ No Jeopardy.
  • 如果是预审听证会驳回 ➡️ No Jeopardy.
  • 如果是民事诉讼 ➡️ No Jeopardy (通常只适用于刑事).
  • 如果是陪审团已宣誓 ➡️ Jeopardy Attached!

questions.question:
A defendant was tried and convicted of murder. The defendant later filed a habeas corpus petition. He contended that because his lawyer at the murder trial had been representing the victim in a criminal charge at the time of the victim's death, the lawyer had a conflict of interest that prevented the defendant from receiving effective assistance of counsel. The lawyer had not revealed this conflict to the trial judge. The trial judge, having no reason to know about the conflict, had not inquired as to whether the lawyer had a conflict of interest that would disqualify her from serving as the defendant's lawyer.
If the defendant's contentions are established and the court overturns the defendant's conviction, what will likely be the reason?

choices.a: The defendant was also able to establish that the conflict adversely affected the lawyer's performance.
choices.b: The defendant was also able to establish that there was a reasonable probability that the outcome would have been different.
choices.c: The lawyer had a conflict of interest that prevented her from rendering effective assistance of counsel.
choices.d: The trial court failed to inquire as to whether the lawyer had a conflict of interest that would disqualify her from serving as the defendant's lawyer.

questions.question:
After a defendant was indicted and arraigned on a robbery charge, the defendant was required to participate in a lineup at a police station. The defendant's lawyer was not informed of the lineup, and the defendant did not waive his right to have his lawyer present. At the lineup, the victim of the robbery identified the defendant as the robber.
At trial, the victim again identified the defendant as the robber. When asked about her identification, the victim stated that she was sure the defendant was the robber because she remembered seeing the mole on his right cheek during the robbery. The defendant's lawyer moves to exclude this testimony as obtained in violation of the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel.
Will the court likely grant this motion?

choices.a: No, because the victim is testifying at the defendant's trial and is available for cross-examination.
choices.b: No, because the victim's identification was not based on the defendant's participation in the lineup.
choices.c: Yes, because the defendant's lawyer was not present at the lineup and the defendant did not waive his right to have his lawyer present.
choices.d: Yes, because the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel applied to the post-indictment lineup.

questions.question:
A man was prosecuted for selling cocaine to an undercover police agent. At his trial, the man testified that he only sold the drugs to the agent because the agent had told him that he (the agent) would be killed by fellow gang members unless he supplied them with cocaine. The prosecution did not cross-examine the man. As rebuttal evidence, however, the prosecutor introduced records, over the man's objection, showing that the man had two prior convictions for narcotics-related offenses. The court instructed the jury concerning the defense of entrapment and added, also over the man's objection but in accord with state law, that it should acquit on the ground of entrapment only if it found that the defendant had established the elements of the defense by a preponderance of the evidence. The man was convicted.
On appeal, the man argued that his conviction should be reversed for two reasons: the trial court violated the man's right to due process of law by imposing on the defense the burden of persuasion and erroneously admitted his prior convictions as substantive evidence concerning entrapment.
How should the appellate court rule on the man's conviction?

choices.a: Affirm the conviction.
choices.b: Reverse the conviction, because the trial court erroneously admitted the man's prior convictions as substantive evidence.
choices.c: Reverse the conviction, because the trial court violated the man's right to due process by imposing on the defense a burden of persuasion concerning entrapment.
choices.d: Reverse the conviction on both grounds.

Q85075

A man was prosecuted for selling cocaine to an undercover police agent. At his trial, the man testified that he only sold the drugs to the agent because the agent had told him that he (the agent) would be killed by fellow gang members unless he supplied them with cocaine. The prosecution did not cross-examine the man. As rebuttal evidence, however, the prosecutor introduced records, over the man's objection, showing that the man had two prior convictions for narcotics-related offenses. The court instructed the jury concerning the defense of entrapment and added, also over the man's objection but in accord with state law, that it should acquit on the ground of entrapment only if it found that the defendant had established the elements of the defense by a preponderance of the evidence. The man was convicted.

On appeal, the man argued that his conviction should be reversed for two reasons: the trial court violated the man's right to due process of law by imposing on the defense the burden of persuasion and erroneously admitted his prior convictions as substantive evidence concerning entrapment.

How should the appellate court rule on the man's conviction?

一名男子因向一名卧底警员出售可卡因而被起诉。在庭审中，该男子作证称，他之所以向该警员出售毒品，是因为该警员告诉他，除非他向其团伙成员提供可卡因，否则他（该警员）将被他们杀害。控方未对该男子进行交叉询问。然而，作为反驳证据，检察官在该男子反对的情况下，出示了记录，显示该男子有两项与麻醉品相关的先前定罪。法庭就“圈套抗辩”（entrapment）向陪审团作出指示，并在该男子反对但符合州法的情况下补充说，只有当陪审团认定被告已通过“优势证据”（preponderance of the evidence）证明了该抗辩的要件时，才应以圈套抗辩为由宣告其无罪。该男子被定罪。

在上诉中，该男子辩称，其定罪应基于两个理由被推翻：初审法庭将说服责任强加于辩方，侵犯了该男子的正当法律程序权利；并且错误地采纳其先前定罪作为关于圈套抗辩的实体证据。

上诉法庭应如何对该男子的定罪作出裁决？
options:
A. Affirm the conviction.
维持原判。

B. Reverse the conviction, because the trial court erroneously admitted the man's prior convictions as substantive evidence.
推翻原判，因为初审法庭错误地采纳了该男子的先前定罪作为实体证据。

C. Reverse the conviction, because the trial court violated the man's right to due process by imposing on the defense a burden of persuasion concerning entrapment.
推翻原判，因为初审法庭就圈套抗辩向辩方施加了说服责任，侵犯了该男子的正当程序权利。

D. Reverse the conviction on both grounds.
基于两个理由均推翻原判。
data.explanation:
Evidence of crimes or bad acts

(Federal Rule of Evidence 404) Admissible for noncharacter purposes - eg:
Motive/opportunity
Intent
Mistake/accident (absence of)
Identity
Common scheme/plan
Mnemonic: MIMIC

Under the harmless error test, an appellate court should affirm a conviction if the prosecution proves beyond a reasonable doubt that a trial error (eg, constitutional violation, evidentiary error) did not contribute to the defendant's conviction. Here, the man is challenging his conviction on two grounds: (1) the jury instruction on entrapment violated his right to due process and (2) the trial court improperly admitted his prior convictions into evidence.

To comply with due process, a jury instruction must explain that the prosecution has the burden to prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. However, due process only applies to criminal offenses - not affirmative defenses, which justify or excuse a defendant's criminal conduct but do not negate an element of the crime. Therefore, the defendant can bear the burden to prove an affirmative defense under any evidentiary standard.

Here, the man was prosecuted for selling cocaine and asserted entrapment as a defense. This defense excuses criminal behavior if (1) the behavior was induced by a government agent and (2) the defendant would not have otherwise committed the crime. And since entrapment does not negate an element of the crime, it is an affirmative defense. Therefore, the trial court's jury instruction - that the man had the burden to prove this defense by a preponderance of the evidence - did not violate due process and is not a ground for reversal (Choices C & D).

The man's second challenge relies on Federal Rule of Evidence 404, which generally bars the prosecution from introducing evidence of the defendant's bad character (eg, past crimes, prior bad acts). But this evidence can be introduced if:
  • it is being used for a noncharacter purpose - eg, to prove motive/opportunity, intent/knowledge, absence of mistake/accident, identity, or common plan/scheme (MIMIC) and
  • its probative value outweighs the danger of unfair prejudice - eg, records showing multiple convictions of unrelated or heinous offenses should be excluded because their usefulness does not outweigh the bias they would cause.
Here, the man's two narcotics-related convictions were admitted as substantive evidence - to rebut the man's entrapment defense. The convictions showed that the man may have committed the crime without the agent's inducement because he did so in the past (evidence of motive or intent - not bad character). And since the prejudice posed by those convictions was outweighed by the probative value of assessing the man's entrapment defense, this evidence was properly admitted. Therefore, his conviction should be affirmed (Choices B & D).

Educational objective: A criminal defendant can be required to prove an affirmative defense under any evidentiary standard. Additionally, evidence of a defendant's bad character is generally inadmissible but can be used for a noncharacter purpose (MIMIC) if its probative value outweighs the danger of unfair prejudice.

选项正确率统计：A选项 35%（正确选项），B选项 29%，C选项 16%，D选项 18%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

犯罪或不良行为的证据

(《联邦证据规则》Federal Rule of Evidence 404) 因非品格目的而可采纳 - 例如：
M动机/机会 (Motive/opportunity)
I意图 (Intent)
M错误/意外（不存在）(Mistake/accident (absence of))
I身份 (Identity)
C共同的计划/方案 (Common scheme/plan)
助记词：MIMIC

根据“无害错误”原则 (harmless error test)，如果控方能排除合理怀疑地证明，审判中的错误（例如，违反宪法、证据错误）并未导致被告被定罪，那么上诉法庭应维持原判。在此案中，该男子基于两个理由对其定罪提出质疑：（1）关于圈套抗辩的陪审团指示侵犯了他的正当程序权利；（2）初审法庭不当采纳其先前定罪作为证据。

为符合正当程序 (due process)，陪审团指示必须说明控方有责任排除合理怀疑地证明刑事犯罪的每一个构成要件。然而，正当程序仅适用于刑事犯罪——不适用于积极抗辩 (affirmative defenses)，积极抗辩旨在为被告的犯罪行为提供正当理由或予以辩解，但并不否定犯罪的构成要件。因此，被告可以被要求根据任何证据标准来承担证明积极抗辩的责任。

在本案中，该男子因出售可卡因被起诉，并主张圈套抗辩。如果（1）该行为是由政府人员引诱的，且（2）若非如此，被告本不会实施该犯罪，则该抗辩可以为犯罪行为提供辩解。并且，由于圈套抗辩并不否定犯罪的构成要件，因此它属于一种积极抗辩。因此，初审法庭的陪审团指示——即该男子有责任通过“优势证据”来证明此项抗辩——并未违反其正当程序权利，也不构成推翻原判的理由（选项C和D）。

该男子的第二个质疑依据是《联邦证据规则》Federal Rule of Evidence 404，该条规则通常禁止控方引入证明被告不良品格（例如，过往犯罪、先前的不良行为）的证据。但该证据在以下情况下可以被引入：
  • 其被用于非品格目的——例如，证明动机/机会、意图/知情、不存在错误/意外、身份或共同计划/方案 (MIMIC) 并且
  • 其证明价值超过了不公平偏见的风险——例如，显示多次不相关或令人发指的罪行的定罪记录应被排除，因为它们的有用性并不超过它们可能引起的偏见。
在本案中，该男子两项与麻醉品相关的定罪被作为实体证据采纳——用以反驳该男子的圈套抗辩。这些定罪表明，该男子可能在没有警员引诱的情况下也实施了该罪行，因为他过去就曾这样做过（这是证明动机或意图的证据——而非不良品格）。并且，由于这些定罪所带来的偏见风险，被其在评估该男子圈套抗辩方面的证明价值所超过，因此该证据被恰当地采纳了。因此，其定罪应予维持（选项B和D）。

教学目的：刑事被告可能被要求根据任何证据标准来证明一项积极抗辩。此外，证明被告不良品格的证据通常是不可采纳的，但如果其证明价值超过了不公平偏见的风险，则可以用于非品格目的（MIMIC）。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV § 1 (due process clause applied to the states).
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (due process clause applied to the federal government).
  • Patterson v. New York, 432 U.S. 197, 210 (holding that a defendant can bear the burden of proof for affirmative defenses).
  • Fed. R. Evid. 404(b)(2) (admissibility of prior criminal convictions as character evidence).

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law & Evidence
正确答案：A (Affirm the conviction)

本题涉及两个核心法律问题：举证责任的分配（正当程序条款）与先前犯罪记录的可采性（证据规则）。上诉法院应维持原判，理由如下：

考点一：积极抗辩的举证责任
法律规则： 虽然正当程序条款（Due Process Clause）要求控方必须排除合理怀疑（Beyond a Reasonable Doubt）地证明犯罪的每一个构成要件（Elements of the crime），但对于积极抗辩（Affirmative Defenses），最高法院允许各州将说服责任（Burden of Persuasion）转移给被告。

在本案中，圈套抗辩 (Entrapment) 是一种积极抗辩。它并不否认被告实施了犯罪行为（即不否定犯罪构成要件），而是主张因为政府的诱导才实施该行为，因此应免除责任。

根据最高法院在 Patterson v. New York 等判例中的确立的原则，州法律要求被告以优势证据标准 (Preponderance of the Evidence) 来证明积极抗辩，并不违反宪法。因此，初审法院的陪审团指示是合法的。

考点二：先前定罪作为实体证据
法律规则： 通常，先前犯罪记录（Prior Convictions）不能用于证明被告具有犯罪倾向（Propensity）。但是，当被告提出圈套抗辩时，他实际上是将自己的犯罪倾向 (Predisposition) 置于争议焦点。

圈套抗辩的核心在于证明被告原本是“无辜的”，是政府植入了犯罪意图。为了反驳这一点，控方有权引入被告先前的类似犯罪记录，以证明被告本身就具有实施此类犯罪的倾向 (Predisposition)，而不仅仅是因为警察的诱导。

在这种情况下，先前的毒品定罪被视为实体证据 (Substantive Evidence)，用于证明被告的意图和心理状态（属于 FRE 404(b) 中的 MIMIC 例外之一，即 Intent/State of Mind 的延伸），而不仅仅是弹劾证据。只要其证明价值超过不公平偏见（FRE 403），即为可采。

💡 MBE 解题技巧
  • 区分“构成要件”与“积极抗辩”： 如果法律要求被告证明他“没有杀人意图”（这是犯罪要件），那是违宪的；但如果要求被告证明“精神错乱”或“受到圈套”（这是借口/抗辩），通常是合宪的。
  • 圈套抗辩的特效： 一旦看到题目中出现 Entrapment Defense，立即联想：控方几乎总是可以引入被告过去的类似犯罪记录来证明 Predisposition。这是 Evidence 题中的常见例外。

questions.question:
A defendant was charged with the capital offense of first-degree murder, for which the only available penalties were death or life in prison without parole. During jury selection, the trial court, over the defendant's objection, granted the prosecution's for-cause challenge of five prospective jurors who indicated upon questioning by both parties that they personally were opposed to the death penalty and were unsure if they could ever vote to impose it. The jury convicted the defendant and, following a separate sentencing hearing, sentenced him to death.
On appeal, the defendant's only argument was that excusing the prospective jurors violated his federal constitutional right to be tried by a jury chosen from a fair cross section of the community.
How should the court of appeals rule on the conviction and the death sentence?

choices.a: Affirm both.
choices.b: Affirm the conviction, but reverse the death sentence and remand for a new sentencing hearing before a different jury.
choices.c: Affirm the conviction, but reverse the death sentence and remand for resentencing to life in prison.
choices.d: Reverse both.

Q85019

A defendant was charged with the capital offense of first-degree murder, for which the only available penalties were death or life in prison without parole. During jury selection, the trial court, over the defendant's objection, granted the prosecution's for-cause challenge of five prospective jurors who indicated upon questioning by both parties that they personally were opposed to the death penalty and were unsure if they could ever vote to impose it. The jury convicted the defendant and, following a separate sentencing hearing, sentenced him to death.

On appeal, the defendant's only argument was that excusing the prospective jurors violated his federal constitutional right to be tried by a jury chosen from a fair cross section of the community.

How should the court of appeals rule on the conviction and the death sentence?

一名被告被控犯有一级谋杀的死刑罪，对此罪行仅有的刑罚是死刑或不得假释的无期徒刑。在陪审团遴选期间，审判法院不顾被告的反对，批准了控方对五名准陪审员提出的有因回避申请，这些准陪审员在双方的讯问中表示，他们个人反对死刑，并且不确定自己是否能够投票判处死刑。陪审团裁定被告有罪，并在一次单独的量刑听证后，判处其死刑。

在上诉中，被告的唯一论点是，排除这些准陪审员的做法侵犯了其由能够公正代表社会各阶层的群体中选出的陪审团进行审判的联邦宪法权利。

上诉法院应如何对该定罪和死刑判决作出裁决？
options:
A. Affirm both.
两者均予以维持。

B. Affirm the conviction, but reverse the death sentence and remand for a new sentencing hearing before a different jury.
维持定罪，但推翻死刑判决，并发回由不同的陪审团进行新的量刑听证。

C. Affirm the conviction, but reverse the death sentence and remand for resentencing to life in prison.
维持定罪，但推翻死刑判决，并发回重审改判为无期徒刑。

D. Reverse both.
两者均予以推翻。
data.explanation:
An appellate court should automatically reverse a defendant's conviction and sentence if a structural error - eg, a violation of a defendant's Sixth Amendment right to an impartial jury - occurred before or during trial. Impartiality has two requirements:
  • the jury pool must be selected from a fair cross-section of the community and
  • the impaneled jury must be unbiased and able to decide the case based on the evidence presented at trial.

To ensure that the impaneled jury is impartial during the guilt and penalty phases of a capital punishment (ie, death penalty) case, the defense and prosecution can challenge potential jurors for cause. A for-cause challenge should be granted if a potential juror's views would prevent or substantially impair his/her ability to impartially decide the case or impose the death penalty.

Here, during jury selection, the judge granted the prosecution's for-cause challenge of five prospective jurors who were opposed to the death penalty and unsure if they could ever vote to impose it. Since those views would substantially impair the jurors' ability to impartially decide this first-degree murder (capital offense) case, they were properly excused. Therefore, the defendant's right to an impartial jury was not violated, and the appellate court should affirm his conviction and death sentence (Choices B, C, & D).

Educational objective: The Sixth Amendment guarantees a criminal defendant the right to be tried by an impartial jury - ie, a jury pool selected from a fair cross-section of the community and an unbiased impaneled jury. Therefore, a potential juror whose views would substantially impair his/her ability to impartially decide the case can be challenged for cause.



选项正确率统计：A选项 76%（正确选项），B选项 13%，C选项 2%，D选项 7%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

如果在审判前或审判中出现了结构性错误——例如，侵犯了被告受Sixth Amendment保护的获得公正陪审团审判的权利——上诉法院应自动推翻被告的定罪和判决。公正性有两个要求：
  • 备选陪审员库必须从能够公正代表社会各阶层的群体中选出，并且
  • 最终选定的陪审团必须是无偏见的，并且能够根据庭审中出示的证据来裁决案件。

为确保最终选定的陪审团在死刑案件的定罪和量刑阶段保持公正，辩方和控方可以对准陪审员提出有因回避申请。如果一名准陪审员的观点会阻止或实质性削弱其公正裁决案件或判处死刑的能力，那么对其提出的有因回避申请就应被批准。

在本案中，陪审团遴选期间，法官批准了控方对五名准陪审员提出的有因回避申请，这些准陪审员反对死刑，且不确定自己是否能够投票判处死刑。由于这些观点会实质性削弱陪审员公正裁决此一级谋杀（死刑罪）案件的能力，他们被正当地排除了。因此，被告获得公正陪审团审判的权利未受侵犯，上诉法院应维持其定罪和死刑判决（选项B、C、D错误）。

教学目标：Sixth Amendment保障刑事被告获得公正陪审团审判的权利——即，备选陪审员库需从能够公正代表社会各阶层的群体中选出，且最终选定的陪审团需无偏见。因此，如果一名准陪审员的观点会实质性削弱其公正裁决案件的能力，则可以对其提出有因回避申请。

References

Wainwright v. Witt, 469 U.S. 412, 424 (1985) (establishing the impartial juror standard in capital punishment cases).

Gray v. Mississippi, 481 U.S. 648, 668 (1987) (holding that the improper dismissal of a juror in a death penalty case is structural error).

MBE 考题解析

宪法权利 / 刑事诉讼程序
正确判决
A. 维持定罪与死刑判决 (Affirm both)

本题考察的是第六修正案 (Sixth Amendment) 中关于陪审团公正性以及死刑案件中陪审员遴选的特殊规则。

⚖️ 核心法律规则
1. 公平代表社会各阶层 (Fair Cross-Section Requirement)

被告有权要求陪审团的候选库 (Venire/Jury Pool) 来自社区的公平截面。但是，这一权利并不延伸到最终选出的审判陪审团 (Petit Jury)。

也就是说，被告无权要求最终坐在法庭上的12个人必须完美代表社会的人口比例。

2. 死刑资格审查 (Death Qualification)

在死刑案件中，如果准陪审员的观点会“阻止或实质性削弱” (Prevent or substantially impair) 其履行职责（即依法判处死刑），控方可以提出有因回避 (Challenge for Cause) 将其排除。

这种排除不违反“公平代表社会各阶层”的原则。

📖 判例依据与逻辑

本题的逻辑直接源于美国最高法院的两个著名判例：

  • Wainwright v. Witt (1985)：确立了标准。如果陪审员因反对死刑而无法公正裁决，可以被排除。题目中陪审员表示“不确定是否能投票判死刑”，符合被排除的标准。
  • Lockhart v. McCree (1986)：这是本题的题眼。被告辩称排除这些反死刑者违反了“Fair Cross-Section”权利。最高法院明确裁定：因反对死刑而被排除的人群不属于“独特的群体” (Distinctive Group)。

结论：排除这些陪审员既符合程序（有因回避），也没有侵犯被告的宪法权利。因此，定罪和量刑均无误。

❌ 为什么推翻判决是错误的？

选项 B、C、D 都主张推翻判决或改判，这需要建立在初审法院犯了“可逆转错误” (Reversible Error) 的基础上。

既然排除那些“无法依法判处死刑”的陪审员是合宪的，那么初审法院就没有错误。没有错误，上诉法院就必须维持原判 (Affirm)。

MBE 解题技巧

看到"Fair Cross-Section"（公平截面）论点时，请记住：

  1. 它只适用于陪审员候选库 (Pool)，不适用于最终选出的陪审团。
  2. 它只保护基于种族、性别等固有特征的群体，不保护基于“政治观点”或“对死刑态度”的群体。

如果题目中被告仅仅因为“反死刑者被排除”而主张违反Fair Cross-Section，该主张必败。

questions.question:
On October 22, a police officer submitted an application for a warrant to search a man's residence for cocaine. In the application, the officer stated under oath that he believed there was cocaine at that location because of information supplied to him on the morning of October 22 by an informant. He described the informant as a cocaine user who had previously supplied accurate information concerning the use of cocaine in the community and summarized what the informant had told him as follows: the previous night, October 21, the informant was in the man's house. The man gave her cocaine. She also saw three cellophane bags containing cocaine in the man's bedroom.
The warrant was issued and a search of the man's residence was conducted on October 22. The search turned up a quantity of heroin but no cocaine. The man was arrested and charged with possession of heroin. The man moved to suppress the use of the heroin as evidence, contending that the informant was not in his residence on October 21 or at any other time.
If, after hearing evidence, the judge concludes that the statement in the application attributed to the informant is incorrect and grants the motion to suppress, what will be the most likely reason?

choices.a: The application contained a material statement that was false.
choices.b: The court also found that the informant's statement was a deliberate lie.
choices.c: The court also found that the officer knew the statement was false.
choices.d: The informant's statement was false and no cocaine was found in the house.

10月22日，一名警官提交了搜查一名男子住所中可卡因的搜查令申请。在该申请中，该警官宣誓称，他相信该地点有可卡因，其依据是10月22日上午一名线人向他提供的情报。他描述该线人是一名可卡因使用者，此前曾提供过关于社区内可卡因使用情况的准确信息，并将其线人告知他的内容总结如下：前一天晚上，即10月21日，该线人在这名男子的家中。该男子给了她可卡因。她还在该男子的卧室里看到了三个装有可卡因的玻璃纸袋。

搜查令被签发，并于10月22日对该男子的住所进行了搜查。搜查发现了若干海洛因，但没有发现可卡因。该男子因持有海洛因而被捕并被起诉。该男子申请排除将海洛因用作证据，主张该线人于10月21日或任何其他时间均未在其住所内。

如果在听取证据后，法官认定申请书中引述的线人陈述不实，并批准了排除动议，最可能的原因是什么？
options:
A. The application contained a material statement that was false.
申请书中包含一项虚假的重大陈述。

B. The court also found that the informant's statement was a deliberate lie.
法庭还认定线人的陈述是蓄意谎言。

C. The court also found that the officer knew the statement was false.
法庭还认定警官知道该陈述是虚假的。

D. The informant's statement was false and no cocaine was found in the house.
线人的陈述是虚假的，且在房屋内未发现可卡因。
data.explanation:
A search warrant is presumptively valid if it (1) is issued by a neutral and detached magistrate (ie, judge) based on probable cause, (2) is supported by a sworn oath or affidavit, and (3) particularly describes the place to be searched and items to be seized. However, a defendant may challenge that presumption and invalidate the warrant if he/she can prove by a preponderance of the evidence that:

the application contains a false statement necessary to the finding of probable cause and the officer submitting the application knew the statement was false or recklessly disregarded its falsity.

Any evidence seized pursuant to an invalid search warrant should be suppressed at trial.

Here, the officer's application for a search warrant stated that he believed there was cocaine at the man's residence based on information supplied by an informant. The trial judge concluded that the statement in the application attributed to the informant was incorrect (false statement). And that statement was the only basis for the officer's application (necessary to finding of probable cause). Therefore, the motion to suppress will likely be granted if the court also finds that the officer knew the statement was false (or recklessly disregarded its falsity) (Choice A).

(Choices B & D) The fact that the informant's statement was a deliberate lie and that no cocaine was found in the house helps show that the application contains a false statement. But the search warrant would only be invalid if the officer knew, or recklessly failed to determine, that the statement was false. Without such evidence, the court would not grant the motion to suppress.

Educational objective: A search warrant is invalid if the preponderance of the evidence shows that (1) the application contains a false statement necessary to the finding of probable cause and (2) the officer who submitted the application knew that the statement was false or recklessly disregarded its falsity.



选项正确率统计：A选项 11%，B选项 2%，C选项 79%（正确选项），D选项 5%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

一份搜查令在以下情况下被推定为有效：(1) 由中立且独立的司法官员（即法官）基于相当理由签发，(2) 有经宣誓的证词或书面陈述支持，以及 (3) 明确描述了待搜查的地点和待扣押的物品。但是，被告可以通过优势证据证明以下情况，从而挑战该推定并使搜查令无效：

申请书中包含一项对于认定相当理由而言属必要的虚假陈述，并且提交申请的警官知道该陈述是虚假的或鲁莽地无视其虚假性。

任何依据无效搜查令所扣押的证据，在审判中应予以排除。

在本案中，警官的搜查令申请书陈述，他基于线人提供的情报，相信该男子住所有可卡因。初审法官认定，申请书中引述的线人陈述不实（虚假陈述）。而该陈述是警官申请的唯一依据（对于认定相当理由而言是必要的）。因此，如果法庭同时认定警官知道该陈述是虚假的（或鲁莽地无视其虚假性），则排除动议很可能会被批准（选项A）。

（选项B和D）线人的陈述是蓄意谎言以及在房屋内未发现可卡因这一事实，有助于证明申请书中包含虚假陈述。但只有在警官知道或鲁莽地未能确定该陈述是虚假的情况下，搜查令才会无效。没有此类证据，法庭不会批准排除动议。

教学目标：如果优势证据表明以下两点，则搜查令无效：(1) 申请书中包含一项对于认定相当理由而言属必要的虚假陈述，以及 (2) 提交申请的警官知道该陈述是虚假的或鲁莽地无视其虚假性。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Franks v. Delaware, 438 U.S. 154, 156 (1978) (holding that an officer's knowing or reckless inclusion of a material false statement in an application for a search warrant invalidates the warrant).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析：搜查令的有效性

正确答案：C
核心考点：Franks Hearing (弗兰克斯听证) 根据最高法院在 Franks v. Delaware (1978) 中的裁决，被告要成功挑战搜查令的有效性并排除证据，必须证明以下两点：
  1. 申请书中包含虚假陈述 (False statement)；且
  2. 警官是故意 (Knowingly) 或鲁莽地 (Recklessly) 做出该虚假陈述的。
深度解析
1. 搜查令的推定有效性
通常情况下，只要搜查令由中立的法官签发且基于表面上的相当理由 (Probable Cause)，它就是有效的。
2. 挑战有效性的唯一路径
本题中，法官已经批准了排除证据的动议 (Motion to Suppress)。这意味着法官不仅认定信息是错误的，还必须认定警官的行为存在不当。
3. 为什么必须选 C？
仅仅因为申请书中有错误信息（选项A），或者线人撒谎（选项B），并不足以使搜查令无效。如果警官是诚实且合理地相信了线人的谎言，那么警官的行为没有过错，搜查令依然有效（基于善意例外 Good Faith Exception）。

因此，要让法官排除证据，法庭必须认定警官本人知道该陈述是虚假的（或者鲁莽地无视真相）。这就是选项 C 的逻辑。
为什么其他选项是错误的？
选项 A (仅包含虚假陈述)：
错误。如果警官被线人蒙骗，但他诚实地相信情报是真实的，那么搜查令仍然有效。单纯的“错误”不足以推翻搜查令。
选项 B (线人蓄意撒谎)：
错误。宪法第四修正案约束的是政府行为（警察），而不是私人线人。只要警察没有参与撒谎且没有鲁莽行事，线人的谎言不会导致搜查令无效。
选项 D (结果未发现可卡因)：
错误。搜查令的有效性取决于签发时是否具备相当理由，而不是搜查的结果。事后未发现证据不能反推搜查令无效。
💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip) 在处理涉及搜查令瑕疵的题目时，请记住：
如果是线人撒谎，搜查令通常有效（除非警察也知情）。
如果是警察撒谎（或鲁莽编造），搜查令才无效。
关键词是警察的主观恶性 (Bad Faith / Mens Rea)。

questions.question:
A defendant was staying at an upscale hotel where he was using his room to run an illegal business. Based on an uncorroborated informant's tip, the police requested that the hotel manager allow them to enter the defendant's room to search for illegal firearms. The manager complied with the request and let the police access the defendant's hotel room without a warrant. Once the police entered the room, they found several illegal firearms that were in plain view.
The defendant was charged with possession of the firearms. He filed a motion to suppress evidence of the firearms prior to trial.
How should the court rule on the defendant's motion to suppress?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the firearms were in plain view.
choices.b: Deny the motion, because the hotel manager had authority to consent to the search of the room.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because the defendant had a reasonable expectation of privacy in the hotel room.
choices.d: Grant the motion, because the informant's tip was not corroborated.

questions.question:
One evening, a man called his sister from jail and told her that he had been arrested. The man did not mention retaining a lawyer, so the sister promptly retained a lawyer on the man's behalf. The lawyer contacted the police and demanded to be present when the man was questioned. The police told the lawyer that the man had fallen asleep and would not be questioned until the morning. However, later that evening, the police gave the man Miranda warnings and questioned him for two hours before he voluntarily confessed to the crime. The man never requested a lawyer, and the police did not mention the man's lawyer before or during the interrogation. At his arraignment the next morning, the man was formally charged with robbery.
Should the man's confession be excluded as a violation of his Sixth Amendment right to counsel?

choices.a: No, because the man had not been arraigned when he confessed.
choices.b: No, because the man waived his right to counsel by voluntarily confessing after receiving Miranda warnings.
choices.c: Yes, because a lawyer had been retained to represent the man before he confessed.
choices.d: Yes, because the police failed to inform the man that his lawyer had requested to be present during his interrogation.

questions.question:
A grand jury returned an indictment charging a man with bank robbery and when he could not make bond, he was jailed pending trial. He had received Miranda warnings when arrested and had made no statement at that time. The prosecutor arranged to have an undercover informant placed as the man's cellmate and instructed the informant to find out about the bank robbery without asking any direct questions about it. The informant, once in the cell, constantly boasted about the crimes that he had committed. Not to be outdone, the man finally declared that he had committed the bank robbery with which he was charged.
At the man's trial, his attorney moved to exclude any testimony from the informant concerning the man's boast.
How will the court likely rule on the motion?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the man had received Miranda warnings.
choices.b: Deny the motion, because the man was not interrogated by the informant.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because the man's privilege against self-incrimination was violated.
choices.d: Grant the motion, because the man's right to counsel was violated.
