MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / 刑事诉讼法
Correct Answer: D

本题的核心考点在于第五修正案 (Fifth Amendment) 下的反对自证其罪特权，特别是关于 Miranda 警告 的放弃 (Waiver) 必须具备的要素。

⚖️ 法律规则解析

根据 Miranda v. Arizona 及其后续判例，警方在进行羁押讯问 (Custodial Interrogation) 之前，必须告知嫌疑人其权利。

嫌疑人可以放弃这些权利，但放弃必须满足三个条件：

  • 知情 (Knowingly)
  • 明智 (Intelligently)
  • 自愿 (Voluntarily)
关键点： 任何由警方胁迫 (Coercion) 导致的放弃都是无效的。胁迫不仅包括身体暴力，还包括心理威胁（如威胁剥夺家庭福利、威胁生意破产等）。
🔍 案情应用分析

1. 羁押 (Custody):
警员将女子扑倒并反剪双臂，此时她显然已被剥夺自由，处于羁押状态。

2. 讯问 (Interrogation):
警员直接问：“告诉我们你做了什么...”，这构成了讯问。

3. 胁迫 (Coercion):
警员威胁说：“否则我们将让你关门大吉，让你的家人去领救济金 (shut you down and see your family on relief)”。

由于存在明显的警方胁迫，该女子并没有“自愿”放弃她的沉默权。因此，她在这种压力下做出的供述违反了第五修正案，法院应批准 (Grant) 排除该证据的动议。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (Hot Pursuit / 紧急追捕):
虽然“紧急追捕”允许警方无证进入住宅进行搜查（第四修正案例外），但它不能免除警方在讯问时遵守第五修正案（Miranda 规则）的义务，更不能为胁迫供述辩护。

选项 B (Emergency Search / 紧急搜查):
同上，第四修正案的搜查例外不能成为违反第五修正案进行胁迫讯问的理由。此外，受害者已失踪数月，很难主张存在“迫在眉睫的危险”来适用公共安全例外 (Public Safety Exception)。

选项 C (Fruit of Poisonous Tree / 毒树之果):
这是一个常见的陷阱。警方搜查的是被铁丝网围起来的田地。根据开阔地原则 (Open Fields Doctrine)，即使有围栏和“禁止入内”标志，开阔田地也不受第四修正案保护。因此，搜查本身是合法的，供述不是非法搜查的“毒果”。供述被排除的真正原因是胁迫。

MBE 解题技巧：
区分第四修正案（搜查/扣押）与第五修正案（自证其罪）。当题目涉及供述 (Confession) 时，优先检查是否存在羁押、讯问以及是否自愿。

questions.question:
The treasurer of a religious charity organization was charged with embezzlement. He received Miranda warnings upon his arrest at work. The treasurer did not respond to questions asked by the two arresting officers during the drive to the police station. When the treasurer and the officers arrived at the police station and began exiting the car, one of the officers asked the treasurer if he could forgive himself for stealing from a charity. The treasurer replied, "No."
At the treasurer's trial, his attorney filed a motion to suppress the treasurer's response to the arresting officer's question.
How should the court rule on the treasurer's motion?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the treasurer did not have the right to end questioning after his arrest unless he asserted his right to have counsel present.
choices.b: Deny the motion, because the treasurer waived his right to remain silent by responding to the police officer's question when exiting the car.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because all questioning should have stopped when the treasurer declined to respond to the officers' questions on the way to the police station.
choices.d: Grant the motion, because the treasurer's answer was given in response to the police officer's question while the treasurer was in custody.

questions.question:
A police officer stopped a man for a traffic offense, searched the man's car, and found cocaine underneath the passenger's seat. The man was arrested and subsequently charged with possession of a controlled substance. The man filed a motion to suppress the cocaine, alleging that the police officer lacked reasonable suspicion to stop him and probable cause to search his car. The court held a hearing on the man's motion to suppress and, after hearing the evidence, found that the officer had both reasonable suspicion to stop the man and probable cause to search his car. The man's motion was accordingly denied. The man subsequently pleaded guilty but reserved the right to appeal the court's denial of his motion and timely did so.
Which standard(s) of review should the court of appeals apply to the trial court's findings of historical fact and conclusions of law?

choices.a: Abuse of discretion as to findings of historical fact and clear error as to conclusions of law.
choices.b: Abuse of discretion as to findings of historical fact and de novo as to conclusions of law.
choices.c: Clear error as to findings of historical fact and de novo as to conclusions of law.
choices.d: De novo as to both findings of historical fact and conclusions of law.

Which standard(s) of review should the court of appeals apply to the trial court's findings of historical fact and conclusions of law?

一名警官因交通违法行为拦下了一名男子，搜查了该男子的汽车，并在乘客座位下发现了可卡因。该男子被逮捕，随后被控持有受管制物质罪。该男子提出排除可卡因证据的动议，声称该警官缺乏合理怀疑（reasonable suspicion）来拦停他，也缺乏相当理由（probable cause）来搜查他的汽车。法院就该男子的排除动议举行了听证会，在听取证据后，认定该警官既有合理怀疑拦停该男子，也有相当理由搜查其汽车。因此，该男子的动议被驳回。该男子随后认罪，但保留了就法院驳回其动议的裁决提起上诉的权利，并及时提起了上诉。

上诉法院在审查初审法院的历史事实认定和法律结论时，应适用何种审查标准？
options:
A. Abuse of discretion as to findings of historical fact and clear error as to conclusions of law.
对历史事实认定采用滥用裁量权标准，对法律结论采用明显错误标准。

B. Abuse of discretion as to findings of historical fact and de novo as to conclusions of law.
对历史事实认定采用滥用裁量权标准，对法律结论采用重新审查（de novo）标准。

C. Clear error as to findings of historical fact and de novo as to conclusions of law.
对历史事实认定采用明显错误（clear error）标准，对法律结论采用重新审查（de novo）标准。

D. De novo as to both findings of historical fact and conclusions of law.
对历史事实认定和法律结论均采用重新审查（de novo）标准。

Appellate standards of review


StandardLevel of reviewApplicability
De novoNo deference to trial judge's legal determination
Reverse if reasonably believe trial judge misinterpreted law		Pure legal issues, eg:
  • conclusions of law
  • content of jury instructions
Clear errorHighly deferential to trial judge's factual findings
Reverse if no reasonable judge would have made this finding		Factual issues in bench trials, eg:
  • credibility of witnesses
  • factual determinations
Substantial evidenceHighly deferential to jury's factual findings
Reverse if no reasonable jury would have made this finding		Factual issues in jury trials, eg:
  • credibility of witnesses
  • jury's verdict
Abuse of discretionHighly deferential to trial judge's discretionary decisions
Reverse only if decision was unreasonable/arbitrary		Discretionary rulings by judge, eg:
  • grant/denial of new trial
  • admissibility of evidence
A trial court rules on a motion to suppress by:
  • determining which historical facts elicited by the parties to accept as true (eg, by judging the credibility of the parties' witnesses at a hearing) and
  • applying the relevant statutory or constitutional standard to those facts to reach a legal conclusion (eg, concluding that an officer had reasonable suspicion or probable cause).


An appellate court should accept the trial court's findings of historical fact unless they are clearly erroneous - ie, if no reasonable judge would have made the findings (Choices A, B & D). That is because the trial court is in the best position to accurately make factual determinations.

However, the appellate court should review the trial court's conclusions of law de novo (ie, anew). This means that the trial court's legal conclusions are given no deference and are independently reviewed by the appellate court (Choice A). This helps prevent unacceptably varied results by trial courts on cases featuring similar facts and allows appellate courts to maintain control of legal rules and unify precedent.

Educational objective: When reviewing a trial court's ruling on a motion to suppress, an appellate court should accept the trial court's findings of historical fact unless they are clearly erroneous. However, the appellate court should review the trial court's conclusions of law de novo.

选项正确率统计：A选项 14%，B选项 20%，C选项 51%（正确选项），D选项 13%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

标准审查级别适用性
重新审查 (De novo)不遵从初审法官的法律判断
若有理由相信初审法官错误解释了法律，则予以推翻		纯法律问题，例如：
  • 法律结论
  • 陪审团指令的内容
明显错误 (Clear error)高度遵从初审法官的事实认定
若无理性的法官会做出此等认定，则予以推翻		法官审判中的事实问题，例如：
  • 证人可信度
  • 事实裁定
实质性证据 (Substantial evidence)高度遵从陪审团的事实认定
若无理性的陪审团会做出此等认定，则予以推翻		陪审团审判中的事实问题，例如：
  • 证人可信度
  • 陪审团的裁决
滥用裁量权 (Abuse of discretion)高度遵从初审法官的裁量决定
仅当决定不合理/武断时才予以推翻		法官的裁量性裁决，例如：
  • 批准/驳回重审
  • 证据的可采性
初审法院通过以下方式就排除证据动议作出裁决：
  • 确定采信当事人提出的哪些历史事实为真（例如，在听证会上判断当事人证人的可信度）以及
  • 将相关的法定或宪法标准适用于这些事实，以得出法律结论（例如，断定警官具有合理怀疑或相当理由）。


上诉法院应接受初审法院的历史事实认定，除非这些认定是明显错误的——即，如果任何理性的法官都不会做出此等认定（选项A、B和D）。这是因为初审法院最适合准确地进行事实裁定。

然而，上诉法院应对初审法院的法律结论进行重新审查（de novo）（即，重新审理）。这意味着初审法院的法律结论不被遵从，而是由上诉法院进行独立审查（选项A）。这有助于防止初审法院对具有相似事实的案件作出不可接受的、各不相同的结果，并使上诉法院能够保持对法律规则的控制和统一判例。

教学目标：在审查初审法院就排除证据动议所做的裁决时，上诉法院应接受初审法院的历史事实认定，除非这些认定是明显错误的。然而，上诉法院应对初审法院的法律结论进行重新审查（de novo）。

References

Ornelas v. United States, 517 U.S. 690, 696 - 98 (1996) (holding that trial court's conclusions of law are subject to de novo review on appeal).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

上诉审查标准 (Standards of Review)

核心解析

本题的正确答案是 C。

在涉及第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）的排除证据动议（Motion to Suppress）中，最高法院确立了双层审查标准：

1. 历史事实认定 (Findings of Historical Fact):

适用 明显错误标准 (Clear Error)。

2. 法律结论 (Conclusions of Law):

适用 重新审查标准 (De Novo)。

这一规则源自著名判例 Ornelas v. United States (1996)。法院认为，关于是否存在“合理怀疑” (Reasonable Suspicion) 或“相当理由” (Probable Cause) 的最终决定是法律问题，应当由上诉法院独立审查。

深度拆解：为什么这样区分？

1. 历史事实 (Historical Facts)

指“发生了什么”。例如：警官是否真的看到了可疑动作？被告是否说了某句话？

  • 理由： 初审法官（Trial Judge）在现场观察了证人的神态、语气，最适合判断证言的可信度（Credibility）。
  • 标准： Clear Error。除非错得离谱，否则上诉法院尊重初审法官的认定。

2. 法律结论 (Conclusions of Law)

指将法律标准（如宪法规定）应用到事实中。例如：基于上述事实，警官的行为是否构成宪法允许的搜查？

  • 理由： 为了保持法律适用的统一性，防止不同的初审法官对相似事实做出截然不同的法律定性。
  • 标准： De Novo。上诉法院不需尊重初审法院的结论，而是像第一次审理一样重新进行法律分析。

💡 考场实战技巧

在 MBE 刑诉法题目中，看到 Motion to Suppress 被否决后的上诉：

  1. 先看题目问的是事实还是法律。
  2. 如果是混合问题（如本题，既有事实认定又有法律定性），记住口诀："Facts are cleared (Clear Error), Law is new (De Novo)."
  3. 陷阱警示： 不要选 "Abuse of Discretion"。虽然证据的可采性（Admissibility，如传闻证据是否采纳）通常适用滥用裁量权标准，但涉及宪法权利（第四修正案搜查扣押）的法律定性，必须适用 De Novo。

questions.question:
A defendant was convicted of fraud after a jury trial in state court. The conviction was affirmed on direct appeal.
The defendant timely moved for postconviction relief under the Sixth Amendment on the ground that his attorney had provided ineffective assistance of counsel. The trial judge, after a hearing, found that the attorney had performed deficiently by failing to raise a proper objection that would have resulted in exclusion of important prosecution evidence.
What more, if anything, must the trial court find in order to sustain the defendant's Sixth Amendment claim?

choices.a: Nothing more, because the unjustifiable failure to object to important prosecution evidence is structural error.
choices.b: That the attorney was court-appointed and not privately retained.
choices.c: That there is a reasonable probability that the trial's outcome would have been different if the attorney had objected.
choices.d: That there is clear and convincing evidence that the trial's outcome would have been different if the attorney had objected.

data.questionStem:
Q84817 A defendant was convicted of fraud after a jury trial in state court. The conviction was affirmed on direct appeal.

The defendant timely moved for postconviction relief under the Sixth Amendment on the ground that his attorney had provided ineffective assistance of counsel. The trial judge, after a hearing, found that the attorney had performed deficiently by failing to raise a proper objection that would have resulted in exclusion of important prosecution evidence.

What more, if anything, must the trial court find in order to sustain the defendant's Sixth Amendment claim? 一名被告在州法院经陪审团审判后被判犯有欺诈罪。该定罪在直接上诉中得到维持。

被告以其律师提供的法律协助无效为由，根据第六修正案及时提出了定罪后济助的动议。庭审法官在举行听证会后，认定该律师未能提出本可导致一项重要控方证据被排除的适当异议，其履职存在缺陷。

为了支持被告的第六修正案主张，庭审法院还必须（若有）作出什么认定？
options:
A. Nothing more, because the unjustifiable failure to object to important prosecution evidence is structural error.
无需更多认定，因为无正当理由未能对重要的控方证据提出异议属于结构性错误。

B. That the attorney was court-appointed and not privately retained.
认定该律师是法院指定的，而非私人聘请的。

C. That there is a reasonable probability that the trial's outcome would have been different if the attorney had objected.
认定若律师提出了异议，审判结果有合理可能性会不同。

D. That there is clear and convincing evidence that the trial's outcome would have been different if the attorney had objected.
有清晰且有说服力的证据表明，若律师提出了异议，审判结果会不同。
data.explanation:
Criminal defendants can challenge their convictions directly (eg, appeal) and/or indirectly (eg, postconviction relief). To obtain postconviction relief, a defendant must file a petition in the trial court. The trial court will then hold a hearing and decide whether the defendant's conviction should be overturned.

The most common claim in a postconviction relief proceeding is that the defendant had ineffective assistance of counsel at trial. Under the Sixth Amendment—applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment's due process clause—all criminal defendants have the right to effective assistance of counsel. To protect that right, a defendant can have his/her conviction overturned by showing:

deficient performance – the attorney's performance during the trial fell below professional standards and

prejudice – there is a reasonable probability that, but for that deficiency, the trial's outcome would have been different.

Here, the defendant timely moved for postconviction relief for ineffective assistance of counsel. After the postconviction relief hearing, the trial judge found that the defendant's attorney had failed to raise an objection that would have excluded important prosecution evidence (deficient performance). But to sustain the defendant's Sixth Amendment claim, the trial judge must also find that there is a reasonable probability that the trial's outcome would have been different had the attorney objected (prejudice).

(Choice A) Structural errors are presumptively harmful since they affect the entire framework of a criminal trial and render it fundamentally unfair. As a result, these errors require automatic reversal on appeal. However, ineffective assistance of counsel is not a structural error because an attorney's misconduct (eg, failure to object) may be harmless. Therefore, the defendant must prove that his/her counsel's performance was deficient and prejudicial.

(Choice B) Criminal defendants are guaranteed effective assistance of counsel under the Sixth Amendment, regardless of whether their attorney was court-appointed or privately retained.

(Choice D) Ineffective assistance of counsel only requires a reasonable probability (ie, a likely chance)—not clear and convincing evidence (ie, a substantially likely chance)—that the defendant would not have been convicted had his/her attorney been competent.

Educational objective: Under the Sixth Amendment, defense counsel was ineffective when (1) his/her performance was deficient and (2) there is a reasonable probability that the trial's outcome would have been different absent the deficient performance.



刑事被告可以通过直接方式（如上诉）和/或间接方式（如定罪后济助）挑战其定罪。要获得定罪后济助 (postconviction relief)，被告必须向庭审法院提交申请。庭审法院随后将举行听证会，并决定是否应推翻被告的定罪。

在定罪后济助程序中最常见的主张是被告在审判中获得了无效的律师协助 (ineffective assistance of counsel)。根据第六修正案——通过第十四修正案的正当程序条款适用于各州——所有刑事被告都有权获得有效的律师协助。为保护此项权利，被告可通过证明以下两点来推翻其定罪：

履职存在缺陷 (deficient performance) – 律师在审判期间的表现低于专业标准，并且

损害 (prejudice) – 存在合理可能性 (reasonable probability)，若非该缺陷，审判结果本会不同。

在本案中，被告以律师协助无效为由，及时申请了定罪后济助。在定罪后济助听证会后，庭审法官认定被告的律师未能提出本可排除重要控方证据的异议（履职存在缺陷）。但要支持被告的第六修正案主张，庭审法官还必须认定，若律师提出了异议，审判结果有合理可能性会不同（损害）。

（选项A） 结构性错误 (Structural errors) 被推定为有害，因为它们影响刑事审判的整个框架，使其根本上不公平。因此，这类错误在上诉中需要自动推翻原判。然而，律师协助无效并非结构性错误，因为律师的不当行为（如未能提出异议）可能是无害的。因此，被告必须证明其律师的履职存在缺陷并造成了损害。

（选项B） 根据第六修正案，刑事被告有权获得有效的律师协助，无论其律师是法院指定的还是私人聘请的。

（选项D） 律师协助无效的主张仅要求存在合理可能性（即很有可能），而并非要求清晰且有说服力的证据（即极有可能），来证明若其律师称职，被告本不会被定罪。

教学目的： 根据第六修正案，在以下情况下，辩护律师的协助是无效的：（1）其履职存在缺陷，以及（2）在没有该缺陷的情况下，审判结果有合理可能性会不同。

References
U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to effective assistance of counsel).

Strickland v. Washington, 466 U.S. 668, 687 (1984) (setting out the requirements for ineffective assistance of counsel).

Weaver v. Massachusetts, 137 S. Ct. 1899, 1910–12 (2017) (holding that postconviction relief claim of ineffective assistance of counsel requires showing of deficient performance and prejudice).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law: Ineffective Assistance of Counsel

本题考察的是美国宪法第六修正案 (Sixth Amendment) 中关于“无效律师协助” (Ineffective Assistance of Counsel, IAC) 的核心判定标准。

⚖️ 核心判例：Strickland v. Washington (1984)

最高法院确立了著名的“双重检验标准” (Two-Prong Test)。被告必须同时证明以下两点才能推翻定罪：

1
履职缺陷 (Deficient Performance)：
律师的表现低于客观合理的专业标准 (fell below an objective standard of reasonableness)。
2
造成损害 (Prejudice)：
存在“合理可能性” (Reasonable Probability)，即如果律师没有犯错，审判结果会不同。
🔍 题目解析

题目中明确指出，庭审法官已经认定律师未能提出异议属于履职缺陷 (Deficient Performance)。这满足了 Strickland 测试的第一步。

为了支持被告的主张，法院必须继续认定第二步：损害 (Prejudice)。

因此，正确答案必须是关于“结果可能不同”的证明标准。

正确答案 C 准确地表述了这一标准：
"Reasonable probability that the trial's outcome would have been different."

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 A (Structural Error)：
错误。 只有极少数根本性错误（如完全剥夺律师权、法官有偏见）才属于“结构性错误”并自动导致重审。普通的律师失误（如未提出异议）必须证明对结果产生了实际影响（Harmless Error Analysis 适用）。
选项 B (Appointed vs. Retained)：
错误。 第六修正案对公设辩护人 (Court-appointed) 和私人律师 (Privately retained) 的要求是一致的。
选项 D (Clear and Convincing)：
错误。 这是一个过高的证明标准。被告只需证明“合理可能性” (Reasonable Probability)，即足以动摇对结果的信心 (sufficient to undermine confidence in the outcome)，而不需要达到“清晰且有说服力” (Clear and Convincing) 的程度。
💡 MBE 备考口诀：
IAC = Deficiency + Prejudice
(律师太烂 + 结果因烂而变)

questions.question:
Two police officers in uniform were on foot patrol in a neighborhood frequented by drug sellers. They noticed a woman walking toward them. As the officers passed the woman, one of them stopped and asked her if she had anything illegal on her. The woman ignored the officer and continued walking. The officer turned around and shouted, "Stop and don't take another step, lady!" The woman turned, looked at the police, and stopped. She put her arms up in the air. As the police approached, she threw a small object into nearby bushes. An officer retrieved the object, which turned out to be a small bag of cocaine, and then arrested the woman.
The woman is charged with possession of the cocaine. She moves pretrial to suppress its use as evidence on the ground that it was obtained as the result of an illegal search and seizure.
Should the court grant the woman's motion?

choices.a: No, because the police had probable cause to seize the package.
choices.b: No, because the woman voluntarily discarded the contraband.
choices.c: Yes, because the police acquired the cocaine as the result of an unlawful seizure.
choices.d: Yes, because the police did not know the item was cocaine until after they had seized it.

data.questionStem:
Q85003

Two police officers in uniform were on foot patrol in a neighborhood frequented by drug sellers. They noticed a woman walking toward them. As the officers passed the woman, one of them stopped and asked her if she had anything illegal on her. The woman ignored the officer and continued walking. The officer turned around and shouted, "Stop and don't take another step, lady!" The woman turned, looked at the police, and stopped. She put her arms up in the air. As the police approached, she threw a small object into nearby bushes. An officer retrieved the object, which turned out to be a small bag of cocaine, and then arrested the woman.

The woman is charged with possession of the cocaine. She moves pretrial to suppress its use as evidence on the ground that it was obtained as the result of an illegal search and seizure.

Should the court grant the woman's motion?

两名身着制服的警官正在一个毒贩经常出没的社区徒步巡逻。他们注意到一名女子朝他们走来。当警官们经过该女子时，其中一人停下来问她身上是否携带任何非法物品。该女子没有理会警官，继续行走。该警官转过身喊道：“女士，站住，不许再走一步！”该女子转身看着警察，停了下来。她将双臂举到空中。当警察走近时，她将一个小物件扔进旁边的灌木丛中。一名警官找到了那个物件，结果是一小袋可卡因，随后逮捕了该女子。

该女子被控持有可卡因。她提出审前动议，以该证据是通过非法搜查与扣押获得为由，要求排除其作为证据使用。

法院是否应批准该女子的动议？
options:
A. No, because the police had probable cause to seize the package.
不应批准，因为警方有合理根据扣押该包裹。

B. No, because the woman voluntarily discarded the contraband.
不应批准，因为该女子是自愿丢弃该违禁品的。

C. Yes, because the police acquired the cocaine as the result of an unlawful seizure.
应该批准，因为警方是在一次非法扣押之后获得了可卡因。

D. Yes, because the police did not know the item was cocaine until after they had seized it.
应该批准，因为警方在扣押该物品之后才知道它是可卡因。
data.explanation:
Police-citizen encounters


TypeCharacteristics
Consensual encounterNo suspicion required Officer may approach citizen/engage in conversation Citizen may:
  • respond to officer or walk away
Terry stop (stop & frisk)Reasonable suspicion required Officer may:
  • briefly question to confirm/dispel suspicion
  • frisk if reasonably believes person armed
Investigative in nature
ArrestProbable cause required Officer may:
  • search incident to arrest
  • interrogate after Mirandizing
Initiates criminal prosecution
A Fourth Amendment seizure occurs when police use their authority or physical force to restrict a person's freedom of movement and the person submits to the restriction. To be reasonable, the seizure must be supported by at least reasonable suspicion - ie, specific and articulable facts that would lead an officer to suspect that the person is, or will be, involved in a crime. If police lack such suspicion, the seizure is unlawful and any evidence obtained as a result of that seizure should be suppressed.

Here, an officer asked the woman if she had anything illegal on her while she was walking in a neighborhood frequented by drug sellers. When the woman ignored the question and walked away, the officer ordered her to stop (use of authority to restrict movement). But the woman's mere presence in the high-crime neighborhood did not create reasonable suspicion to seize her (as recognized in Brown v. Texas ), so the stop was unlawful. And since the cocaine was discarded and then retrieved as a result of that stop, the cocaine should be suppressed.

(Choice A) The exclusionary rule requires the suppression of any evidence obtained as a result of police misconduct. Therefore, though police may have had probable cause to seize the cocaine, it still must be suppressed since it stemmed from an unlawful seizure of the woman.

(Choice B) Police may freely seize property that has been voluntarily abandoned. But here, the cocaine was not voluntarily abandoned since it was discarded in response to police misconduct (unlawful seizure).

(Choice D) Had the seizure of the woman been supported by reasonable suspicion, the cocaine could have been lawfully seized - even if the police did not know it was cocaine at that time.

Educational objective: To be reasonable, a seizure of a person must be supported by at least reasonable suspicion - ie, specific and articulable facts that would lead an officer to suspect that the person is, or will be, involved in a crime. And a person's mere presence in a high-crime area does not establish such suspicion.

选项正确率统计：A选项 13%，B选项 44%，C选项 40%（正确选项），D选项 1%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

警察与公民的接触


类型特征
两厢情愿的接触无需怀疑
警官可以接近公民/进行交谈
公民可以：
  • 回应警官 或 走开
Terry式截停 (截停与搜身)需要合理怀疑
警官可以：
  • 短暂询问以确认/消除怀疑
  • 如果合理相信此人持有武器，可进行搜身
具有调查性质
逮捕需要合理根据
警官可以：
  • 附带逮捕进行搜查
  • 在告知米兰达警告后进行讯问
启动刑事诉讼
当警察利用其权力或有形力量限制一个人的行动自由，并且该人服从该限制时，就发生了《第四修正案》意义上的扣押。为具备合理性，该扣押必须至少有合理怀疑的支持——即，具体且可明确表述的事实，这些事实将导致警官怀疑此人正在或将要参与犯罪。如果警方缺乏此类怀疑，该扣押即为非法，任何因此次扣押而获得的证据都应被排除。

在本案中，一名警官在该女子于一个毒贩经常出没的社区行走时，询问她是否携带任何非法物品。当该女子无视问题并走开时，警官命令她停下（利用权力限制其行动）。但是，该女子仅仅身处高犯罪率社区并不构成扣押她的合理怀疑（如在 Brown v. Texas 案中所承认的），因此这次截停是非法的。并且，由于可卡因是在这次截停之后被丢弃并被寻回的，该可卡因应被排除。

(选项A) 证据排除规则要求排除任何因警察不当行为而获得的证据。因此，尽管警方可能有合理根据扣押可卡因，但由于该证据源于对该女子的非法扣押，它仍然必须被排除。

(选项B) 警方可以自由扣押自愿抛弃的财产。但在本案中，可卡因并非自愿抛弃，因为它是在回应警察的不当行为（非法扣押）时被丢弃的。

(选项D) 假如对该女子的扣押有合理怀疑的支持，那么即使警方当时不知道那是可卡因，也可以合法地扣押它。

教学目标：为具备合理性，对一个人的扣押必须至少有合理怀疑的支持——即，具体且可明确表述的事实，这些事实将导致警官怀疑此人正在或将要参与犯罪。而一个人仅仅身处高犯罪率地区并不构成此类怀疑。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Brown v. Texas, 443 U.S. 47, 52 (1979) (recognizing that a person's mere presence in a high-crime area does not establish a basis to detain the person).
  • United States v. Morin, 665 F.2d 765, 770 (5th Cir. 1982) (explaining that abandonment of property prompted by police misconduct is not voluntary).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Fourth Amendment

本题考察的核心是第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）下的“扣押”（Seizure）定义以及“毒树之果”（Fruit of the Poisonous Tree）原则。

初步接触 (Initial Contact) 警察询问，女子无视并走开。此时为自愿接触，女子有权离开。
命令与服从 (Command & Submission) 警察喊“站住”，女子停下并举手。关键点：此时发生了扣押 (Seizure)。
丢弃物品 (Discarding Object) 女子在被扣押后扔掉可卡因。
搜查与逮捕 (Search & Arrest) 警察捡起物品并逮捕女子。
核心考点：Terry Stop 的合法性
根据 Terry v. Ohio，警察进行调查性截停（Investigatory Stop）必须基于合理怀疑 (Reasonable Suspicion)，即必须有具体的事实表明犯罪正在进行或即将发生。
判例规则 (Rule of Law):
仅身处“高犯罪率地区”(High-crime area) 本身不足以构成拦截公民的合理怀疑 (Brown v. Texas)。

在本案中，警察拦截该女子的唯一依据是她出现在毒品交易频发的地区。当她行使权利拒绝回答并走开时，警察并没有额外的理由怀疑她犯罪。因此，警察命令她停下（且她确实停下了）构成了一次非法扣押 (Unlawful Seizure)。

✅ 正确答案：C

理由：因为警方是在非法扣押之后才获得了可卡因。

根据证据排除规则 (Exclusionary Rule)，由于最初的截停（Seizure）是非法的（缺乏合理怀疑），因此作为该非法行为直接结果（Direct Result）而获得的所有证据（即被丢弃的可卡因）都必须被排除。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A 错误： 即使后来发现了毒品（有了逮捕的合理根据 Probable Cause），但这不能反过来证明最初拦截行为的合法性。
选项 B 错误（常见陷阱）： 虽然通常丢弃物（Abandoned Property）不受宪法保护，但如果是因警察的非法行为（非法截停）而被迫丢弃的，这种丢弃不被视为“自愿”，证据仍需排除。
选项 D 错误： 警察是否知道那是可卡因并不重要，关键在于截停人本身是否合法。
MBE 策略：先判断警察行为是否合法，再看证据链是否被污染。

questions.question:
Police officers had probable cause to believe that a man had committed a series of armed bank robberies with an accomplice.
The officers obtained a valid arrest warrant for the man and went to his house to arrest him. The officers found the front door ajar and could hear a radio playing inside. They knocked on the door, identified themselves as police officers, and stated that they had a warrant. Getting no response, the officers entered the house. After the officers called the man's name several times and again identified themselves as police officers, the man emerged from the basement and was arrested. The officers went into the basement to look for the accomplice. They opened a closet door and found cocaine in plain view. They did not find the accomplice.
The man was indicted for cocaine possession. He has moved to suppress the cocaine as evidence on the ground that it was obtained in violation of the Fourth Amendment.
Should the court grant the motion to suppress?

choices.a: No, because the officers discovered the cocaine during a lawful protective sweep of the house looking for the man's accomplice.
choices.b: No, because the search was incident to the man's arrest.
choices.c: Yes, because the officers did not have a search warrant.
choices.d: Yes, because the officers did not have probable cause to believe that cocaine would be in the closet.

data.questionStem:
Q84811 Police officers had probable cause to believe that a man had committed a series of armed bank robberies with an accomplice.

The officers obtained a valid arrest warrant for the man and went to his house to arrest him. The officers found the front door ajar and could hear a radio playing inside. They knocked on the door, identified themselves as police officers, and stated that they had a warrant. Getting no response, the officers entered the house. After the officers called the man's name several times and again identified themselves as police officers, the man emerged from the basement and was arrested. The officers went into the basement to look for the accomplice. They opened a closet door and found cocaine in plain view. They did not find the accomplice.

The man was indicted for cocaine possession. He has moved to suppress the cocaine as evidence on the ground that it was obtained in violation of the Fourth Amendment.

Should the court grant the motion to suppress? 警官有相当理由相信一名男子与一名同伙共同实施了一系列持械银行抢劫。

警官获得了对该男子的有效逮捕令，并前往其住所进行逮捕。警官发现前门虚掩，并能听到室内有收音机在播放。他们敲了门，表明自己是警察，并声明他们持有逮捕令。在没有得到回应后，警官进入了房屋。在警官多次呼叫该男子姓名并再次表明警察身份后，该男子从地下室走出来并被逮捕。警官进入地下室寻找同伙。他们打开一个壁橱门，发现了清晰可见的可卡因。他们没有找到同伙。

该男子因持有可卡因而被起诉。他以可卡因是违反第四修正案获得的为由，申请排除该证据。

法院是否应批准该排除动议？
options:
A. No, because the officers discovered the cocaine during a lawful protective sweep of the house looking for the man's accomplice.
不应批准，因为警官是在为寻找该男子的同伙而对房屋进行合法的保护性搜查时发现可卡因的。

B. No, because the search was incident to the man's arrest.
不应批准，因为该搜查是附随于该男子被捕而进行的。

C. Yes, because the officers did not have a search warrant.
应批准，因为警官没有搜查令。

D. Yes, because the officers did not have probable cause to believe that cocaine would be in the closet.
应批准，因为警官没有相当理由相信壁橱里会有可卡因。
data.explanation:
A court should deny a defendant's motion to suppress if the contested evidence was obtained during a reasonable Fourth Amendment search. A protective sweep—ie, a quick, warrantless search of the premises made incident to an arrest—is reasonable if: police have a reasonable suspicion (ie, a belief based on specific, articulable facts) that the premises harbor someone who poses a threat to the safety of persons at the scene and the sweep is limited to a cursory inspection of places where a person could hide.

Evidence or contraband found in plain view during the sweep may be seized without a warrant and admitted at trial.

Here, officers arrested the man pursuant to a warrant as he emerged from the basement of his home. The officers then conducted a protective sweep of the premises. That sweep was lawful because the man was suspected of committing armed bank robberies with an accomplice (reasonable suspicion of danger) and the sweep was limited to the basement and closet (places a person could hide). Therefore, the cocaine found in plain view during the sweep was lawfully seized and should be admitted (not suppressed) at trial.

(Choice B) The search-incident-to-lawful-arrest exception to the warrant requirement allows officers to conduct a warrantless search of an arrested person and the areas in his/her immediate reach. This exception does not apply here since the basement was not in the man's reach. Therefore, this is not a basis to deny the motion to suppress.

(Choice C) Police do not need a search warrant to conduct a protective sweep—or to seize evidence found in plain view during that sweep—if they reasonably suspect that a dangerous person is in the area to be searched (and the search is limited to places a person could hide).

(Choice D) Police did not have probable cause to believe that cocaine would be found in the closet. But since the cocaine was discovered during a lawful protective sweep, they did not need probable cause (or a warrant) to seize it.

Educational objective: Police can conduct a protective sweep—a quick, warrantless search of the premises made incident to an arrest—if they reasonably suspect that a dangerous person may be on the premises and the sweep is limited to places where a person may be found. Evidence found in plain view during the sweep may be seized without a warrant.



如果争议证据是在符合第四修正案的合理搜查中获得的，法院应驳回被告的排除动议。一次保护性搜查（protective sweep）——即在逮捕时对场所进行的快速、无证搜查——在以下情况下是合理的： 警察有合理怀疑（reasonable suspicion）（即基于具体、可明确阐述的事实的信念），认为场所有藏匿对现场人员安全构成威胁的人，并且 该搜查仅限于对可能藏匿人员之处的粗略检查。

在搜查过程中一目了然（plain view）发现的证据或违禁品，可以在没有搜查令的情况下被扣押，并在审判中被采纳。

在本案中，警官根据逮捕令在该男子从其家中地下室出来时将其逮捕。随后，警官对该场所进行了保护性搜查。该搜查是合法的，因为该男子涉嫌与同伙共同实施持械银行抢劫（存在危险的合理怀疑），且搜查范围仅限于地下室和壁橱（可能藏匿人员的地方）。因此，在搜查过程中一目了然发现的可卡因是合法扣押的，应在审判中被采纳（而非排除）。

（选项B） 附随合法逮捕搜查的例外规则允许警官对被捕者及其直接可及范围内的区域进行无证搜查。此例外不适用于本案，因为地下室不在该男子的可及范围内。因此，这不能作为驳回排除动议的依据。

（选项C） 如果警察合理怀疑待搜查区域内有危险人物（且搜查仅限于可能藏匿人员的地方），则进行保护性搜查或扣押在该搜查中一目了然发现的证据时，不需要搜查令。

（选项D） 警察没有相当理由相信壁橱里会发现可卡因。但由于可卡因是在合法的保护性搜查中发现的，他们不需要相当理由（或搜查令）来扣押它。

教学目的： 如果警察合理怀疑场所内可能有危险人物，并且搜查范围仅限于可能发现人员的地方，他们就可以进行保护性搜查——一种在逮捕时对场所进行的快速、无证搜查。在搜查过程中一目了然发现的证据可以在没有搜查令的情况下被扣押。

References

U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).

Maryland v. Buie, 494 U.S. 325, 334–36 (1990) (explaining that officers may conduct a protective sweep if they have reasonable suspicion that a dangerous person is in the area swept).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Fourth Amendment
正确答案：A 法院不应批准排除动议，因为这是合法的保护性搜查 (Protective Sweep)。
⚖️ 核心法律规则：保护性搜查
Protective Sweep (Maryland v. Buie)
这是一种为了保护警察和现场人员安全而进行的快速、有限的搜查。它是无证搜查 (Warrantless Search) 的例外情况之一。

根据最高法院判例，保护性搜查分为两种情况，本题考查的是第二种（需要合理怀疑）：

  • 前提：警察必须有合理怀疑 (Reasonable Suspicion)，认为逮捕现场可能藏匿着其他危险人物。
  • 范围：仅限于对可能藏人的地方（如壁橱、床底）进行粗略检查 (Cursory Inspection)。
  • 结果：在合法搜查范围内，如果发现一目了然 (Plain View) 的违禁品，可以合法扣押。
🔍 本案逻辑链条

让我们将规则应用到题目中的事实：

1. 为什么可以搜查地下室？
警察知道嫌疑人有同伙 (Accomplice) 且涉及持械 (Armed) 抢劫。这构成了“存在危险人物”的合理怀疑。嫌疑人刚从地下室出来，警察有理由检查地下室是否藏有同伙。

2. 为什么可以打开壁橱？
壁橱是一个可以藏人 (Places a person could hide) 的空间。搜查范围是合法的。

3. 为什么可卡因可以作为证据？
虽然警察没有搜查毒品的搜查令，也没有理由相信壁橱里有毒品，但他们在合法寻找同伙时，发现了一目了然 (Plain View) 的可卡因。因此，扣押是合法的。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 B (SITA) 错误
这是最强的干扰项。附随逮捕的搜查 (Search Incident to Arrest) 仅限于被捕者的“翼展范围” (Wingspan/Immediate control)。嫌疑人已被逮捕，地下室通常超出了其直接控制范围。本题的合法性基础是“保护性搜查”，而非 SITA。
选项 C (无搜查令) 错误
保护性搜查是第四修正案搜查令要求的例外 (Exception)。只要满足条件，不需要搜查令。
选项 D (无相当理由) 错误
警察不需要对“发现毒品”有相当理由 (Probable Cause)。他们只需要对“存在危险人物”有合理怀疑。一旦进入合法位置，Plain View 规则允许扣押毒品。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理第四修正案题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 是否有搜查令？ (本题：有逮捕令，无搜查令)
  2. 是否适用例外情况？
    • 如果是为了找证据 ➔ 考虑 SITA（仅限翼展范围）。
    • 如果是为了找人/安全 ➔ 考虑 Protective Sweep（全屋可能藏人的地方）。
  3. Plain View 的应用： 只要警察合法待在那个位置，看到的东西就是合法的证据。

questions.question:
During jury selection at a criminal trial, the defendant used all of his peremptory challenges to strike men from the jury. The prosecution objected to the defendant's actions. The defendant provided a gender-neutral reason for striking the potential male jurors, which the court found to be pretextual.
Was the defendant's use of peremptory challenges unconstitutional?

choices.a: No, because the Constitution does not prohibit criminal defendants from exercising discriminatory peremptory challenges.
choices.b: No, because the defendant struck members of his own gender from the jury.
choices.c: Yes, because the defendant's actions prevented the selection of an impartial jury.
choices.d: Yes, because the defendant's actions violated the equal protection clause.

questions.question:
On an interstate highway, a police officer encountered a car being driven well below the posted minimum speed limit. The officer stopped the car. After approaching the driver's window, the officer noticed that the driver's eyes were bloodshot and that the driver appeared nervous. The officer asked if the driver had any weapons or drugs in his possession, and the driver informed the officer that he had a handgun in his backseat but that he was licensed to lawfully carry it. The officer immediately asked the driver to exit the car. The driver complied.
The officer asked the driver if he would consent to a search of his car and the driver replied, "Sure." While searching the car, the officer found two pounds of marijuana, a scale, and several plastic baggies underneath the passenger seat. The officer asked, "Does this marijuana and paraphernalia belong to you?" The driver confessed that it did. The officer then handcuffed and arrested the driver for possession of marijuana with intent to distribute.
If the driver moves to suppress his admission about the marijuana and paraphernalia belonging to him, how will the court likely rule on his motion?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the driver consented to the officer's search of his car during the traffic stop.
choices.b: Deny the motion, because the driver was not in custody at the time that he made the incriminating statement to the officer.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because the driver was effectively placed in custody when he was ordered out of his car by the officer.
choices.d: Grant the motion, because the officer's question was intended to elicit an incriminating response from the driver.

If the driver moves to suppress his admission about the marijuana and paraphernalia belonging to him, how will the court likely rule on his motion?

在一条州际公路上，一名警官遇到一辆远低于规定最低限速行驶的汽车。警官拦停了该车。靠近驾驶员车窗后，警官注意到驾驶员双眼充血，神情紧张。警官询问驾驶员是否持有任何武器或毒品，驾驶员告知警官其后座有一把手枪，但他持有合法携带该枪支的许可证。警官立即要求驾驶员下车。驾驶员遵从了指示。

警官询问驾驶员是否同意搜查其车辆，驾驶员回答：“当然可以。”在搜查车辆时，警官在乘客座位下方发现了两磅大麻、一个秤和几个塑料袋。警官问道：“这些大麻和相关用具是你的吗？”驾驶员承认是他的。警官随后给驾驶员戴上手铐，并以意图分销而持有大麻的罪名将其逮捕。

如果驾驶员提出动议，要求排除其关于大麻和相关用具归其所有的供认，法院将可能如何裁定该动议？
options:
A. Deny the motion, because the driver consented to the officer's search of his car during the traffic stop.
驳回动议，因为在交通截停期间，驾驶员同意了警官对其车辆的搜查。

B. Deny the motion, because the driver was not in custody at the time that he made the incriminating statement to the officer.
驳回动议，因为驾驶员在向警官作出有罪陈述时，并未处于羁押状态。

C. Grant the motion, because the driver was effectively placed in custody when he was ordered out of his car by the officer.
批准动议，因为当警官命令驾驶员下车时，驾驶员已被有效置于羁押状态。

D. Grant the motion, because the officer's question was intended to elicit an incriminating response from the driver.
批准动议，因为警官的问题旨在引出驾驶员的有罪答复。
data.explanation:
A motion to suppress an incriminating statement should be granted if law enforcement failed to provide Miranda warnings prior to a custodial interrogation. A custodial interrogation occurs when a person is:
  • in custody - placed under formal arrest or so restrained in his/her freedom of movement that a reasonable person would not feel free to terminate the encounter and
  • subjected to interrogation - express questions, words, or actions directed at the person that an officer knows or should know are likely to elicit an incriminating response.
Although traffic stops restrain freedom of movement, drivers are generally not in custody for Miranda purposes because such encounters are typically brief and temporary.

Here, the driver made an incriminating statement when asked whether the marijuana and paraphernalia belonged to him. But since the driver was not in custody during this traffic stop, the officer did not need to administer Miranda warnings. Therefore, the court will likely deny the driver's motion to suppress.

(Choice A) The driver's consent to a search of his car pertained to his Fourth Amendment protection against unreasonable searches and seizures - not the admissibility of his statement. The determining factor for the statement's admissibility is whether the driver was subjected to a custodial interrogation.

(Choice C) Merely asking a person to step out of the vehicle during a traffic stop does not render the person "in custody" for Miranda purposes.

(Choice D) The officer's question to the driver was intended to elicit an incriminating response. However, the driver was not entitled to Miranda warnings because he was not in custody.

Educational objective: Miranda warnings must be provided to suspects before they are subjected to custodial interrogations. Since drivers are generally not in custody during traffic stops, Miranda warnings are not needed.



选项正确率统计：A选项 31%，B选项 39%（正确选项），C选项 18%，D选项 11%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

如果在羁押讯问之前，执法部门未能提供 Miranda 警告，则排除有罪陈述的动议应被批准。当一个人处于以下情况时，即构成羁押讯问：
  • 处于羁押状态 - 被正式逮捕，或其行动自由受到限制，以至于一个理性人会认为自己无法自由终止此次接触并且
  • 受到讯问 - 警官知道或理应知道，其针对该人所做的明确提问、言语或行为，很可能引出有罪答复。
尽管交通截停会限制行动自由，但就 Miranda 警告而言，驾驶员通常不被视为处于羁押状态，因为此类接触通常是短暂和临时性的。

在本案中，当被问及大麻和相关用具是否属于他时，驾驶员作出了有罪陈述。但由于在这次交通截停期间，驾驶员并未处于羁押状态，因此警官无需给予 Miranda 警告。因此，法院很可能会驳回驾驶员的排除动议。

(选项 A) 驾驶员同意搜查其车辆，这涉及到美国宪法第四修正案赋予他的、免受不合理搜查和扣押的权利，而非其陈述的可采性。决定该陈述可采性的因素是，驾驶员是否受到了羁押讯问。

(选项 C) 在交通截停期间，仅仅要求一个人下车，并不会使其就 Miranda 警告而言，被视为“处于羁押状态”。

(选项 D) 警官向驾驶员提出的问题确实旨在引出有罪答复。然而，由于驾驶员并未处于羁押状态，他无权获得 Miranda 警告。

教学要点：在嫌疑人受到羁押讯问之前，必须向其提供 Miranda 警告。由于在交通截停期间，驾驶员通常不被视为处于羁押状态，因此不需要 Miranda 警告。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 468 - 70 (1966) (listing Miranda warnings).
  • Berkemer v. McCarty, 468 U.S. 420, 440 (1984) (recognizing that a person is not in custody during an investigatory detention).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Miranda Rights
✅ 正确答案：选项 B
核心考点：羁押讯问 (Custodial Interrogation)

本题考察的核心是 Miranda 警告 的触发条件。根据 Miranda v. Arizona，警方只有在对嫌疑人进行“羁押讯问”时，才必须宣读 Miranda 权利。

公式：
羁押 (Custody) + 讯问 (Interrogation) = 需要 Miranda

如果缺少其中任何一个要素，警方未宣读 Miranda 权利并不影响供词的可采性 (Admissibility)。

深度解析：为什么选 B？

虽然警官的问题（“这些大麻是你的吗？”）明显构成了讯问 (Interrogation)，因为这旨在引出有罪供述，但关键在于羁押 (Custody) 这一要素缺失。

法律依据 (Berkemer v. McCarty, 1984)：

  • 最高法院裁定，普通的交通截停 (Traffic Stop) 通常不构成 Miranda 意义上的“羁押”。
  • 虽然驾驶员的行动自由受到限制（不能直接开走），但这种拘留通常是短暂的 (Temporary) 和公开的 (Public)。
  • 因此，这种环境不像警察局审讯室那样具有“强迫性气氛” (Coercive Atmosphere)。

在本案中，驾驶员虽然被叫下车，但并未被戴上手铐，也未被告知被捕。因此，他当时并未处于“羁押”状态，警官无需给予 Miranda 警告，供词有效。

为什么其他选项是错的？

❌ 选项 A (Consent to Search)：混淆概念
同意搜查涉及的是第四修正案（搜查与扣押），而本题讨论的是供词的可采性（第五修正案）。同意搜查并不意味着放弃了反对自证其罪的权利，两者是独立的法律问题。

❌ 选项 C (Ordered out of car)：法律误解
根据 Pennsylvania v. Mimms，出于警官安全考虑，在合法交通截停中命令驾驶员下车是允许的，这一行为本身并不将普通的交通截停转化为“羁押”。

❌ 选项 D (Intent to elicit)：只对了一半
这个选项正确地指出了警官的行为构成了“讯问”。但是，MBE 题目中常见的陷阱是：仅仅有讯问是不够的，必须同时满足“羁押”这一条件。因为没有羁押，所以即便有讯问意图，也不需要 Miranda。

💡 MBE 实战技巧

在处理涉及 Miranda 的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 看环境：是在警察局审讯室，还是路边？（路边通常 = 非羁押）。
  2. 看束缚：嫌疑人是否被戴上手铐？是否被告知 "You are under arrest"？（如果没有，通常 = 非羁押）。
  3. 看顺序：是先问话后逮捕，还是先逮捕后问话？

记住：普通的交通违章截停（Terry Stop）不是 Custody。

questions.question:
Four hours into a defendant's assault trial, the lawyers gathered in the judge's chambers to discuss an evidentiary issue. While there, the judge received a phone call from his wife telling him that her mother had suddenly died. Without asking the lawyers what they wanted to do, the judge brought the lawyers back into the courtroom, declared a mistrial, excused the jury, and rushed home to his wife.
A new jury was impaneled the next day before a second judge.
The defendant has objected to the second trial on double jeopardy grounds.
Would the second trial violate the prohibition against double jeopardy?

choices.a: No, because the first judge acted in good faith in declaring a mistrial.
choices.b: No, because the first trial did not produce a verdict.
choices.c: Yes, because the second judge's evidentiary rulings might be inconsistent with those of the first judge.
choices.d: Yes, because there was no manifest necessity for a mistrial.

data.questionStem:
Q84810 Four hours into a defendant's assault trial, the lawyers gathered in the judge's chambers to discuss an evidentiary issue. While there, the judge received a phone call from his wife telling him that her mother had suddenly died. Without asking the lawyers what they wanted to do, the judge brought the lawyers back into the courtroom, declared a mistrial, excused the jury, and rushed home to his wife.

A new jury was impaneled the next day before a second judge.

The defendant has objected to the second trial on double jeopardy grounds.

Would the second trial violate the prohibition against double jeopardy? 在一名被告人的攻击罪审判进行四小时后，律师们聚集在法官办公室内讨论一个证据问题。在此期间，法官接到妻子的电话，得知他岳母突然去世。法官没有询问律师们的意见，就将他们带回法庭，宣布审判无效，解散了陪审团，然后赶回家中陪伴妻子。

第二天，在第二位法官面前组成了新的陪审团。

被告人以一事不再理为由反对第二次审判。

第二次审判是否违反禁止一事不再理的原则？
options:
A. No, because the first judge acted in good faith in declaring a mistrial.
否，因为第一位法官在宣布审判无效时是出于善意。

B. No, because the first trial did not produce a verdict.
否，因为第一次审判没有作出裁决。

C. Yes, because the second judge's evidentiary rulings might be inconsistent with those of the first judge.
是，因为第二位法官的证据裁定可能与第一位法官的不一致。

D. Yes, because there was no manifest necessity for a mistrial.
是，因为宣布审判无效不具备明显必要性。
data.explanation:
No double jeopardy protections
(retrial permitted for same offense)


No attachmentJury was not impaneled & sworn or
Judge did not begin to hear evidence
MistrialRequested by defendant or
Based on manifest necessity
AppealAppellate court discovered trial error & remanded case
New factsFacts necessary for greater offense did not exist at first trial
Guilty plea to lesser offenseGreater offense was charged at time of plea to lesser offense
The Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause bars multiple punishments and a second prosecution for the same offense following a conviction or an acquittal (ie, a final judgment). Since a mistrial terminates a trial prior to a final judgment, double jeopardy permits a retrial when (1) the defendant requested the mistrial or (2) the mistrial was based on a manifest necessity—ie:

an unforeseeable event made it highly necessary to terminate the proceedings (eg, the death of a juror) and

the judge exercised sound and rational discretion before declaring the mistrial (eg, allowing both sides the opportunity to speak, considering the available alternatives).

Here, the judge learned that his mother-in-law had suddenly died (unforeseeable event) and declared a mistrial. But the judge did so without considering other alternatives like postponing the trial or substituting another judge (no exercise of sound and rational discretion). As a result, there was no manifest necessity for the mistrial, and a second trial would violate the double jeopardy clause.

(Choice A) The judge acted in good faith since he declared the mistrial to tend to personal issues-not to prejudice the defendant. But since there was no manifest necessity for the mistrial, the defendant cannot be retried.

(Choice B) Although the first trial did not produce a verdict (since the judge declared a mistrial), double jeopardy prohibits a second prosecution because the mistrial was not based on a manifest necessity. If it had been, the second trial would have been permissible.

(Choice C) While the second judge's evidentiary rulings might be inconsistent with those of the first judge, the double jeopardy clause is violated due to the lack of a manifest necessity for the mistrial. Had the mistrial been based on a manifest necessity, a second trial before a different judge would not have violated the double jeopardy clause despite the risk of inconsistent evidentiary rulings.

无一事不再理保护
(允许对同一罪行进行重审)

法官未开始听取证据

对较轻罪行作有罪答辩在对较轻罪行作答辩时，更重的罪行已被指控
美国宪法第五修正案的一事不再理条款禁止对同一罪行进行多次惩罚和在定罪或宣告无罪（即终局判决）后再次起诉。由于无效审判在终局判决前终止审判，因此在以下情况下，一事不再理原则允许重审：(1) 被告人请求宣布审判无效，或 (2) 无效审判基于明显必要性——即：

一个不可预见的事件使得极有必要终止诉讼程序（例如，陪审员死亡）并且

法官在宣布审判无效前行使了健全合理的自由裁量权（例如，给予双方发言机会，考虑可行的替代方案）。

在本案中，法官得知其岳母突然去世（不可预见的事件）并宣布审判无效。但法官在这样做时没有考虑其他替代方案，如推迟审判或更换另一位法官（未行使健全合理的自由裁量权）。因此，宣布审判无效不具备明显必要性，第二次审判将违反一事不再理条款。

（选项A）法官是出于善意行事，因为他宣布审判无效是为了处理个人事务，而不是为了损害被告人的利益。但由于宣布审判无效不具备明显必要性，因此不能对被告人进行重审。

（选项B）尽管第一次审判没有作出裁决（因为法官宣布了审判无效），但一事不再理原则禁止进行第二次起诉，因为该无效审判并非基于明显必要性。如果基于此，第二次审判本是允许的。

（选项C）尽管第二位法官的证据裁定可能与第一位法官的不一致，但一事不再理条款被违反是由于宣布审判无效缺乏明显必要性。如果该无效审判是基于明显必要性，那么即使存在证据裁定不一致的风险，由不同法官进行的第二次审判也不会违反一事不再理条款。

Educational objective:
Double jeopardy does not bar a second prosecution following a mistrial if the defendant
requested the mistrial or it was based on a manifest necessity—(1) when an unforeseeable
event made it highly necessary to end the proceedings and (2) the judge exercised sound
and rational discretion before doing so.

References
U.S. Const. amend. V (prohibition against double jeopardy).

United States v. Perez, 22 U.S. 579, 580 (1824) (holding that a retrial is permitted when it is
based on a manifest necessity).

United States v. Jorn, 400 U.S. 470, 486–87 (1971); Arizona v. Washington, 434 U.S. 497,
514–17 (1978) (explaining that a judge must exercise sound and rational discretion when
determining whether manifest necessity exists).

Love v. Morton, 944 F.Supp. 379, 390–91 (D.N.J. 1996) (finding that there was no manifest
necessity for a mistrial when the judge's mother-in-law died because he failed to exercise
sound and rational discretion).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law / Double Jeopardy
正确答案
选项 D
⚖️ 核心考点：明显必要性 (Manifest Necessity)

根据美国宪法第五修正案的一事不再理条款 (Double Jeopardy Clause)，如果法官在没有被告同意的情况下宣布无效审判 (Mistrial)，除非存在“明显必要性”，否则禁止重审。

逻辑推演路径
1
风险何时附着 (Attachment of Jeopardy)？
在陪审团审判中，陪审团宣誓就职时，风险即已附着。本案中审判已进行4小时，因此一事不再理保护已生效。
2
法官的行为是否恰当？
法官因家庭紧急情况（岳母去世）宣布无效审判。虽然理由正当，但最高法院要求法官在宣布无效审判前必须行使“健全的自由裁量权” (Sound Discretion)。
3
为何没有“明显必要性”？
法官没有咨询律师，也没有考虑替代方案（如休庭延期、更换法官等）。这种仓促的决定 (acted precipitously) 意味着不存在法律意义上的“明显必要性”。
参考判例：United States v. Jorn; Love v. Morton
4
结论
由于缺乏明显必要性，且被告未同意无效审判，第二次审判违反了一事不再理原则。
为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A (Good Faith) 错误：
法官的主观善意 (Good Faith) 不能弥补程序上的错误。即使法官不是为了伤害被告，但他未能考虑替代方案，依然导致重审被禁止。
选项 B (No Verdict) 错误：
这是无效审判的定义，而不是允许重审的理由。只有在被告请求无效审判或存在明显必要性时，未获裁决的案件才能重审。
💡 MBE 提分技巧

在涉及 Mistrial 的题目中，如果法官是因为突发状况（生病、缺席等）直接宣布无效审判，一定要检查法官是否“尝试过其他补救措施”。如果法官“立即”或“未咨询双方”就解散陪审团，通常意味着缺乏 Manifest Necessity，从而禁止重审。

questions.question:
A department store had experienced a growing incidence of shoplifting. At the store's request, the police concealed a detective at a vantage point above the women's apparel fitting rooms where she could see into these rooms, where customers tried on clothes. The detective saw a teenager enter a fitting room, shut the door, stuff a dress into her purse, leave the fitting room, and start for the street door. By prearranged signal, the detective notified another police officer near the door, who detained the teenager as she started to go out into the street. The teenager was placed under arrest, and the dress was retrieved from her purse.
The teenager is charged with shoplifting. At trial, she moves to suppress the introduction of the dress into evidence.
How will the court likely rule on her motion?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the detective could see into the room and thus the teenager's activities were legitimately in plain view.
choices.b: Deny the motion, because the search and seizure were made incident to a valid arrest based on probable cause.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because an individual has a reasonable expectation of privacy while using a department store fitting room.
choices.d: Grant the motion, because the police should have secured a search warrant to search her purse.

一家百货公司遭遇了日益增多的商店盗窃事件。应商店要求，警方将一名侦探隐藏在女装试衣间上方的一个有利位置，从那里她可以窥视顾客试穿衣服的这些房间。该侦探看到一名青少年进入试衣间，关上门，将一件连衣裙塞进她的手提包，离开试衣间，然后走向临街的大门。通过预先安排的信号，该侦探通知了门口附近的另一名警官，当该青少年正要走到街上时，这名警官将其拘留。该青少年被逮捕，连衣裙也从她的手提包中被搜出。

该青少年被控商店盗窃。在审判中，她提出动议，要求排除将该连衣裙作为证据采纳。

法院很可能会如何裁定她的动议？
options:
A. Deny the motion, because the detective could see into the room and thus the teenager's activities were legitimately in plain view.
驳回动议，因为侦探可以看到房间内的情况，因此该青少年的活动合法地处于一目了然（plain view）的状态。

B. Deny the motion, because the search and seizure were made incident to a valid arrest based on probable cause.
驳回动议，因为搜查和扣押是基于合理根据（probable cause）的有效逮捕的附带行为。

C. Grant the motion, because an individual has a reasonable expectation of privacy while using a department store fitting room.
批准动议，因为个人在使用百货公司试衣间时拥有合理的隐私期待。

D. Grant the motion, because the police should have secured a search warrant to search her purse.
批准动议，因为警方本应获得搜查令才能搜查她的手提包。
data.explanation:
The Fourth Amendment protects persons from unreasonable government searches and seizures. A Fourth Amendment search occurs when one of the following tests is met:
  • Physical trespass test - the government physically intruded upon a constitutionally protected area - a person's body, home, papers, or effects - to obtain information.
  • Reasonable expectation of privacy test - the government invaded (1) a person's subjective expectation of privacy (2) that society would find objectively reasonable.

A Fourth Amendment search is presumptively unreasonable if it is conducted without a warrant. And under the fruit of the poisonous tree doctrine, any evidence that stems from an unreasonable search should be suppressed at trial.

Here, the physical trespass test is not met since a department store fitting room is not a constitutionally protected area. However, the reasonable expectation of privacy test is met since society would find the teenager's subjective expectation of privacy in the fitting room objectively reasonable. And since the detective did not have a warrant to search the fitting room, the search was unreasonable and violated the Fourth Amendment.

Due to the unreasonable search, the detective was able to see the teenager stuff a dress into her purse. The detective then notified another police officer, who arrested the teenager and retrieved the stolen dress. And since the seizure of the dress (fruit) stemmed from the unreasonable search (poisonous tree), the court should grant the teenager's motion to suppress the introduction of the dress into evidence.

(Choice A) Under the plain view doctrine, police may seize an item without a warrant if (1) it is in plain view, (2) they immediately recognize it as contraband, and (3) they are lawfully in the area - eg, they have a warrant to search the premises for another item. Here, the detective could plainly see into the fitting room and immediately recognized the dress as evidence of the crime. But since she was there unlawfully (eg, without a warrant), this doctrine does not apply.

(Choice B) After making a valid arrest based on untainted probable cause, police may (1) conduct a warrantless search of a person's body and the area within his/her immediate control and (2) seize any evidence discovered in that search. But here, the teenager's arrest was based on tainted probable cause (the warrantless search of the fitting room), so the search of her purse and seizure of the dress were incident to an invalid arrest.

(Choice D) The police should have secured a search warrant based on untainted probable cause to search the teenager's purse. However, the police could not do so since they only had tainted probable cause supplied by the detective's unreasonable search of the dressing room. Therefore, the court will likely grant the motion to suppress because the detective violated the teenager's reasonable expectation of privacy.

Educational objective: A Fourth Amendment search occurs when the government (1) physically intrudes upon a constitutionally protected area or (2) invades a person's subjective and objectively reasonable expectation of privacy. A warrantless Fourth Amendment search is presumptively unreasonable, and any evidence that stems from the search should be suppressed.



选项正确率统计：A选项 3%，B选项 15%，C选项 80%（正确选项），D选项 0%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

Fourth Amendment 保护个人免受政府不合理的搜查和扣押。当满足以下任一标准时，即构成 Fourth Amendment 所指的搜查：
  • 物理侵入标准 - 政府为获取信息而物理侵入受宪法保护的区域——即个人身体、住宅、文件或财物。
  • 合理隐私期待标准 - 政府侵犯了（1）个人主观上的隐私期待，并且（2）该期待被社会认为是客观上合理的。

在没有搜查令的情况下进行的 Fourth Amendment 搜查被推定为不合理。并且，根据毒树之果原则（fruit of the poisonous tree doctrine），任何源于不合理搜查的证据在审判中都应被排除。

在本案中，物理侵入标准未被满足，因为百货公司的试衣间不属于受宪法保护的区域。然而，合理隐私期待标准得到了满足，因为社会会认为该青少年在试衣间内的主观隐私期待是客观上合理的。并且，由于该侦探没有搜查试衣间的搜查令，其搜查行为是不合理的，违反了 Fourth Amendment。

由于这次不合理的搜查，侦探才得以看到该青少年将连衣裙塞进手提包。随后，该侦探通知了另一名警官，后者逮捕了该青少年并搜出了被盗的连衣裙。并且，由于连衣裙的扣押（果实）源于不合理的搜查（毒树），法院应批准该青少年提出的排除该连衣裙作为证据的动议。

(选项A) 根据一目了然原则（plain view doctrine），警方可以在没有搜查令的情况下扣押物品，前提是（1）该物品处于一目了然的位置，（2）他们能立即识别出其为违禁品，以及（3）他们处于该区域是合法的——例如，他们持有搜查该场所其他物品的搜查令。在本案中，侦探可以清楚地看到试衣间内，并立即认出该连衣裙是犯罪证据。但由于她身处该地不合法（例如，没有搜查令），该原则不适用。

(选项B) 在基于未受污染的合理根据（probable cause）进行有效逮捕后，警方可以（1）对被捕者的人身及其直接控制范围内的区域进行无证搜查，并（2）扣押在该搜查中发现的任何证据。但在本案中，对该青少年的逮捕是基于受污染的合理根据（对试衣间的无证搜查），因此对其手提包的搜查和连衣裙的扣押是附带于一次无效逮捕的行为。

(选项D) 警方本应基于未受污染的合理根据申请搜查令，以搜查该青少年的手提包。然而，警方无法这样做，因为他们仅有的合理根据是由侦探对更衣室的不合理搜查所提供的受污染的合理根据。因此，法院很可能会批准排除证据的动议，因为侦探侵犯了该青少年的合理隐私期待。

教学目标：当政府（1）物理侵入受宪法保护的区域，或（2）侵犯了个人主观上且客观上合理的隐私期待时，即构成 Fourth Amendment 所指的搜查。无证的 Fourth Amendment 搜查被推定为不合理，任何源于该搜查的证据都应被排除。

References

U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).

Katz v. United States, 389 U.S. 347, 361 (1967) (establishing the reasonable expectation of privacy test).

United States v. Jones, 565 U.S. 400, 407 (2012) (explaining the physical trespass test).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Search & Seizure
核心考点：Katz 测试

本题的核心在于判断警方的行为是否构成了美国宪法第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）下的“搜查”（Search）。

根据 Katz v. United States (1967) 确立的标准，如果满足以下两点，即构成搜查：
  1. 个人表现出了主观的隐私期待 (Subjective expectation of privacy)；
  2. 这种期待被社会认为是客观合理的 (Objectively reasonable)。

如果构成了“搜查”，警方通常需要搜查令 (Warrant)，否则该搜查被推定为不合理。

本案分析
1. 试衣间的性质
试衣间 (Fitting room) 是顾客更换衣物的私密空间。顾客关上门，主观上显然有隐私期待。社会普遍认为在试衣间内不应被偷窥，因此这种期待是客观合理的。
2. 警方的行为
警方在没有搜查令的情况下，通过隐藏位置窥视试衣间内部。这侵犯了被告的合理隐私期待 (Reasonable Expectation of Privacy, REP)。
3. 结论
警方的窥视行为构成了非法的无证搜查 (Illegal warrantless search)。
证据排除规则

由于最初的观察是非法的，根据“毒树之果”原则 (Fruit of the Poisonous Tree Doctrine)，由此衍生的所有证据都必须被排除。

毒树 (Poisonous Tree)
非法窥视试衣间
⬇️
果实 (Fruit)
看到偷窃行为 ➔ 逮捕 ➔ 搜查手提包 ➔ 发现连衣裙

因此，法院应批准排除连衣裙作为证据的动议。

✅ 正确答案：选项 C

"Grant the motion, because an individual has a reasonable expectation of privacy while using a department store fitting room."

这是最直接的法律依据。因为存在合理的隐私期待，警方的窥视才构成搜查；因为没有搜查令，搜查才非法；因为搜查非法，证据才被排除。

❌ 易错项辨析：选项 A

Plain View (一目了然法则) 为什么不适用？

Plain View Doctrine 适用的前提是警方必须合法地处于 (lawfully present) 能够观察到证据的位置。

在本案中，侦探是通过侵犯隐私（非法搜查）才获得了观察位置，因此不能援引 Plain View 原则来洗白其发现的证据。

❌ 易错项辨析：选项 B

Search Incident to Arrest (逮捕附带搜查) 为什么不适用？

SIA 必须基于合法的逮捕 (Valid Arrest)。本案中，逮捕的理由（Probable Cause）完全来自于非法的偷窥。由于“毒树之果”效应，逮捕本身也是非法的，因此附带的搜查也是非法的。

💡 MBE 考试技巧：
遇到 Fourth Amendment 题目，首先问自己：
"Did the police intrude on a reasonable expectation of privacy?"
如果是，且没有 Warrant 或 Exception，那就是违宪。

questions.question:
A necktie salesman was charged with the murder of a woman who had been strangled and whose body was found in the woods near his home. The salesman suffers from a neurological problem that makes it impossible for him to remember an occurrence for longer than 48 hours.
After the salesman was charged, the police visited him and asked if they might search his home. The salesman consented. During their search, the police found a diary written by the salesman. An entry dated the same day as the woman's disappearance read, "Indescribable excitement. Why did no one ever tell me that killing gave such pleasure to the master?"
The salesman was charged with murder. His attorney has moved to exclude the diary from evidence on the ground that its admission would violate the salesman's privilege against self-incrimination. His counsel has also argued that the salesman could not give informed consent to the search because more than 48 hours had passed since the making of the entry and hence he could not remember the existence of the incriminating entry at the time he gave his consent. There is no evidence that the police officers who secured the salesman's consent to the search were aware of his memory impairment.
Should the court admit the diary into evidence?

choices.a: No, because the salesman was not competent to consent to a search.
choices.b: No, because use of the diary as evidence would violate the salesman's privilege against self-incrimination.
choices.c: Yes, because the salesman's consent was not obtained by intentional police misconduct and the salesman was not compelled to make the diary entry.
choices.d: Yes, pursuant to the good-faith exception to the exclusionary rule.

Q85076

A necktie salesman was charged with the murder of a woman who had been strangled and whose body was found in the woods near his home. The salesman suffers from a neurological problem that makes it impossible for him to remember an occurrence for longer than 48 hours.

After the salesman was charged, the police visited him and asked if they might search his home. The salesman consented. During their search, the police found a diary written by the salesman. An entry dated the same day as the woman's disappearance read, "Indescribable excitement. Why did no one ever tell me that killing gave such pleasure to the master?"

The salesman was charged with murder. His attorney has moved to exclude the diary from evidence on the ground that its admission would violate the salesman's privilege against self-incrimination. His counsel has also argued that the salesman could not give informed consent to the search because more than 48 hours had passed since the making of the entry and hence he could not remember the existence of the incriminating entry at the time he gave his consent. There is no evidence that the police officers who secured the salesman's consent to the search were aware of his memory impairment.

Should the court admit the diary into evidence?

一名领带销售员被指控谋杀一名妇女，该妇女被勒死，其尸体在他家附近的树林中被发现。该销售员患有神经系统问题，导致他无法记住任何超过48小时的事件。

在该销售员被指控后，警方拜访了他，并询问是否可以搜查他的家。该销售员表示同意。在搜查过程中，警方发现了一本该销售员写的日记。一篇与该女子失踪同日期的条目写道：“难以形容的兴奋。为什么从来没有人告诉我，杀戮能给主人带来如此大的快感？”

该销售员被控犯有谋杀罪。他的律师已动议将日记排除在证据之外，理由是采纳日记将侵犯销售员反对自证其罪的特权。其律师还辩称，该销售员无法对搜查作出知情同意，因为距离写下该日记条目已超过48小时，因此他在同意搜查时已不记得存在这条可致其入罪的记录。没有证据表明，获得销售员搜查同意的警官知道他的记忆障碍。

法院是否应该将该日记采纳为证据？
options:
A. No, because the salesman was not competent to consent to a search.
不应采纳，因为该销售员不具备同意搜查的法律能力。

B. No, because use of the diary as evidence would violate the salesman's privilege against self-incrimination.
不应采纳，因为使用该日记作为证据将侵犯销售员反对自证其罪的特权。

C. Yes, because the salesman's consent was not obtained by intentional police misconduct and the salesman was not compelled to make the diary entry.
应该采纳，因为销售员的同意并非通过警方的故意不当行为获得，且销售员并未被强迫写下日记条目。

D. Yes, pursuant to the good-faith exception to the exclusionary rule.
应该采纳，依据证据排除规则的善意例外原则。
data.explanation:
The salesman argues that the warrantless search of his home violated the Fourth Amendment because he could not give informed consent to the search. However, consent need only be given freely and voluntarily (ie, without police coercion ) - informed consent is not required. Therefore, police do not need to inform a suspect of his/her right to refuse consent or the incriminating evidence they hope to obtain.

Here, due to his neurological condition, the salesman could not remember the incriminating diary entry when he consented to the police search. But since his consent was not obtained by intentional police misconduct or other coercive measures, it was given voluntarily. Therefore, the police had valid consent to search the salesman's home, and the diary discovered during the search should not be excluded on Fourth Amendment grounds.

The salesman also argues that admitting the diary would violate his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. This privilege protects persons from being compelled to produce or create self-incriminating evidence - ie, evidence that could be used (or lead to other evidence that might be used) against him/her in a criminal prosecution. But this protection does not apply to documents obtained during a constitutional search since the government did not compel the person to produce or create them.

Here, the diary entry is incriminating because it implicates the salesman in the woman's murder. But admitting this evidence would not violate his privilege against self-incrimination since (1) it was discovered during a lawful search of his home (no compelled production) and (2) the salesman was not compelled to create the diary entry (Choice B). Therefore, the court should deny the salesman's motion and admit the diary into evidence.

(Choice A) Incompetency (eg, neurological or mental illness) alone does not invalidate a person's consent. Instead, it is one factor used to determine if consent was voluntary. But the salesman's competency is not an issue here since there is no evidence that the police knew about his neurological condition (or took advantage of it to coerce his consent).

(Choice D) The good-faith exception to the exclusionary rule allows the admission of illegally seized evidence if police reasonably believed that they were acting lawfully (eg, relying on a warrant later deemed invalid). But this exception does not apply here since the officers legally searched the salesman's home and seized the diary.

Educational objective: Police may conduct a warrantless search if the person consented to the search voluntarily - ie, without police coercion - even if the consent was not informed. Additionally, the privilege against self-incrimination only applies to the compelled production or creation of evidence - not evidence discovered during a constitutional search.



选项正确率统计：A选项 4%，B选项 7%，C选项 73%（正确选项），D选项 14%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

该销售员辩称，对其住所的无证搜查违反了Fourth Amendment，因为他无法对搜查作出知情同意。然而，同意只需自由且自愿地作出（即没有警方的胁迫）——法律不要求知情同意。因此，警方无需告知嫌疑人其有权拒绝同意，也无需告知他们希望获得的致罪证据。

在本案中，由于其神经系统状况，该销售员在同意警方搜查时，已不记得那条可致其入罪的日记条目。但由于他的同意并非通过警方的故意不当行为或其他胁迫手段获得，因此该同意是自愿作出的。所以，警方对销售员住所的搜查获得了有效同意，搜查中发现的日记不应以违反Fourth Amendment为由被排除。

该销售员还辩称，采纳该日记将侵犯其Fifth Amendment规定的反对自证其罪的特权。该特权保护个人免于被强迫出示或制作自证其罪的证据——即，在刑事诉讼中可能被用来（或导致发现其他可能被用来）对其不利的证据。但此项保护不适用于在合宪搜查中获取的文件，因为政府并未强迫该人出示或制作这些文件。

在本案中，日记条目是可致入罪的，因为它暗示销售员与该女子的谋杀案有关。但采纳该证据并不会侵犯他反对自证其罪的特权，因为（1）它是在对其住所的合法搜查中发现的（没有被强迫出示），并且（2）该销售员并未被强迫制作该日记条目（选项B）。因此，法院应驳回该销售员的动议，并将该日记采纳为证据。

（选项A）不具备法律能力（例如，神经或精神疾病）本身并不会使一个人的同意无效。相反，它是在确定同意是否自愿时所考虑的一个因素。但在本案中，该销售员的法律能力不成问题，因为没有证据表明警方知道他的神经系统状况（或利用此状况来胁迫他同意）。

（选项D）证据排除规则的善意例外原则允许采纳非法扣押的证据，前提是警方有理由相信其行为是合法的（例如，依赖一份后来被裁定为无效的搜查令）。但此例外不适用于本案，因为警官是合法地搜查了销售员的住所并扣押了日记。

教学目标：如果个人自愿同意搜查（即没有警方的胁迫），即使该同意并非知情同意，警方也可以进行无证搜查。此外，反对自证其罪的特权仅适用于被强迫出示或制作的证据，而不适用于在合宪搜查中发现的证据。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Schneckloth v. Bustamonte, 412 U.S. 218, 225 - 28 (1973) (explaining that consent must be voluntary and not the result of police coercion).
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • United States v. Hubbell, 530 U.S. 27, 35 - 36 (2000) (explaining that contents of documents that a defendant was not compelled to create are not privileged).

MBE 考题解析

Constitutional Law / Criminal Procedure
Topic: Search & Seizure / Self-Incrimination
正确答案：选项 C Yes, because the salesman's consent was not obtained by intentional police misconduct...

核心考点深度解析

1. 第四修正案：同意搜查 (Consent Search)

本题的关键在于判断被告的“同意”是否有效。根据 Fourth Amendment，警方在获得有效同意的情况下可以进行无证搜查。

法律标准：同意必须是自愿的 (Voluntary)，即没有警方的胁迫 (Coercion)。

误区警示：法律不要求“知情同意” (Informed Consent)。

  • 警方不需要告知嫌疑人他有权拒绝。
  • 嫌疑人不需要确切记得家里有什么罪证。

本案分析：虽然被告有记忆障碍，但警方并不知道这一点，也没有利用这一点进行胁迫。在“总体情况” (Totality of the Circumstances) 下，他的同意是自愿的。

2. 第五修正案：反对自证其罪 (Self-Incrimination)

被告律师辩称日记违反了 Fifth Amendment。这个论点是错误的。

✍️
自愿书写
(非强迫制作)
+
👮‍♂️
合法搜查
(非强迫提交)
=
✅
可采纳

原理：第五修正案保护的是“被强迫的” (Compelled) 证言。

  • 被告写日记时是自愿的（没有警察拿枪指着他写）。
  • 警方获取日记是通过合法的搜查（Consent Search），而不是通过传票强迫被告“交出”日记。

因此，日记作为证据不违反第五修正案。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (Competence)

错误理由： 精神或神经问题本身不会自动导致同意无效。只有当警方利用这种精神状态进行胁迫，或者该状态导致当事人完全无法理解其行为性质时才无效。本案中警方不知情，且无胁迫行为。

选项 B (Privilege)

错误理由： 如上所述，第五修正案不保护在合法搜查中被扣押的、自愿撰写的私人文件。

选项 D (Good Faith)

错误理由： Good-faith exception 通常适用于警方依赖了一份后来被判定无效的搜查令 (Warrant) 的情况。本案是无证搜查 (Warrantless Search)，依据的是同意，因此该例外原则不适用（也不需要适用，因为搜查本身就是合法的）。

🎓 MBE 考试通关秘籍

1. 区分 "Voluntary" vs. "Informed"：
在 Fourth Amendment 同意搜查中，只要没有胁迫 (Coercion) 就是有效的。不要被“嫌疑人不知道后果”或“嫌疑人记性不好”所迷惑。

2. 私人文件的获取方式：
如果是警方搜出来的（Search），通常不涉及第五修正案问题；如果是强迫被告交出来的（Subpoena），才可能涉及第五修正案的“强迫性行为”。

questions.question:
After a liquor store was robbed, the police received an anonymous telephone call naming a store employee as the perpetrator of the robbery. Honestly believing that their actions were permitted by the U.S. Constitution, the police talked one of the employee's neighbors into going to the employee's home with a hidden recording device to engage him in a conversation about the crime. The neighbor went to the employee's home and was invited inside. During the conversation in the employee's home, the employee admitted having committed the robbery.
The employee was charged with the robbery in state court. He has moved to suppress the recording on the grounds that the method of obtaining it violated both his federal and his state constitutional rights.
Assume that a clear precedent from the state's highest court would result in a finding that the conduct of the police in making the recording violated the employee's rights under the state constitution, and that excluding the recording is the proper remedy.
Should the court grant the employee's motion?

choices.a: No, because the employee's federal constitutional rights were not violated, and this circumstance overrides any state constitutional provisions.
choices.b: No, because the police were acting in the good-faith belief that the federal Constitution permitted their actions.
choices.c: Yes, because the making of the recording violated the employee's federal constitutional rights.
choices.d: Yes, because the making of the recording violated the state constitution.

Honestly believing that their actions were permitted by the U.S. Constitution, the police talked one of the employee's neighbors into going to the employee's home with a hidden recording device to engage him in a conversation about the crime. The neighbor went to the employee's home and was invited inside. During the conversation in the employee's home, the employee admitted having committed the robbery.

The employee was charged with the robbery in state court. He has moved to suppress the recording on the grounds that the method of obtaining it violated both his federal and his state constitutional rights.

Assume that a clear precedent from the state's highest court would result in a finding that the conduct of the police in making the recording violated the employee's rights under the state constitution, and that excluding the recording is the proper remedy.

Should the court grant the employee's motion?

一家酒类商店被抢劫后，警方接到一个匿名电话，指称一名商店雇员是抢劫案的作案人。警方真诚地相信其行为是 U.S. Constitution 所允许的，因此说服该雇员的一位邻居携带隐藏的录音设备前往雇员家中，与其就该犯罪行为进行交谈。邻居前往该雇员的家，并被邀请入内。在雇员家中的谈话期间，该雇员承认实施了抢劫。

该雇员在州法院被指控犯有抢劫罪。他已动议排除该录音，理由是获取录音的方法侵犯了其联邦和州的宪法权利。

假设该州最高法院的一个明确判例会导致认定警方的录音行为侵犯了该雇员在州宪法下的权利，并且排除该录音是适当的救济措施。

法院是否应批准该雇员的动议？
options:
A. No, because the employee's federal constitutional rights were not violated, and this circumstance overrides any state constitutional provisions.
不应批准，因为该雇员的联邦宪法权利未被侵犯，并且此情况优先于任何州宪法条款。

B. No, because the police were acting in the good-faith belief that the federal Constitution permitted their actions.
不应批准，因为警方是基于善意信念行事，认为联邦宪法允许其行为。

C. Yes, because the making of the recording violated the employee's federal constitutional rights.
应批准，因为制作该录音侵犯了该雇员的联邦宪法权利。

D. Yes, because the making of the recording violated the state constitution.
应批准，因为制作该录音违反了州宪法。
data.explanation:
Although the federal Constitution sets a "floor" for personal liberties, state constitutions may offer protections that exceed the minimum federal constitutional requirements. And when a state's highest court sets clear precedent regarding a state constitutional right, lower state courts (trial and intermediate courts) must follow that precedent when resolving a similar legal issue.

Here, the employee moved to suppress (ie, exclude) the recording from evidence on the grounds that it was obtained in violation of his state and federal constitutional rights. The state's highest court has set a clear precedent establishing that the recording violated the employee's state constitutional rights and should be excluded from evidence. Therefore, the state court must follow this precedent and suppress the recording on this ground.

(Choices A & C) A defendant's Fourth Amendment rights are not violated when a government informant speaks with the defendant and secretly records their conversation (as seen here). However, compliance with the federal Constitution does not excuse a violation of a defendant's broader state constitutional protections. Therefore, the motion to suppress the recording should be granted on state constitutional grounds.

(Choice B) Under the good-faith exception, evidence obtained in violation of a defendant's federal constitutional rights is admissible if the police reasonably believed that they were acting lawfully (eg, that their actions were permitted by a prior court ruling). But here, the police's good-faith belief that the federal Constitution permitted the recording is irrelevant since this state's clear precedent holds that their actions violated the state constitution.

Educational objective: State constitutions may offer greater protections than the federal Constitution - eg, a state exclusionary rule can suppress more evidence than the federal exclusionary rule. And lower state courts must comply with precedents from the state's highest court that interpreted those protections.



选项正确率统计：A选项 6%，B选项 15%，C选项 25%，D选项 52%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

尽管联邦宪法为个人自由设定了“底线”，但州宪法可以提供超出联邦宪法最低要求的保护。并且，当一个州的最高法院就某项州宪法权利确立了明确的判例时，下级州法院（审判法院和上诉法院）在解决类似的法律问题时必须遵循该判例。

在本案中，该雇员以获取录音的方式违反其州和联邦宪法权利为由，动议排除（即不采纳为证据）该录音。该州最高法院已确立明确判例，认定该录音侵犯了雇员的州宪法权利，应被排除在证据之外。因此，州法院必须遵循此判例，并以此为由排除该录音。

（选项 A 和 C）当政府线人与被告交谈并秘密录下其对话时（如本案所示），被告的 Fourth Amendment 权利并未受到侵犯。然而，遵守联邦宪法并不能成为侵犯被告更广泛的州宪法保护的理由。因此，应基于州宪法的理由批准排除该录音的动议。

（选项 B）根据善意例外规则，如果警方有合理理由相信其行为合法（例如，其行为是依据先前的法院裁决所允许的），那么违反被告联邦宪法权利所获得的证据是可采纳的。但在本案中，警方善意地相信联邦宪法允许该录音是无关紧要的，因为该州的明确判例认定其行为违反了州宪法。

教学目标：州宪法可能提供比联邦宪法更强的保护——例如，州的证据排除规则可以比联邦的证据排除规则排除更多的证据。并且，下级州法院必须遵守该州最高法院就这些保护所作出的解释性判例。

References

Ker v. California, 374 U.S. 23, 34 (1963) (explaining that states can grant broader rights than the U.S. Constitution).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析：宪法保护层级

D

正确选项

核心法律原则

Federalism (联邦主义) Supremacy Clause (至高条款)

本题考察的是美国宪法与州宪法之间的关系，即“底线与天花板”理论。

  • 联邦宪法 (U.S. Constitution)：设定了个人权利保护的最低标准 (Floor)。任何州不得提供低于此标准的保护。
  • 州宪法 (State Constitution)：可以提供比联邦宪法更高、更广泛 (Broader) 的保护。

案情深度解析

1. 联邦宪法层面：
根据美国最高法院的判例（如 United States v. White），警方使用线人（"False Friend"）携带窃听器进入嫌疑人家中录音，并不违反第四修正案 (Fourth Amendment)。因为嫌疑人是自愿向第三方透露信息，他承担了该第三方可能是警方线人的风险。

2. 州宪法层面：
题目明确指出：该州最高法院有明确判例 (Clear Precedent)，认定这种行为违反了州宪法。

3. 结论：
虽然警方的行为符合联邦宪法，但违反了提供“更高保护”的州宪法。在州法院审理州法指控的案件中，必须遵循州最高法院对州宪法的解释。因此，证据必须被排除。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A 错误：
虽然联邦法律是最高法律（Supremacy Clause），但这仅适用于州法试图剥夺联邦权利的情况。州法给予被告更多权利并不与联邦法律冲突，因此联邦宪法不会“覆盖” (Override) 州宪法提供的额外保护。

选项 B 错误：
善意例外 (Good-faith exception) 通常适用于联邦第四修正案的排除规则。但在本案中，排除证据的依据是州宪法。如果州最高法院决定不承认善意例外，或者认定州宪法的违规不能通过善意来补救，那么警方的善意信念就无关紧要。

选项 C 错误：
这是一个事实错误。如前所述，根据现行联邦判例，秘密录制与线人的对话并不违反联邦宪法权利。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

当题目中出现“州最高法院判例” (State Supreme Court Precedent) 且涉及个人权利时，请记住：

  1. 州可以给被告更多权利，不能给更少。
  2. 如果州宪法说“这是违法的”，即使联邦最高法院说“这是合法的”，在州法院系统中，州法说了算。
  3. 这就是所谓的 Independent and Adequate State Grounds（独立且充分的州法依据）。
MBE Criminal Procedure & Constitutional Law Review

questions.question:
A defendant was validly arrested for the murder of a store clerk and was taken to a police station where he was given Miranda warnings. When an interrogator asked the defendant, "Do you understand your Miranda rights, and are you willing to give up those rights and talk to us?" the defendant replied, "Yes." When asked, "Did you kill the clerk?" the defendant replied, "No." When asked, "Where were you on the day the clerk was killed?" the defendant replied, "Maybe I should talk to a lawyer." The interrogator asked, "Are you sure?" and the defendant replied, "I'm not sure." The interrogator then asked, "Why would you want to talk with a lawyer?" and the defendant replied, "Because I killed the clerk. It was an accident, and I think I need a lawyer to defend me." At that point all interrogation ceased. Later, the defendant was formally charged with murdering the clerk.
The defendant has moved to suppress evidence of his statement "I killed the clerk" on the ground that this statement was elicited in violation of his Miranda rights. Should the defendant's motion be granted?

choices.a: No, because although the defendant effectively asserted the right to counsel, the question "Why would you want to talk with a lawyer?" did not constitute custodial interrogation.
choices.b: No, because the defendant did not effectively assert the right to counsel, and his conduct prior to making the statement constituted a valid waiver of his Miranda rights.
choices.c: Yes, because although the defendant did not effectively assert the right to counsel, his conduct prior to making the statement did not constitute a valid waiver of his Miranda rights.
choices.d: Yes, because the defendant effectively asserted the right to counsel, and the question "Why would you want to talk with a lawyer?" constituted custodial interrogation.

一名被告因谋杀一名商店店员而被合法逮捕，并被带到警察局，在那里他被告知了 Miranda 警告。当审讯人员问被告：“你是否理解你的 Miranda 权利，并愿意放弃这些权利与我们交谈？”被告回答：“是的。”当被问及：“你是否杀害了店员？”被告回答：“没有。”当被问及：“店员被杀害那天你在哪里？”被告回答：“也许我应该和律师谈谈。”审讯人员问道：“你确定吗？”被告回答：“我不确定。”审讯人员接着问：“你为什么想和律师谈？”被告回答：“因为我杀了那个店员。那是个意外，我认为我需要一个律师为我辩护。”此时，所有审讯都停止了。后来，被告被正式指控谋杀该店员。

被告已提出动议，以其“我杀了店员”的陈述是在违反其 Miranda 权利的情况下诱导得出的为由，要求排除该陈述证据。被告的动议应被批准吗？
options:
A. No, because although the defendant effectively asserted the right to counsel, the question "Why would you want to talk with a lawyer?" did not constitute custodial interrogation.
不应批准，因为尽管被告有效地主张了获得律师帮助的权利，但“你为什么想和律师谈？”这个问题不构成羁押讯问。

B. No, because the defendant did not effectively assert the right to counsel, and his conduct prior to making the statement constituted a valid waiver of his Miranda rights.
不应批准，因为被告并未有效地主张获得律师帮助的权利，并且他在做出该陈述之前的行为构成了对其 Miranda 权利的有效放弃。

C. Yes, because although the defendant did not effectively assert the right to counsel, his conduct prior to making the statement did not constitute a valid waiver of his Miranda rights.
应批准，因为尽管被告并未有效地主张获得律师帮助的权利，但他在做出该陈述之前的行为并不构成对其 Miranda 权利的有效放弃。

D. Yes, because the defendant effectively asserted the right to counsel, and the question "Why would you want to talk with a lawyer?" constituted custodial interrogation.
应批准，因为被告有效地主张了获得律师帮助的权利，并且“你为什么想和律师谈？”这个问题构成了羁押讯问。
data.explanation:
Fifth & Sixth Amendment Right to Counsel


Right to counselApplicabilityRequestWaiver
Fifth AmendmentSuspect has right to counsel when: in custody and subjected to interrogationUnambiguous request requiredValid if made: knowingly intelligently voluntarily
Sixth AmendmentDefendant has right to counsel when: judicial proceedings commence and critical stage of prosecutionNo request required (attaches automatically)
Police must inform suspects of their Fifth Amendment Miranda right to counsel before a custodial interrogation. Police are free to question a suspect if he/she waives this right, but must stop questioning once the suspect makes an unambiguous request for counsel (eg, "I want a lawyer"). If police fail to honor that request and continue to question the suspect without the presence of counsel, the court should suppress the suspect's responses.

Here, the defendant validly waived his Miranda right to counsel before the custodial interrogation. And though the defendant later told the police interrogator " Maybe I should talk to a lawyer" and reiterated that he was " not sure ," his statements were too ambiguous to effectively request counsel. Therefore, the interrogator was free to continue questioning the defendant without counsel present and the court should deny the defendant's motion to suppress his statement that he killed the clerk.

(Choices A & D) Since the defendant was validly arrested (custody) and the police interrogator's questioning was reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response (interrogation), the question "Why would you want to talk to a lawyer?" does constitute custodial interrogation. But since the defendant validly waived his Miranda rights and did not effectively assert his right to counsel, his answer is admissible at trial.

(Choice C) After being Mirandized, the defendant clearly stated that he understood his rights and that he was willing to give up those rights and talk to the interrogator. Therefore, the defendant unequivocally and validly waived his Miranda rights.

Educational objective: Police are free to question a suspect who waives his/her Fifth Amendment (Miranda) right to counsel. However, if the suspect later makes an unambiguous request for counsel, police must stop questioning until the suspect's lawyer is present. If the police continue questioning, the suspect's responses should be suppressed.

选项正确率统计：A选项 0%，B选项 81%（正确选项），C选项 10%，D选项 7%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

第五和第六修正案中的律师帮助权


律师帮助权适用性请求放弃
Fifth Amendment嫌疑人在以下情况有权获得律师帮助：处于羁押状态并接受讯问需要明确无误的请求在以下情况下有效：知情地、明智地、自愿地
Sixth Amendment被告在以下情况有权获得律师帮助：司法程序开始且处于起诉的关键阶段无需请求（自动附加）
在进行羁押讯问前，警方必须告知嫌疑人其第五修正案中的 Miranda 律师帮助权。如果嫌疑人放弃了此项权利，警方可以自由地进行讯问，但一旦嫌疑人提出明确无误的律师请求（例如，“我想要一名律师”），则必须停止讯问。如果警方未能尊重该请求，并在没有律师在场的情况下继续讯问嫌疑人，法院应排除嫌疑人的回答作为证据。

在本案中，被告在羁押讯问前有效地放弃了他的 Miranda 律师帮助权。而且，尽管被告后来告诉审讯人员“也许我应该和律师谈谈”，并重申他“不确定”，但他的陈述过于含糊，不足以有效地请求律师帮助。因此，审讯人员可以在没有律师在场的情况下继续讯问被告，法院应驳回被告要求排除其杀害店员陈述的动议。

（选项 A 和 D）由于被告被合法逮捕（羁押），且警方审讯人员的提问有合理可能引出有罪回应（讯问），因此“你为什么想和律师谈？”这个问题确实构成了羁押讯问。但由于被告有效地放弃了他的 Miranda 权利，并且没有有效地主张其获得律师帮助的权利，因此他的回答在审判中可以作为证据采纳。

（选项 C）在被告知 Miranda 警告后，被告明确表示他理解自己的权利，并愿意放弃这些权利与审讯人员交谈。因此，被告明确无误且有效地放弃了他的 Miranda 权利。

教学目的：警方可以自由讯问放弃其第五修正案（Miranda）律师帮助权的嫌疑人。但是，如果嫌疑人随后明确无误地请求律师帮助，警方必须停止讯问，直到嫌疑人的律师到场。如果警方继续讯问，嫌疑人的回答应被排除作为证据。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. V.
  • Davis v. United States, 512 U.S. 452 (1994) (ineffective assertion of right to counsel).
