questions.question:
A defendant was indicted and arrested for bank robbery. The defendant had an initial appearance before a magistrate judge in which he was notified of the charges and told that counsel would be appointed for him the next day. The police then required the defendant to participate with other prisoners in a lineup in which each person had to wear a white T-shirt and say, "Put your hands in the air." At the lineup, witnesses to the bank robbery identified the defendant as the bank robber. The next day, counsel was provided and the defendant was arraigned on the charges.
The defendant argues that his Sixth Amendment right to counsel was violated when he was denied counsel at two critical stages of the proceeding: his initial appearance in court before the magistrate judge and the lineup identification.
Was the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel violated?

choices.a: No.
choices.b: Yes, based only on the denial of counsel at the initial appearance.
choices.c: Yes, based only on the denial of counsel at the lineup.
choices.d: Yes, based on the denial of counsel at both stages of the proceeding.

Q84802 A defendant was indicted and arrested for bank robbery. The defendant had an initial appearance before a magistrate judge in which he was notified of the charges and told that counsel would be appointed for him the next day. The police then required the defendant to participate with other prisoners in a lineup in which each person had to wear a white T- shirt and say, "Put your hands in the air." At the lineup, witnesses to the bank robbery identified the defendant as the bank robber. The next day, counsel was provided and the defendant was arraigned on the charges.

The defendant argues that his Sixth Amendment right to counsel was violated when he was denied counsel at two critical stages of the proceeding: his initial appearance in court before the magistrate judge and the lineup identification.

Was the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel violated? 一名被告因银行抢劫被起诉并逮捕。该被告在治安法官面前进行了首次出庭，在庭上他被告知了所控罪名，并被告知第二天将为他指定律师。随后，警方要求该被告与其他囚犯一起参加一个列队指认程序，其中每个人都必须穿白色T恤并说：“把手举起来。”在列队指认中，银行抢劫案的目击者指认该被告为银行劫匪。第二天，律师被提供给了被告，被告就这些指控被传讯。

被告辩称，由于他在两个关键诉讼阶段被拒绝提供律师，即在治安法官面前的首次出庭和列队指认，其第六修正案的律师权受到了侵犯。

被告的第六修正案律师权是否受到了侵犯？
options:
A. No.
没有。

B. Yes, based only on the denial of counsel at the initial appearance.
是，但仅基于在首次出庭时被拒绝提供律师。

C. Yes, based only on the denial of counsel at the lineup.
是，但仅基于在列队指认时被拒绝提供律师。

D. Yes, based on the denial of counsel at both stages of the proceeding.
是，基于在这两个诉讼阶段均被拒绝提供律师。
data.explanation:
Sixth Amendment right to counsel
(critical stages after prosecution has commenced)

Interrogations & lineups
Preliminary hearings & arraignments
Plea negotiations & hearings
Trial & sentencing
Appeals

The Sixth Amendment right to counsel:

automatically attaches once judicial proceedings commence (eg, indictment, filing of formal charges, preliminary hearing, arraignment) and

guarantees that criminal defendants will have the assistance of counsel during all critical stages of prosecution—any event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial.

An indictment is a judicial proceeding that triggers a defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel. And a post-indictment lineup is a critical stage of prosecution because suggestive lineup procedures can lead to an unreliable and prejudicial identification. Since an attorney would have helped to ensure that the lineup was conducted fairly and protected the defendant's right to a fair trial, the denial of counsel violated his Sixth Amendment right.

In contrast, an initial appearance is not a critical stage if the judge merely conducts administrative tasks like notifying the defendant of the charges and explaining that an attorney will be appointed the next day. As a result, the defendant did not have a Sixth Amendment right to counsel during his initial appearance (Choices A, B & D).

But had the defendant been required to make decisions that might adversely affect the outcome of his trial (eg, deciding whether to enter an affirmative defense), then his initial appearance would have been a critical stage.

Educational objective: The Sixth Amendment right to counsel automatically attaches once judicial proceedings begin and applies to all critical stages of prosecution. A critical stage is any event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial.

第六修正案律师权
（刑事诉讼开始后的关键阶段）

审讯与列队指认
预审听证与传讯
认罪协商与听证
审判与量刑
上诉

第六修正案律师权：

一旦司法程序开始（例如，起诉、正式指控的提交、预审听证、传讯），该权利即自动产生，并且

保证刑事被告在所有刑事诉讼的关键阶段都能获得律师的帮助——关键阶段是指任何在缺少律师的情况下可能损害被告获得公平审判权利的事件。

起诉是一项触发被告第六修正案律师权的司法程序。而起诉后的列队指认是刑事诉讼的一个关键阶段，因为具有暗示性的列队指认程序可能导致不可靠且带有偏见的指认。由于律师本可以帮助确保列队指认的公正进行，并保护被告获得公平审判的权利，因此拒绝提供律师侵犯了他的第六修正案权利。

相比之下，如果法官仅执行行政任务，例如告知被告所控罪名并解释第二天将为其指定律师，那么首次出庭就不是一个关键阶段。因此，被告在其首次出庭期间不享有第六修正案律师权（选项A、B和D）。

但如果被告被要求做出可能对其审判结果产生不利影响的决定（例如，决定是否提出积极抗辩），那么他的首次出庭就会成为一个关键阶段。

教学目的： 第六修正案律师权在司法程序一旦开始后即自动产生，并适用于所有刑事诉讼的关键阶段。关键阶段是指任何在缺少律师的情况下可能损害被告获得公平审判权利的事件。

References

U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to assistance of counsel).

Rothgery v. Gillespie County, 554 U.S. 191, 198 (2008) (explaining that right to counsel attaches at commencement of judicial proceedings).

United States v. Wade, 388 U.S. 218, 237 (1967) (recognizing that post-indictment lineup is a critical stage of prosecution).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure: Right to Counsel
⚖️ 第六修正案律师权 (Sixth Amendment)

分析律师权是否受侵犯，必须遵循两步走逻辑：

  1. 权利附着 (Attachment)： 对抗性司法程序（如起诉 Indictment）开始了吗？
  2. 关键阶段 (Critical Stage)： 这是一个没有律师在场就会导致不公的关键阶段吗？

本题中，被告已被起诉 (Indicted)，因此第六修正案权利已经附着。现在的核心问题是：题目中的两个事件是否属于“关键阶段”？

1. 首次出庭 (Initial Appearance) 未侵权

虽然权利已附着，但如果法官仅进行行政性告知（通知罪名、告知将指派律师），且被告未被要求进行任何可能损害其审判权利的决定（如抗辩 Plea），则此时不是关键阶段。

参考判例：Rothgery v. Gillespie County (2008) - 权利虽在此刻附着，但若无实质性损害，律师缺席不构成违宪。
2. 起诉后列队指认 (Post-indictment Lineup) 侵犯权利

起诉后的列队指认属于关键阶段。因为指认具有暗示性风险，律师在场可以监督程序的公平性，防止不可靠的指认成为审判证据。

注意：这里是被告亲自参与的列队指认（Corporeal lineup），而非照片指认（Photo array）。

参考判例：United States v. Wade (1967) - 起诉后的列队指认必须有律师在场。
💡 MBE 避坑指南

考生常混淆“权利附着”与“权利受侵犯”。

  • 附着 (Attachment)： 只要起诉或正式指控，权利就有了。
  • 侵犯 (Violation)： 只有在随后的“关键阶段”拒绝提供律师，才算侵犯。

本题中，首次出庭时权利已附着，但因其非关键阶段，故无侵犯；列队指认既在附着后，又是关键阶段，故构成侵犯。

✅ 正确答案：C (仅基于列队指认)

Without a warrant, police officers searched the garbage cans in the alley behind a man's house and discovered chemicals used to make methamphetamine, as well as cooking utensils and containers with the man's fingerprints on them. The alley was a public thoroughfare maintained by the city, and the garbage was picked up once a week by a private sanitation company. The items were found inside the garbage cans in plastic bags that had been tied closed and further secured with tape. The man was charged in federal court with the manufacture of methamphetamine.
Did the search of the garbage cans violate the Fourth Amendment?

choices.a: No, because the man had no reasonable expectation of privacy in garbage left in the alley.
choices.b: No, because the probative value of the evidence outweighs the man's modest privacy claims in his garbage.
choices.c: Yes, because the alley was within the curtilage of the man's home and entry without a warrant was unconstitutional.
choices.d: Yes, because there is a reasonable expectation of privacy in one's secured garbage containers.

data.questionStem:
Q84813 Without a warrant, police officers searched the garbage cans in the alley behind a man's house and discovered chemicals used to make methamphetamine, as well as cooking utensils and containers with the man's fingerprints on them. The alley was a public thoroughfare maintained by the city, and the garbage was picked up once a week by a private sanitation company. The items were found inside the garbage cans in plastic bags that had been tied closed and further secured with tape. The man was charged in federal court with the manufacture of methamphetamine.

Did the search of the garbage cans violate the Fourth Amendment? 在没有搜查令的情况下，警察搜查了一名男子房屋后的小巷里的垃圾桶，发现了用于制造甲基苯丙胺的化学品，以及带有该男子指纹的炊具和容器。该小巷是由市政府维护的公共通道，垃圾每周由一家私营环卫公司收走一次。这些物品是在垃圾桶内的塑料袋中发现的，袋子被扎紧并用胶带进一步加固。该男子在联邦法院被控制造甲基苯丙胺。

对垃圾桶的搜查是否违反了第四修正案？
options:
A. No, because the man had no reasonable expectation of privacy in garbage left in the alley.
否，因为该男子对遗留在小巷里的垃圾没有合理的隐私期待。

B. No, because the probative value of the evidence outweighs the man's modest privacy claims in his garbage.
否，因为证据的证明价值超过了该男子对其垃圾的有限隐私主张。

C. Yes, because the alley was within the curtilage of the man's home and entry without a warrant was unconstitutional.
是，因为小巷位于该男子住宅的庭园范围内，无证进入是违宪的。

D. Yes, because there is a reasonable expectation of privacy in one's secured garbage containers.
是，因为个人对已加固的垃圾容器存在合理的隐私期待。
data.explanation:
The Fourth Amendment is violated when the government conducts an unreasonable search or seizure—ie, when police act without a warrant and no exception applies. A Fourth Amendment search occurs if one of the following tests is met:

Physical trespass test – the government physically intruded upon a constitutionally protected area to obtain information (eg, an intrusion upon the curtilage-the area immediately surrounding and commonly associated with a person's dwelling).

Reasonable expectation of privacy test – the government invaded a person's subjective expectation of privacy that society would find objectively reasonable.

In California v. Greenwood, the Supreme Court held that (1) public areas are not constitutionally protected and (2) persons have no reasonable expectation of privacy in items that are accessible or visible to anyone (including police). Therefore, police may freely inspect items left in a public area or exposed to the public.

Here, the officers did not conduct a search under the physical trespass test since the garbage cans were in a public thoroughfare located behind the man's house—not a constitutionally protected area (Choice C). Additionally, there was no search under the reasonable expectation of privacy test since the man had no objectively reasonable expectation of privacy in garbage cans that were readily accessible in a public alley (Choice D). Therefore, the officers did not violate the Fourth Amendment when they rummaged through the garbage cans.

(Choice B) The probative value of the evidence sought (ie, its tendency to make a fact more or less probable) cannot justify a violation of the defendant's Fourth Amendment right to privacy-no matter how modest. Instead, probative value is used to determine whether the evidence is relevant and admissible at trial.



当政府进行不合理的搜查或扣押时，即当警察在没有搜查令且没有例外情况适用的情况下采取行动时，就违反了第四修正案。如果满足以下任一测试，则构成第四修正案所指的搜查：

物理侵入测试 – 政府为获取信息而物理侵入受宪法保护的区域（例如，侵入庭园——即紧邻个人住宅并通常与之相关的区域）。

合理隐私期待测试 – 政府侵犯了个人主观上期待的、且社会认为客观上合理的隐私。

在“加利福尼亚州诉格林伍德案”(California v. Greenwood)中，最高法院裁定：(1) 公共区域不受宪法保护；(2) 个人对任何人（包括警察）可接触或可见的物品没有合理的隐私期待。因此，警察可以自由检查遗留在公共区域或向公众暴露的物品。

在本案中，警官的行为不构成物理侵入测试下的搜查，因为垃圾桶位于该男子房屋后的公共通道上，而非受宪法保护的区域（选项C）。此外，该行为也不构成合理隐私期待测试下的搜查，因为该男子对位于公共小巷内、随时可被接触的垃圾桶没有客观上合理的隐私期待（选项D）。因此，警官翻查垃圾桶的行为没有违反第四修正案。

（选项B）所寻求证据的证明价值（即其使某一事实更可能或更不可能的倾向性）不能成为侵犯被告第四修正案隐私权的理由，无论该隐私权多么有限。相反，证明价值是用于确定证据在审判中是否具有相关性和可采性。

Educational objective:
The government does not need a warrant to inspect items left in a public area or exposed to
the public since (1) public areas are not constitutionally protected and (2) persons have no
reasonable expectation of privacy in such items.

References
U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
California v. Greenwood, 486 U.S. 35, 40–41 (1988) (recognizing that individuals do not
have a reasonable expectation of privacy in garbage placed on a public street).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Fourth Amendment
正确答案：A
否，因为该男子对遗留在小巷里的垃圾没有合理的隐私期待。

本题的核心考点是：第四修正案对被遗弃在公共区域等待收集的垃圾是否提供保护？

核心判例与规则
California v. Greenwood (1988)
美国最高法院在该案中确立了规则：一旦垃圾被放置在房屋外部（curtilage 之外）的公共区域（如路边或小巷）等待收集，原主对该垃圾便不再拥有“合理的隐私期待” (Reasonable Expectation of Privacy)。

根据第四修正案，搜查（Search）的定义基于 Katz 测试的两个分支：

  1. 主观期待：个人是否表现出了实际的隐私期待？（本题中男子将袋子扎紧并封口，表现了主观期待）。
  2. 客观合理性：社会是否认为这种期待是合理的？（关键点：法院认为不合理）。
隐私期待范围图解
住宅内部
(最高保护)
庭园范围
(部分保护)
公共小巷
(无保护)

▲ 垃圾一旦进入公共区域，即失去宪法保护

本题案情拆解
1
位置 (Location)：垃圾桶位于“公共通道”(public thoroughfare) 的小巷中。这通常不属于住宅的庭园范围 (Curtilage)。
2
第三方接触 (Third Party Access)：垃圾是留给私营环卫公司收走的。最高法院认为，当你将物品交给第三方（收垃圾的人）时，你已经承担了该物品可能被其他人（包括警察、拾荒者、动物）翻阅的风险。
3
加固措施无效：虽然袋子被扎紧并用胶带封住（试图保护隐私），但这并不能改变其位于公共区域且准备被“销毁/带走”的本质。因此，客观上不存在合理的隐私期待。
为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 B 错误：“证据的证明价值” (Probative value) 永远不能用来事后证成搜查的合法性。宪法权利的衡量不基于证据是否有用，而基于搜查行为本身是否合理。
选项 C 错误：题目明确指出小巷是“由市政府维护的公共通道”。这不属于庭园范围 (Curtilage)。即使在庭园边缘，如果是为了公共收集而放置，通常也不受保护。
选项 D 错误：这是最大的干扰项。虽然使用了不透明袋子和胶带（Opague bags and tape），但这仅代表主观意愿。在 Greenwood 案中，法院明确指出，不透明的塑料袋不足以在公共街道上建立第四修正案的保护。
MBE 解题技巧： 遇到“翻垃圾” (Trash Pull) 的题目，只要垃圾是在公共区域等待收集，警察就不需要搜查令。记住关键词：No Reasonable Expectation of Privacy (REP).

questions.question:
FBI agents, without a warrant and without the permission of foreign law enforcement or judicial officers, entered a foreign country, kidnapped a businessman—a U.S. citizen wanted in the United States for drug-smuggling violations—on the street, and forcibly drove him back to State A. Thereafter, the agents, again without a warrant, broke into the State A home of the businessman's girlfriend and arrested her.
The businessman and his girlfriend were both indicted for narcotics violations. Both moved to dismiss the indictment on the ground that their arrests violated the Fourth Amendment.
How should the court rule on their motions to dismiss?

choices.a: Deny both motions.
choices.b: Grant the businessman's motion but deny the girlfriend's motion.
choices.c: Grant the girlfriend's motion but deny the businessman's motion.
choices.d: Grant both motions.

data.questionStem:
Q85014

FBI agents, without a warrant and without the permission of foreign law enforcement or judicial officers, entered a foreign country, kidnapped a businessman - a U.S. citizen wanted in the United States for drug-smuggling violations - on the street, and forcibly drove him back to State A. Thereafter, the agents, again without a warrant, broke into the State A home of the businessman's girlfriend and arrested her.

The businessman and his girlfriend were both indicted for narcotics violations. Both moved to dismiss the indictment on the ground that their arrests violated the Fourth Amendment.

How should the court rule on their motions to dismiss?

FBI探员，在没有逮捕令且未经外国执法或司法官员许可的情况下，进入一个外国，在街上绑架了一名商人——一名因在美国涉嫌走私毒品而被通缉的美国公民——并强行将他带回A州。此后，这些探员再次在没有逮捕令的情况下，闯入该商人在A州的女友家中并逮捕了她。

该商人和他的女友均因麻醉品犯罪被起诉。两人都以逮捕行为违反了Fourth Amendment为由，请求驳回起诉。

法院应如何裁定他们驳回起诉的动议？
options:
A. Deny both motions.
驳回两项动议。

B. Grant the businessman's motion but deny the girlfriend's motion.
批准商人的动议，但驳回女友的动议。

C. Grant the girlfriend's motion but deny the businessman's motion.
批准女友的动议，但驳回商人的动议。

D. Grant both motions.
批准两项动议。
data.explanation:
Grounds for Dismissing an Indictment


Grounds for dismissing indictmentFails to charge actual crime
Omits elements of crime
Deficient indictmentStatute of limitations has run
Improper venue or jurisdiction
Defective grand jury proceedingsAdmission of unqualified grand juror
Exclusion of grand juror based on race/gender
Prosecutorial misconduct
Constitutional violationFifth Amendment double jeopardy clause
Sixth Amendment right to speedy trial
Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment due process clauses
An indictment is a written statement by a grand jury that formally charges a person with a criminal offense after a finding of probable cause. It can be dismissed for
  • defective grand jury proceedings,
  • deficiencies in the indictment, or
  • violations of certain constitutional rights.
Here, both defendants moved to dismiss the indictment on the ground that their arrests violated the Fourth Amendment. But since a Fourth Amendment violation is not a proper basis to dismiss an indictment, both motions should be denied (Choices B, C, & D).

And even if an indictment could be dismissed based on a Fourth Amendment violation, the businessman's arrest was proper. Police can lawfully arrest persons:
  • outside their home if police have probable cause to believe that they committed a felony or
  • inside their home if police have a valid warrant authorizing their arrest.

Here, FBI agents kidnapped the businessman in a foreign country and drove him back to State A to face charges for narcotics violations. This arrest was valid since
  • it occurred on the street (outside his home) and
  • the police had probable cause to believe that he had committed a felony (drug smuggling).
And under the Ker/Frisbie doctrine, a defendant can be prosecuted in the United States even if he/she was forcibly abducted from another country without a warrant or the other country's permission. Therefore, the businessman was properly indicted.

In contrast, the girlfriend's arrest was invalid since
  • it occurred inside her State A home but
  • the police had no arrest warrant.
And though the court will not dismiss the indictment on this basis, she can move to suppress any evidence discovered from that illegal arrest at trial.

Educational objective: An illegal Fourth Amendment arrest is not a valid basis to dismiss an indictment, but evidence obtained from an illegal arrest can be suppressed at trial.

选项正确率统计：A选项 15%（正确选项），B选项 0%，C选项 43%，D选项 39%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

驳回起诉的理由


驳回起诉的理由未能指控实际罪行
遗漏犯罪构成要件
有缺陷的起诉书诉讼时效已过
审判地或管辖权不当
有缺陷的大陪审团程序接纳不合格的大陪审员
因种族/性别而排除大陪审员
检察官不当行为
违反宪法Fifth Amendment一事不再理条款
Sixth Amendment快速审判权
Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment正当程序条款
起诉书是大陪审团在认定存在合理根据后，正式指控某人犯有刑事罪行的书面陈述。它可能因以下原因被驳回：
  • 有缺陷的大陪审团程序，
  • 起诉书本身的缺陷，或
  • 对某些宪法权利的侵犯。
在本案中，两名被告均以其逮捕行为违反了Fourth Amendment为由，请求驳回起诉。但由于违反Fourth Amendment并非驳回起诉的适当理由，因此两项动议均应被驳回（选项B、C和D）。

并且，即使可以基于违反Fourth Amendment而驳回起诉，商人的逮捕也是合法的。警方可以合法逮捕以下人员：
  • 在住宅外，如果警方有合理根据相信其犯有重罪 或
  • 在住宅内，如果警方持有授权逮捕的有效逮捕令。

在本案中，FBI探员在一个外国绑架了该商人，并将他带回A州，以面对麻醉品犯罪的指控。这次逮捕是有效的，因为
  • 逮捕发生于街道上（其住宅之外），并且
  • 警方有合理根据相信他犯有重罪（走私毒品）。
并且，根据Ker/Frisbie原则，即使被告是在没有逮捕令或未经他国许可的情况下被从另一国强行绑架回美国，他/她仍可在美国被起诉。因此，对该商人的起诉是适当的。

相比之下，对女友的逮捕是无效的，因为
  • 逮捕发生于她在A州的家中，但
  • 警方没有逮捕令。
尽管法院不会因此驳回起诉，但她可以在审判中动议排除从该非法逮捕中发现的任何证据。

教学目标：一次非法的、违反Fourth Amendment的逮捕，并非驳回起诉的有效依据，但从非法逮捕中获得的证据可以在审判中被排除。

References

U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).

United States v. Crews, 445 U.S. 463, 474 (1980) ("An illegal arrest, without more, has never been viewed as a bar to subsequent prosecution . . . .").

Ker v. Illinois, 119 U.S. 436, 444 (1886); Frisbie v. Collins, 342 U.S. 519, 522 (1952) (holding that a forcible abduction does not preclude prosecution).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure / Fourth Amendment
正确答案：A (Deny both motions) 法院应驳回两人的动议。无论是商人的跨境绑架，还是女友的非法逮捕，都不能成为驳回起诉（Dismissal of Indictment）的理由。
核心考点：非法逮捕的后果

这是本题最大的陷阱。考生容易混淆“非法逮捕的后果”与“非法搜查的后果”。

  • 规则： 非法逮捕本身（Illegal Arrest）并不是驳回起诉（Indictment）的理由。
  • 救济措施： 如果逮捕违反了 Fourth Amendment，正确的救济措施是排除规则 (Exclusionary Rule)，即禁止在审判中使用因非法逮捕而获得的证据（如供述、搜出的物品）。
  • 结论： 即使逮捕完全非法，政府仍然可以将该被告带上法庭进行审判（只要有其他独立证据证明其有罪）。
United States v. Crews (1980)
最高法院明确指出："An illegal arrest, without more, has never been viewed as a bar to subsequent prosecution."（仅有非法逮捕这一事实，从未被视为阻止后续起诉的障碍。）
商人的情况：跨境绑架

对于被FBI从国外“绑架”回来的商人，适用著名的 Ker-Frisbie Doctrine。

即使被告是被强行绑架（forcible abduction）带入法院管辖区域的，法院依然拥有对该被告的对人管辖权 (Personal Jurisdiction)。

⚠️ 注意： 除非美国与该国签署的引渡条约中有明确条款规定“绑架即丧失管辖权”（这极其罕见），否则违反国际法或外国法律的绑架行为不影响美国法院的审判权。
女友的情况：无证入室逮捕

FBI在没有逮捕令的情况下闯入女友家中逮捕她，这确实违反了 Fourth Amendment（参见 Payton v. New York）。

  • 违宪点： 警方在住宅内逮捕嫌疑人通常需要逮捕令。
  • 后果： 逮捕是非法的。
  • 判决逻辑： 尽管逮捕非法，但如前所述，救济手段不是驳回起诉。她可以申请排除逮捕时获得的证据，但不能要求直接撤销案件。
💡 考试通关技巧

在 MBE 刑诉法题目中，当你看到被告提出 "Motion to Dismiss Indictment"（驳回起诉动议）时，请务必警惕：

  1. 大陪审团程序缺陷（如种族歧视）👉 可能驳回。
  2. 双重危险 (Double Jeopardy) 👉 可能驳回。
  3. 违反 Fourth Amendment (非法搜查/逮捕) 👉 绝不会驳回起诉，只能排除证据。

本题中，两人都试图用 Fourth Amendment 违宪来攻击 Indictment 本身，这在法律上是行不通的。

© MBE Exam Prep Guide | Criminal Procedure

questions.question:
A man was in jail after being arrested for burglary. When the police attempted to question him, the man invoked his Miranda rights and refused to answer any questions. The man was subsequently tried, convicted, and sentenced to a prison term for the burglary. Three years later, while the man was serving his prison sentence for the burglary, a police detective from a nearby town questioned him about an unsolved homicide. The detective did not know that the man had invoked Miranda at an earlier time. The man waived his Miranda rights and made several incriminating statements to the detective. When he was later charged with the homicide, the man moved to suppress these statements, claiming that his earlier refusal to waive his Miranda rights should have been honored.
Should the court suppress the statements?

choices.a: No, because the detective was unaware that the man had originally invoked his Miranda rights.
choices.b: No, because the man's prior invocation of his Miranda rights did not preclude the later interrogation.
choices.c: Yes, because the man had earlier invoked his Miranda rights, and the police were not permitted to resume questioning, even after a time lapse of years.
choices.d: Yes, because the man was incarcerated, and his earlier invocation of his Miranda rights shielded him from further questioning until he was released.

data.questionStem:
Q84824 A man was in jail after being arrested for burglary. When the police attempted to question him, the man invoked his Miranda rights and refused to answer any questions. The man was subsequently tried, convicted, and sentenced to a prison term for the burglary. Three years later, while the man was serving his prison sentence for the burglary, a police detective from a nearby town questioned him about an unsolved homicide. The detective did not know that the man had invoked Miranda at an earlier time. The man waived his Miranda rights and made several incriminating statements to the detective. When he was later charged with the homicide, the man moved to suppress these statements, claiming that his earlier refusal to waive his Miranda rights should have been honored.

Should the court suppress the statements? 一名男子因入室盗窃被捕后入狱。当警方试图审问他时，该男子援引其米兰达权利，拒绝回答任何问题。该男子随后因入室盗窃罪被审判、定罪并被判处有期徒刑。三年后，当该男子因入室盗窃罪服刑期间，一名来自邻近城镇的警探就一宗未决的凶杀案对他进行了审问。该警探并不知道该男子早前曾援引过米兰达权利。该男子放弃了他的米兰达权利，并向警探作出了几项对其不利的陈述。当他后来被指控犯有凶杀罪时，该男子动议排除这些陈述，声称他早前拒绝放弃米兰达权利的决定应得到尊重。

法院是否应该排除这些陈述？
options:
A. No, because the detective was unaware that the man had originally invoked his Miranda rights.
不应排除，因为警探不知道该男子最初曾援引其米兰达权利。

B. No, because the man's prior invocation of his Miranda rights did not preclude the later interrogation.
不应排除，因为该男子先前援引其米兰达权利并不妨碍后来的审讯。

C. Yes, because the man had earlier invoked his Miranda rights, and the police were not permitted to resume questioning, even after a time lapse of years.
应排除，因为该男子早前已援引其米兰达权利，即使时隔数年，警方也不得恢复审问。

D. Yes, because the man was incarcerated, and his earlier invocation of his Miranda rights shielded him from further questioning until he was released.
应排除，因为该男子被监禁，他早前援引米兰达权利保护他免于进一步审问，直到他被释放为止。
data.explanation:
A motion to suppress should be granted if the defendant's statement was taken in violation of his/her Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. To comply with this privilege, police must give a suspect Miranda warnings (eg, the right to speak to an attorney) before conducting a custodial interrogation. If the suspect invokes his/her right to counsel, any custodial interrogation must stop until:

the suspect's attorney is present

the suspect voluntarily reinitiates the interrogation or

14 days have passed since the suspect was released from police custody OR was no longer subject to coercive pressures associated with police custody (Choices C & D).

Here, the man invoked his Miranda right to counsel during a prior custodial interrogation, after which he was convicted and sent to prison (released from police custody). Three years later, a detective interrogated the man about a homicide. Since more than 14 days had passed since the man was released from police custody, the detective was free to question him after he waived his Miranda rights. Therefore, the man's motion to suppress should be denied.

(Choice A) An invocation of the right to counsel is valid against all police officers—including subsequent interrogators who are unaware of the invocation. Therefore, the court would not deny the man's motion to suppress merely because the detective did not know that the man had invoked his Miranda rights in a prior interrogation.

Educational objective: When a suspect invokes his/her Miranda right to counsel, all police interrogation must stop until (1) the suspect's attorney is present, (2) the suspect voluntarily reinitiates the questioning, or (3) fourteen days have passed since the suspect was released from custody or free of coercive pressures associated with police custody.



如果被告的陈述是在违反其第五修正案反对自证其罪的特权的情况下获取的，那么排除证据的动议应被批准。为遵守此特权，警方在进行羁押性审讯前，必须向嫌疑人发出米兰达警告（例如，与律师交谈的权利）。如果嫌疑人援引其获得律师帮助的权利，任何羁押性审讯都必须停止，直到：

嫌疑人的律师在场

嫌疑人自愿重新开始审讯 或

自嫌疑人从警方羁押中释放或不再受到与警方羁押相关的强制压力起已过去14天 (选项C和D)。

在本案中，该男子在之前的一次羁押性审讯中援引了其获得律师帮助的米兰达权利，之后他被定罪并送入监狱（从警方羁押中释放）。三年后，一名警探就一宗凶杀案审问了该男子。由于距离该男子从警方羁押中释放已超过14天，警探在他放弃米兰达权利后可以自由地审问他。因此，该男子排除证据的动议应被驳回。

(选项A) 援引律师帮助权对所有警官均有效——包括那些不知道该援引的后续审讯者。因此，法院不会仅仅因为警探不知道该男子在之前的审讯中曾援引其米兰达权利而驳回其排除证据的动议。

教学目的：
当嫌疑人援引其获得律师帮助的米兰达权利时，所有警方审讯必须停止，直到 (1) 嫌疑人的律师在场，(2) 嫌疑人自愿重新开始审问，或 (3) 自嫌疑人从羁押中释放或摆脱与警方羁押相关的强制压力起已过去十四天。

References

U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
Arizona v. Roberson, 486 U.S. 675, 682–85 (1988) (recognizing that the invocation of Miranda rights extends to interrogations about other crimes).
Maryland v. Shatzer, 559 U.S. 98, 110 (2010) (holding that a break in the chain of custody ends Miranda protection).

MBE 考点解析

米兰达权利的“有效期”与羁押中断

核心考点：羁押中断规则

本题考察的是美国宪法第五修正案（Fifth Amendment）中关于米兰达权利（Miranda Rights）援引后的时效性问题。

关键判例：Maryland v. Shatzer (2010)

根据 Edwards v. Arizona 确立的规则，一旦嫌疑人援引了律师帮助权（Right to Counsel），警方必须停止审讯，直到律师在场。

但是，Shatzer 案确立了一个重要的例外：

如果嫌疑人经历了“羁押中断” (Break in Custody)，且时间超过 14天，警方可以重新接触嫌疑人，再次宣读米兰达警告并寻求放弃权利（Waiver）。

案情分析与正确答案

在本案中：

  • 第一次审讯：嫌疑人援引了米兰达权利。
  • 中间过程：嫌疑人被定罪并入狱服刑，时间过去了三年。
  • 第二次审讯：新的警探重新宣读权利，嫌疑人放弃权利并招供。

关键点监狱服刑算不算“羁押”？

最高法院在 Shatzer 案中裁定，回到普通监狱人口（General Prison Population）服刑，被视为米兰达语境下的“羁押中断”。因为在普通监狱生活中，嫌疑人已经习惯了环境，不再受到当初被捕时那种高强度的、旨在迫使招供的强制性压力（Coercive Pressure）。

结论：

由于时间间隔（3年）远超 14 天，且嫌疑人已处于服刑状态（视为羁押中断），之前的米兰达援引已经失效。警方可以重新审讯。

正确答案是 B。

不应排除证据，因为先前的援引并不永久禁止后续的审讯。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (错误)：警探不知情

这是一个常见的陷阱。根据 Arizona v. Roberson，米兰达权利的援引对所有执法人员有效。警方的知识是“推定的”（Imputed Knowledge）。如果还在 14 天保护期内，即使第二个警探真的不知道，审讯也是违法的。本题的关键在于时间间隔，而不是警探的主观知情状态。

选项 C (错误)：永久禁止

米兰达权利的援引并不是永久的“护身符”。Shatzer 案明确拒绝了这种永久性的保护，设立了 14 天的界限。

选项 D (错误)：监禁即羁押

虽然嫌疑人在物理上被“监禁”（Incarcerated），但在米兰达法律分析中，已判刑的囚犯在普通监区的生活不被视为 Miranda 意义上的“羁押性审讯环境”（Custodial Interrogation Context）。因此，他在监狱里的这段时间构成了“羁押中断”。

💡 考试技巧

在 MBE 刑法题中，当你看到：

  1. 嫌疑人援引权利（我要律师）；
  2. 警方停止审讯；
  3. 释放 或 回到监狱普通监区；
  4. 时间流逝（注意 14天 这个数字）；

一定要立刻联想到 14-Day Rule (Maryland v. Shatzer)。只要超过14天，警方就可以“重启”游戏。

questions.question:
A woman who is a computer expert decided to dedicate herself to exposing persons who trafficked in child pornography. She posted a number of sexually oriented photographs on her website. The file for each photograph contained an embedded Trojan horse program (a program that would allow the woman to enter the computer of anyone who downloaded the photograph). A man downloaded one of those photographs onto his personal computer. Using the embedded program, the woman entered the man's computer and found a file containing a pornographic photograph of a child. She copied the file and turned it over to a federal law enforcement agency. A federal agent told her that a successful prosecution would require more than one photograph and offered her a monetary reward for additional photographs leading to the man's conviction. The woman entered the man's computer again, and this time she found hundreds of child pornography photographs, which she turned over to the federal agency.
The man was charged with multiple counts of violating federal child pornography statutes. He has moved to suppress the photographs that the woman discovered on his computer. The motion is based on both the Fourth Amendment and a federal statute forbidding interception of electronic communication without permission. The parties have stipulated that the woman's conduct in downloading photographs from the man's computer violated the interception statute.
How should the court rule on the defendant's motion to suppress?

choices.a: Deny the motion as to all photographs.
choices.b: Grant the motion as to all photographs, because the woman acted without probable cause.
choices.c: Grant the motion as to all photographs, because the woman violated the federal interception statute.
choices.d: Grant the motion only as to the second set of photographs.

Q85068

A woman who is a computer expert decided to dedicate herself to exposing persons who trafficked in child pornography. She posted a number of sexually oriented photographs on her website. The file for each photograph contained an embedded Trojan horse program (a program that would allow the woman to enter the computer of anyone who downloaded the photograph). A man downloaded one of those photographs onto his personal computer. Using the embedded program, the woman entered the man's computer and found a file containing a pornographic photograph of a child. She copied the file and turned it over to a federal law enforcement agency. A federal agent told her that a successful prosecution would require more than one photograph and offered her a monetary reward for additional photographs leading to the man's conviction. The woman entered the man's computer again, and this time she found hundreds of child pornography photographs, which she turned over to the federal agency.

The man was charged with multiple counts of violating federal child pornography statutes. He has moved to suppress the photographs that the woman discovered on his computer. The motion is based on both the Fourth Amendment and a federal statute forbidding interception of electronic communication without permission. The parties have stipulated that the woman's conduct in downloading photographs from the man's computer violated the interception statute.

How should the court rule on the defendant's motion to suppress?

一名女性计算机专家决定致力于揭露贩卖儿童色情制品的人。她在自己的网站上发布了多张性导向的照片。每张照片的文件都含有一个嵌入的木马程序（一种允许该女子进入任何下载该照片者电脑的程序）。一名男子将其中一张照片下载到了他的个人电脑上。利用这个嵌入的程序，该女子进入了该男子的电脑，并发现了一个包含儿童色情照片的文件。她复制了该文件并将其交给了联邦执法机构。一名联邦探员告诉她，成功的起诉需要不止一张照片，并向她提供了金钱奖励，以换取能导致该男子定罪的更多照片。该女子再次进入该男子的电脑，这一次她发现了数百张儿童色情照片，并将它们交给了联邦机构。

该男子被控多项违反联邦儿童色情法规的罪名。他已提出动议，要求排除（suppress）该女子在其电脑上发现的照片作为证据。该动议的依据是《Fourth Amendment》和一项禁止未经许可（permission）截取电子通信的联邦法规。双方当事人已约定（stipulated），该女子从该男子电脑下载照片的行为违反了该截取法规。

法院应如何裁定被告的排除证据动议？
options:
A. Deny the motion as to all photographs.
驳回针对所有照片的动议。

B. Grant the motion as to all photographs, because the woman acted without probable cause.
批准针对所有照片的动议，因为该女子在没有“合理理由”（probable cause）的情况下行事。

C. Grant the motion as to all photographs, because the woman violated the federal interception statute.
批准针对所有照片的动议，因为该女子违反了联邦截取法规。

D. Grant the motion only as to the second set of photographs.
仅批准针对第二组照片的动议。
data.explanation:
The exclusionary rule requires the suppression of evidence obtained in violation of the law or a defendant's constitutional rights (eg, from a warrantless search). Since this rule seeks to deter government misconduct, it only applies to the actions of government agents (eg, government employees, persons working on the government's behalf). Therefore, evidence is admissible if it was obtained by a private individual acting on his/her own behalf, without the government's knowledge or participation (eg, concerned citizens, vigilantes).

Here, the woman used an embedded Trojan horse program to conduct two searches of the man's computer. During the first search, the woman discovered a child pornography photograph. Since that search was motivated by her personal desire to expose persons who trafficked in child pornography, she was acting as a private individual without the government's knowledge or participation. Therefore, the exclusionary rule does not apply, and the court should deny the man's motion to suppress the first photograph.

Once the woman gave that photograph to the federal law enforcement agency, a federal agent offered her a monetary reward for additional photographs leading to the man's conviction. The woman then conducted a second search of the man's computer on the agency's behalf. Therefore, she was acting as a government agent during that search. And since the search violated the Fourth Amendment (no warrant) and the federal interception statute, the court should grant the man's motion to suppress the second set of photographs (Choice A).

(Choice B) Government agents generally need a warrant based on probable cause to conduct a Fourth Amendment search, but private individuals do not. Therefore, the fact that the woman acted without probable cause would only support the suppression of photographs obtained during her second (government) search - not her first (private) search.

(Choice C) Although the parties stipulated that the woman's conduct violated the federal interception statute, that stipulation only supports the exclusion of the second set of photographs (government search).

Educational objective: The exclusionary rule requires suppression of evidence that was illegally or unconstitutionally obtained by government agents - not private individuals acting without the government's knowledge or participation.



选项正确率统计：A选项 7%，B选项 0%，C选项 13%，D选项 77%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

证据排除法则（exclusionary rule）要求排除违反法律或被告宪法权利（例如，通过无证搜查）所获得的证据。由于该法则旨在遏制政府的不当行为，它仅适用于政府探员的行为（例如，政府雇员、代表政府工作的人员）。因此，如果证据是由私人代表其自身行事、在政府不知情或未参与的情况下获得的，则该证据是可采纳的（admissible）（例如，热心公民、义务警员）。

在本案中，该女子使用嵌入的木马程序对该男子的电脑进行了两次搜查。在第一次搜查中，该女子发现了一张儿童色情照片。由于该次搜查是出于她揭露贩卖儿童色情制品者的个人意愿，她是在政府不知情或未参与的情况下，作为私人行事。因此，证据排除法则不适用，法院应驳回该男子排除第一张照片的动议。

当该女子将该照片交给联邦执法机构后，一名联邦探员向她提供了金钱奖励，以换取能导致该男子定罪的更多照片。之后，该女子代表该机构对该男子的电脑进行了第二次搜查。因此，在该次搜查中，她是作为一名政府探员行事。并且，由于该次搜查违反了《Fourth Amendment》（无搜查令）和联邦截取法规，法院应批准该男子排除第二组照片的动议（选项A）。

（选项B）政府探员通常需要基于“合理理由”（probable cause）的搜查令才能进行《Fourth Amendment》搜查，但私人则不需要。因此，该女子在没有“合理理由”的情况下行事这一事实，仅支持排除其第二次（政府）搜查中获得的照片，而不支持排除其第一次（私人）搜查中获得的照片。

（选项C）尽管双方当事人约定该女子的行为违反了联邦截取法规，但该约定仅支持排除第二组照片（政府搜查）。

教学目标：证据排除法则要求排除由政府探员非法或违宪获得的证据——而非由政府不知情或未参与、且独立行事的私人所获得的证据。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Jacobsen, 466 U.S. 109, 113 (1984) (finding that the Fourth Amendment applies to searches conducted by the government and individuals working on its behalf, but not private individuals).
  • Nardone v. United States, 308 U.S. 338, 340 - 41 (1939) (explaining that evidence obtained in violation of a federal statute is subject to the exclusionary rule).

MBE 考点解析：第四修正案与私人搜查

本题考察的核心是美国宪法第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）的适用范围，特别是“政府行为”（State Action）与“私人行为”（Private Action）的界限。

核心原则：
第四修正案仅保护公民免受政府（Government）的不合理搜查和扣押。它不适用于私人（Private Individual）的行为，除非该私人是作为政府的代理人或工具行事。

案情两阶段分析

要正确回答此题，必须将该女子的行为分为两个独立的时间段进行分析：

第一阶段：私人搜查
行为：女子出于个人意愿（揭露色情贩子），利用木马程序搜查并发现第一张照片。
法律定性：这是纯粹的私人行为。政府并未参与、不知情，也未鼓励。
结果：证据可采 (Admissible)。
即使该行为违反了截取法规，但由于不是政府行为，宪法排除规则不适用。
第二阶段：政府代理
行为：联邦探员提供金钱奖励（Reward），要求更多证据。女子为了奖励再次搜查。
法律定性：此时身份发生了质的转变。由于政府的鼓励（金钱诱惑）和具体指示，她已成为政府探员（Government Agent）。
结果：证据排除 (Suppressed)。
作为政府代理人，她没有搜查令（Warrant），且违反了截取法规，因此触发证据排除法则。

判决逻辑 (Rationale)

法院应仅批准针对第二组照片的动议（选项 D）。

  • 针对第一组照片：虽然违反了联邦法规，但证据排除法则（Exclusionary Rule）旨在威慑警察的不当行为，不适用于私人。因此，第一张照片可以作为证据。
  • 针对第二组照片：女子已变身为政府工具（Instrument of the state）。政府不能通过利用私人来规避第四修正案对搜查令的要求。因此，第二组照片是非法搜查所得，必须排除。
💡
MBE 考试技巧：
在涉及搜查（Search）的题目中，首先问自己：“这是谁干的？”
  • 如果是警察 → 检查是否有 Warrant 或例外情况。
  • 如果是普通公民 → 检查政府是否在背后“指使”或“参与”。
一旦政府介入（提供奖励、指示、协助），私人行为即转化为政府行为（State Action）。

questions.question:
A federal grand jury that was investigating drug trafficking in the jurisdiction subpoenaed a witness to testify. The prosecutor advised the witness that he had a Fifth Amendment privilege not to testify if he so chose. The witness asked that his attorney be allowed to advise him inside the grand jury room, but the prosecutor refused to allow the attorney inside. After speaking with his attorney outside the grand jury room, the witness decided to testify. During his testimony, he made self-incriminating statements.
The witness was subsequently indicted for drug crimes. The indictment was based on the witness's grand jury testimony and on evidence seized in an unconstitutional search of the witness's home.
The witness has moved to dismiss the indictment.
Should the court dismiss the indictment?

choices.a: No, because the witness had no right to counsel inside the grand jury room and the illegally seized evidence did not affect the validity of the indictment.
choices.b: No, because the witness waived his constitutional rights by testifying.
choices.c: Yes, because the indictment was based upon illegally seized evidence.
choices.d: Yes, because the witness was denied his constitutional right to advice of counsel.

data.questionStem:
Q85013

A federal grand jury that was investigating drug trafficking in the jurisdiction subpoenaed a witness to testify. The prosecutor advised the witness that he had a Fifth Amendment privilege not to testify if he so chose. The witness asked that his attorney be allowed to advise him inside the grand jury room, but the prosecutor refused to allow the attorney inside. After speaking with his attorney outside the grand jury room, the witness decided to testify. During his testimony, he made self-incriminating statements.

The witness was subsequently indicted for drug crimes. The indictment was based on the witness's grand jury testimony and on evidence seized in an unconstitutional search of the witness's home.

The witness has moved to dismiss the indictment.

Should the court dismiss the indictment?

一个正在调查该司法管辖区内毒品贩运的联邦大陪审团传唤了一名证人作证。检察官告知该证人，如果他选择不作证，他拥有 Fifth Amendment 规定的不作证特权。该证人请求允许其律师在大陪审团室内为他提供建议，但检察官拒绝让律师进入。在与律师在大陪审团室外商谈后，该证人决定作证。在他的证词中，他做出了自证其罪的陈述。

该证人随后因毒品犯罪被起诉。该起诉是基于该证人向大陪审团提供的证词，以及通过对证人住宅的违宪搜查所扣押的证据。

该证人已动议驳回该起诉。

法院应否驳回该起诉？
options:
A. No, because the witness had no right to counsel inside the grand jury room and the illegally seized evidence did not affect the validity of the indictment.
不应，因为证人在大陪审团室内没有获得律师帮助的权利，且非法扣押的证据不影响起诉的有效性。

B. No, because the witness waived his constitutional rights by testifying.
不应，因为证人通过作证放弃了他的宪法权利。

C. Yes, because the indictment was based upon illegally seized evidence.
应，因为该起诉是基于非法扣押的证据。

D. Yes, because the witness was denied his constitutional right to advice of counsel.
应，因为证人被剥夺了其获得律师建议的宪法权利。
data.explanation:
Rights & privileges that may be invoked at grand jury proceedings


Constitutional rights
  • Privilege against self-incrimination (Fifth Amendment)
  • Equal protection (Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment)
  • Congressmen's privilege not to be questioned about legislative activities (speech or debate clause)
Privileges
  • Attorney-client privilege
  • Spousal privilege
  • Marital communications privilege
  • Psychotherapist-patient privilege
An indictment is a written statement by a grand jury that formally charges a person with a crime after a finding of probable cause. But since a grand jury only has the investigatory power to indict (not the judicial power to convict), a witness may only invoke certain constitutional rights during grand jury proceedings.

A witness may consult with an attorney outside the grand jury room (as seen here). But since a witness has no Sixth Amendment right to have counsel inside the grand jury room, the prosecutor had the right to refuse the witness's request to have his attorney inside. Therefore, the witness's self-incriminating testimony before the grand jury did not violate the Sixth Amendment, and the subsequent indictment should not be dismissed on this basis (Choice D).

The indictment was also based on evidence seized during an unconstitutional Fourth Amendment search of the witness's home. Pursuant to the exclusionary rule, illegally seized evidence should be suppressed at trial to discourage unconstitutional police conduct. However, the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings since the grand jury is an investigatory body - not a judicial one. Therefore, the illegally seized evidence does not affect the validity of the indictment, and it should not be dismissed (Choice C).

(Choice B) Though the witness waived his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination by testifying, he did not waive his Fourth or Sixth Amendment rights because they do not apply during grand jury proceedings. And since witnesses can only waive rights they possess, this is not a basis to deny the motion.

Educational objective: Since grand jury proceedings are investigatory in nature, only certain constitutional protections apply. A grand jury witness can consult with an attorney outside the grand jury room but has no Sixth Amendment right to counsel inside that room. And the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings.

选项正确率统计：A选项 71%（正确选项），B选项 14%，C选项 11%，D选项 2%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

可在大陪审团程序中援引的权利与特权


宪法权利
  • 反对自证其罪的特权 (Fifth Amendment)
  • 平等保护 (Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment)
  • 国会议员不因其立法活动而受质询的特权（言论或辩论条款）
特权
  • 律师-当事人特权
  • 配偶特权
  • 婚姻交流特权
  • 心理治疗师-患者特权
起诉书是大陪审团在认定存在合理根据后，正式指控某人犯罪的书面陈述。但由于大陪审团仅有调查并提起公诉的权力（而非定罪的司法权力），因此证人在大陪审团程序中只能援引某些特定的宪法权利。

证人可以在大陪审团室外与律师商议（如本案所示）。但由于证人并无 Sixth Amendment 权利要求律师进入大陪审团室，检察官有权拒绝证人让其律师进入的请求。因此，证人在大陪审团面前所作的自证其罪的证词并未违反 Sixth Amendment，后续的起诉不应基于此理由被驳回（选项 D）。

该起诉还基于通过对证人住宅的违宪 Fourth Amendment 搜查所扣押的证据。根据证据排除法则，非法扣押的证据在审判中应被排除，以遏制违宪的警察行为。然而，证据排除法则不适用于大陪审团程序，因为大陪审团是一个调查机构，而非司法机构。因此，非法扣押的证据不影响起诉的有效性，起诉不应被驳回（选项 C）。

（选项 B）尽管证人通过作证放弃了其反对自证其罪的 Fifth Amendment 特权，但他并未放弃其 Fourth 或 Sixth Amendment 权利，因为这些权利不适用于大陪审团程序。并且，由于证人只能放弃他们所拥有的权利，这不能作为驳回该动议的依据。

教学目标：由于大陪审团程序本质上是调查性的，因此仅有特定的宪法保护适用。大陪审团的证人可以在大陪审团室外与律师商议，但在室内没有 Sixth Amendment 规定的获得律师帮助的权利。并且，证据排除法则不适用于大陪审团程序。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to counsel).
  • United States v. Mandujano, 425 U.S. 564, 581 (1976) (finding that a witness has no right to counsel inside the grand jury room).
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Calandra, 414 U.S. 338, 351 - 52 (1974) (holding that the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析：大陪审团程序的特殊性

本题考察的是美国刑事诉讼法中关于大陪审团（Grand Jury）程序的两个核心考点：律师协助权的范围和证据排除规则的适用性。

正确答案：A

法院不应驳回起诉，因为证人在大陪审团室内无权要求律师在场，且非法获取的证据不影响起诉书的有效性。

核心考点一：证据排除规则不适用

规则：证据排除规则（Exclusionary Rule）通常禁止在刑事审判（Trial）中使用违反第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）获取的证据。但是，这一规则不适用于大陪审团程序。

法律依据：
大陪审团是一个调查机构（Investigatory Body），而非裁决机构。最高法院在 United States v. Calandra (1974) 中裁定，允许大陪审团使用非法搜查获得的证据，因为将排除规则延伸至此会阻碍大陪审团的调查职能。

结论：即使起诉书（Indictment）部分基于非法搜查获得的证据，该起诉书仍然有效。因此，选项 C 错误。

核心考点二：大陪审团室内的律师权

规则：虽然证人有权在作证间隙走出房间咨询律师，但第六修正案（Sixth Amendment）的律师协助权并不延伸至大陪审团室内部。

  • Outside: 证人可以离开房间咨询律师。
  • Inside: 律师不能进入大陪审团室陪伴证人。

法律依据：
在 United States v. Mandujano (1976) 中，法院确认证人没有宪法权利要求律师在大陪审团室内在场。

结论：检察官拒绝律师进入房间并未侵犯证人的宪法权利。因此，选项 D 错误。

其他选项分析

  • 选项 B (错误)： 虽然证人作证确实放弃了第五修正案（Fifth Amendment）的反对自证其罪特权，但这并不是法院拒绝驳回起诉的主要理由。法院拒绝驳回是因为起诉本身的程序和依据在法律上是允许的（即没有违反律师权，且可以使用非法证据）。

🎓 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在处理涉及 Grand Jury 的 MBE 题目时，请记住它是“低保护区”：

  1. 证据规则宽松：可以使用传闻证据（Hearsay）和非法搜查得来的证据。
  2. 律师限制：律师只能在门外等候，不能进屋。
  3. 目的不同：它的目的是决定是否有“合理根据”（Probable Cause）起诉，而不是判定有罪。
MBE Criminal Procedure Review

questions.question:
Police officers received a report that someone had been murdered. Upon arriving at the scene, a police detective interviewed the only eyewitness to the event. The detective's report, which was delivered to the prosecutor, stated that the eyewitness could not identify the perpetrator of the crime.
A man was subsequently charged with murder. His attorney requested that the prosecution turn over all evidence favorable to the defense. The prosecutor substantially complied with the request but inadvertently failed to disclose the detective's report. At trial, the eyewitness identified the man as the murderer.
The man's attorney learned of the report after the man was convicted. On appeal, the man's attorney argued that the prosecutor's failure to turn over the detective's report violated the man's constitutional rights. He further argued that there was a reasonable probability of a different outcome had the report been disclosed to the defense.
Should the appellate court reverse the man's conviction?

choices.a: No, because the evidence impeached the eyewitness's testimony but did not exonerate the man.
choices.b: No, because the prosecutor did not intentionally withhold the detective's report.
choices.c: Yes, because the man was prejudiced by the prosecutor's failure to disclose the detective's report.
choices.d: Yes, because the man's attorney requested that the prosecution turn over all favorable evidence.

questions.question:
A 17-year-old high school student decided to rob a convenience store. The student entered the store, brandished a pistol, and threatened to shoot the clerk unless she placed the contents of the cash register into a bag. After the clerk emptied the cash register, the student ordered her to lie on the floor and count to 500. To discourage the clerk from moving, the student fired the pistol at the floor immediately beside the clerk. The bullet ricocheted off the floor and struck the clerk in the head, killing her.
The student is now 18 years old and on trial for felony murder.
Can the state constitutionally seek the death penalty?

choices.a: No, because the death penalty cannot be imposed in felony-murder cases.
choices.b: No, because the student was under 18 years of age when he committed the crime.
choices.c: Yes, because the homicide occurred during the commission of an inherently dangerous felony.
choices.d: Yes, because the punishment is not disproportionately excessive in relation to the crime committed.

questions.question:
A man decided to rob a grocery store. During the robbery, he held a store clerk at gunpoint and hit the clerk in the face with the gun before fleeing the store. The police located the store clerk in the hospital the following day. While at the store clerk's bedside, the police officers presented a photo array of possible suspects to the store clerk and went through each photo without making any statements or gestures to him. The store clerk identified the man as the robber, and the man was subsequently arrested. Immediately after his arrest, the man was informed of his Miranda rights. He immediately invoked his right to counsel.
The man has been formally charged with armed robbery. Before trial, the man's attorney filed a motion to exclude the store clerk's identification.
How should the court rule?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the man had not been formally charged when the identification was made.
choices.b: Deny the motion, because there is no right to counsel at a photo array.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because the man did not have the opportunity to select or object to the photos in advance.
choices.d: Grant the motion, because the man invoked his right to counsel.

questions.question:
A man was arrested and charged with arson. The indictment alleges that the man committed the crime three years ago. The defense has learned that the prosecutor had enough evidence to prosecute the man several months after the arson but made a good-faith decision to delay bringing charges to investigate whether others were involved in the crime. The man contends that the delay has prejudiced his defense because a friend who could have provided the man with an alibi has recently died.
The applicable jurisdiction does not have a statute of limitations regarding arson.
Has the prosecutor's delay violated the man's constitutional rights?

choices.a: No, because the Constitution does not protect a defendant from pre-accusation delay.
choices.b: No, because the delay was attributable to the prosecution's good-faith investigation of the crime.
choices.c: Yes, because the delay violated the man's right to a speedy trial under the Sixth Amendment.
choices.d: Yes, because the man's case was prejudiced by the delay.

questions.question:
A defendant was tried for armed robbery. The state introduced evidence that a man, identified by witnesses as the defendant, entered a convenience store at 11:00 p.m. on March 5, threatened the clerk with a gun, and took $75 from the cash register.
The defendant did not testify, but his sister did. She testified that on March 5, at the time of the robbery, the defendant was with her in a city 300 miles away. On cross-examination, the sister admitted having given a statement to the police in which she had said that the defendant was not with her on March 5, but she claimed that the earlier statement was mistaken.
The court instructed the jurors that in order to convict the defendant, they had to find all of the elements of the crime beyond a reasonable doubt.
As to the defendant's claim of alibi, which of the following additional instructions would be proper?

choices.a: Alibi is a matter of defense and so must be established by the defendant; however, the burden of persuasion is by a preponderance of the evidence, not beyond a reasonable doubt.
choices.b: Before you may consider the defendant's claim of alibi, you must decide whether he has produced sufficient evidence to raise the issue.
choices.c: If the defendant's evidence has caused you to have a reasonable doubt as to whether he was the robber, you must find him not guilty.
choices.d: If you have a reasonable doubt as to whether the defendant was present at the convenience store at about 11:00 p.m. on March 5, you must find him not guilty.

data.questionStem:
Q85067

A defendant was tried for armed robbery. The state introduced evidence that a man, identified by witnesses as the defendant, entered a convenience store at 11:00 p.m. on March 5, threatened the clerk with a gun, and took $75 from the cash register.

The defendant did not testify, but his sister did. She testified that on March 5, at the time of the robbery, the defendant was with her in a city 300 miles away. On cross-examination, the sister admitted having given a statement to the police in which she had said that the defendant was not with her on March 5, but she claimed that the earlier statement was mistaken.

The court instructed the jurors that in order to convict the defendant, they had to find all of the elements of the crime beyond a reasonable doubt.

As to the defendant's claim of alibi, which of the following additional instructions would be proper?

一名被告因持械抢劫罪受审。控方（州政府）出示证据，证明一名被证人指认为被告的男子，于3月5日晚11时进入一家便利店，用枪威胁店员，并从收银机中取走75美元。

被告没有作证，但他的姐姐作证了。她作证称，在3月5日抢劫案发生时，被告正和她在一起，身处300英里外的一座城市。在交叉询问中，姐姐承认曾向警方提供过一份陈述，其中她称被告在3月5日并未与她在一起，但她声称之前的陈述是错误的。

法庭指示陪审员，若要裁定被告有罪，他们必须毫无合理疑点地认定犯罪的所有要素。

关于被告的不在场证明主张，以下哪项附加指示是恰当的？
options:
A. Alibi is a matter of defense and so must be established by the defendant; however, the burden of persuasion is by a preponderance of the evidence, not beyond a reasonable doubt.
不在场证明属于抗辩事由，因此必须由被告来确立；然而，其说服责任的标准是优势证据，而非毫无合理疑点。

B. Before you may consider the defendant's claim of alibi, you must decide whether he has produced sufficient evidence to raise the issue.
在你们可以考虑被告的不在场证明主张之前，你们必须判断他是否已提出充分证据来引出此争议点。

C. If the defendant's evidence has caused you to have a reasonable doubt as to whether he was the robber, you must find him not guilty.
如果被告的证据已使你们对他是否是抢劫犯产生合理怀疑，你们必须裁定他无罪。

D. If you have a reasonable doubt as to whether the defendant was present at the convenience store at about 11:00 p.m. on March 5, you must find him not guilty.
如果你们对于被告是否于3月5日晚11时左右在便利店现场存有合理怀疑，你们必须裁定他无罪。
data.explanation:
Criminal defenses: burdens & standards of proof


Negation defenseChallenges element of crime (eg, alibi, lack of intent) Fifth Amendment assigns burden to prosecution to prove element beyond a reasonable doubt
Affirmative defenseJustifies or excuses criminal conduct, but does not challenge element of crime (eg, entrapment, self-defense, duress) Statute assigns burden (prosecution or defense) & standard of proof (eg, preponderance, clear & convincing, beyond a reasonable doubt)
Due process requires that the prosecution prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, when a defendant asserts a defense that negates an element of the crime (eg, an alibi defense), the prosecution bears the burden of proof - not the defendant. However, the prosecution is not required to disprove an affirmative defense (eg, self-defense, duress) since it justifies or excuses the defendant's criminal conduct but does not negate an element of the crime.

Here, the defendant was on trial for armed robbery, which requires proof that he was at the convenience store at about 11:00 p.m. on March 5. Since the defendant's sister testified that he was with her 300 miles away when the crime occurred, her alibi testimony challenges an element of the crime that the prosecution must prove beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, the trial court should instruct the jury that if it has a reasonable doubt as to whether the defendant was at the convenience store, it must find him not guilty.

(Choice A) The burden of proof can be placed on the defendant only for affirmative defenses - not for defenses that challenge an element of the criminal offense (eg, alibi, lack of intent). Additionally, any level of proof can be imposed - eg, preponderance of the evidence, clear and convincing evidence, beyond a reasonable doubt.

(Choice B) A defendant must produce sufficient evidence to raise an affirmative defense, but not to raise an alibi defense since it negates an element of the charged crime. Instead, the prosecution must produce sufficient evidence to establish all elements of the criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt.

(Choice C) Although the jury must find the defendant not guilty if it has a reasonable doubt as to whether he was the robber, this jury instruction wrongfully places the burden of proof for an element of the crime on the defendant.

Educational objective: The prosecution must prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, the prosecution bears the burden of proof when a defendant raises a defense that challenges an element of the offense.

选项正确率统计：A选项 23%，B选项 5%，C选项 23%，D选项 47%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

刑事抗辩：举证责任与证明标准


否定性抗辩 (Negation defense)挑战犯罪要素（例如，不在场证明，缺乏意图）
Fifth Amendment（第五修正案）将证明犯罪要素的责任分配给控方，且证明标准为毫无合理疑点
肯定性抗辩 (Affirmative defense)为犯罪行为提供正当理由或予以免责，但不挑战犯罪要素（例如，圈套、自卫、胁迫）
法规分配举证责任（控方或辩方）和证明标准（例如，优势证据，清晰且有说服力的证据，毫无合理疑点）
正当程序 (Due process) 要求控方必须毫无合理疑点地证明刑事犯罪的每一个要素。因此，当被告提出一项否定犯罪要素的抗辩（例如，不在场证明抗辩）时，举证责任由控方承担，而非被告。然而，控方无需反驳一项肯定性抗辩（例如，自卫、胁迫），因为该抗辩是为被告的犯罪行为提供正当理由或予以免责，而并非否定犯罪的某个要素。

在本案中，被告因持械抢劫罪受审，该罪名要求证明他于3月5日晚11时左右在便利店现场。由于被告的姐姐作证称，在犯罪发生时，被告与她一同身处300英里之外，她的不在场证明证词挑战了控方必须毫无合理疑点地证明的一个犯罪要素。因此，审判法院应指示陪审团，如果他们对被告是否在便利店现场存有合理怀疑，就必须裁定其无罪。

(选项A) 举证责任只能就肯定性抗辩加于被告，而不能就挑战刑事犯罪要素的抗辩（例如，不在场证明，缺乏意图）加于被告。此外，可以施加任何程度的证明标准——例如，优势证据、清晰且有说服力的证据、毫无合理疑点。

(选项B) 被告必须提出充分证据以引出肯定性抗辩，但对于引出不在场证明抗辩则无此要求，因为它否定了被指控罪行的一个要素。相反，控方必须提出充分证据，以毫无合理疑点地确立刑事犯罪的所有要素。

(选项C) 尽管如果陪审团对被告是否是抢劫犯存有合理怀疑，就必须裁定其无罪，但这一陪审团指示错误地将被告的犯罪要素的举证责任加于被告。

教学目标：控方必须毫无合理疑点地证明刑事犯罪的每一个要素。因此，当被告提出挑战犯罪要素的抗辩时，举证责任由控方承担。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV § 1 (due process clause).
  • In re Winship, 397 U.S. 358, 364 (1970) (stating that the prosecution must prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure & Constitutional Protection

核心原则

举证责任与正当程序

本题的核心考点在于宪法正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause) 对刑事案件举证责任的要求。

根据最高法院在 In re Winship (1970) 案中的裁定：

控方 (Prosecution) 必须承担证明刑事犯罪每一个构成要件 (Every Element) 的责任，且证明标准必须达到毫无合理疑点 (Beyond a Reasonable Doubt)。
难点辨析

不在场证明 (Alibi) 的性质

很多考生容易混淆“不在场证明”与“肯定性抗辩”。

  • 肯定性抗辩 (Affirmative Defense)： 如自卫 (Self-defense)、精神错乱 (Insanity)。被告承认做了该行为，但有正当理由。对于此类抗辩，法律允许将举证责任转移给被告。
  • 否定性抗辩 (Negation Defense)： 如不在场证明 (Alibi)。被告声称：“我当时不在那里，所以我不可能犯罪。”

关键逻辑： 不在场证明直接否定了犯罪的核心要素——被告在场 (Presence/Identity)。既然“被告在场”是控方必须证明的要素，那么控方就必须毫无合理疑点地证明它。

如果要求被告证明自己不在场，实际上就是免除了控方证明被告在场的责任，这违反了宪法。

答案详解

为什么选 D？

正确选项 D "If you have a reasonable doubt as to whether the defendant was present at the convenience store at about 11:00 p.m. on March 5, you must find him not guilty."

解析：

这个指示正确地将焦点放在了合理怀疑 (Reasonable Doubt) 上，并且针对的是犯罪要素（在场/时间/地点）。

它不需要被告去“证明”什么，而是告诉陪审团：只要对“被告是否在场”这一要素存疑（无论是因为控方证据不足，还是因为姐姐的证词），根据宪法，就必须判无罪。

选项 A 错误： 声称不在场证明必须由被告确立且标准是优势证据 (Preponderance of evidence)。这是违宪的，因为这转移了犯罪要素的举证责任。
选项 B 错误： 要求被告提出“充分证据”才能让陪审团考虑不在场证明。这同样暗示了被告有某种初始负担。实际上，只要证据记录中有任何内容引发了对“在场”的怀疑，陪审团都应考虑。
选项 C 错误（高干扰项）： "If the defendant's evidence has caused you..."
这个选项很狡猾。它暗示合理怀疑必须是由被告的证据引发的。但实际上，合理怀疑可能仅仅源于控方证人的不可靠。将怀疑的来源限制在被告的证据上，不恰当地加重了被告的负担。
MBE 考试技巧

如何秒杀此类题目

  1. 识别抗辩类型： 看到 Alibi（不在场）或 Lack of Intent（缺乏意图），立即反应这是在攻击犯罪要素 (Element)。
  2. 寻找举证责任： 对于攻击犯罪要素的抗辩，举证责任永远在控方 (Prosecution)。
  3. 警惕陷阱： 任何暗示“被告必须证明...” (Defendant must prove / establish) 的选项对于 Alibi 几乎都是错的。
  4. 最佳指示： 正确的 Jury Instruction 通常是：“如果陪审团对[该要素]有合理怀疑，必须判无罪。”

questions.question:
A state grand jury investigating a murder learned that the key suspect might have kept a diary. The grand jury issued a subpoena duces tecum requiring the suspect to produce any diary. The subpoena made clear that the grand jury was seeking only the diary and not any testimony from the suspect. The suspect refused to produce the diary, citing his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination.
Under what circumstances, if any, may the grand jury compel production of the diary over the suspect's assertion of his Fifth Amendment privilege?

choices.a: It may compel production without granting immunity, because the suspect was not compelled to write a diary.
choices.b: It may compel production if the suspect is granted use and derivative use immunity from the act of production.
choices.c: It may compel production only if the suspect is granted transactional immunity.
choices.d: It may not compel production of a private diary under any circumstances.

Q85009

A state grand jury investigating a murder learned that the key suspect might have kept a diary. The grand jury issued a subpoena duces tecum requiring the suspect to produce any diary. The subpoena made clear that the grand jury was seeking only the diary and not any testimony from the suspect. The suspect refused to produce the diary, citing his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination.

Under what circumstances, if any, may the grand jury compel production of the diary over the suspect's assertion of his Fifth Amendment privilege?

一个正在调查谋杀案的州大陪审团得知，关键嫌疑人可能写有日记。大陪审团签发了一份携带物证传票（subpoena duces tecum），要求嫌疑人交出任何日记。该传票明确指出，大陪审团只寻求日记，而非嫌疑人的任何证词。嫌疑人以其根据 Fifth Amendment（第五修正案）享有的反对自证其罪的特权为由，拒绝交出日记。

在何种情况下（若有），大陪审团可以不顾嫌疑人主张的 Fifth Amendment 特权，强制其交出日记？
options:
A. It may compel production without granting immunity, because the suspect was not compelled to write a diary.
可以强制其交出而无需授予豁免权，因为嫌疑人并非被强迫写日记。

B. It may compel production if the suspect is granted use and derivative use immunity from the act of production.
如果嫌疑人因其交出行为而获得使用及派生使用豁免权，则可以强制其交出。

C. It may compel production only if the suspect is granted transactional immunity.
只有在嫌疑人被授予交易豁免权（transactional immunity）的情况下，才能强制其交出。

D. It may not compel production of a private diary under any circumstances.
在任何情况下都不得强制交出私人日记。
data.explanation:
The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination protects suspects from being compelled to provide self-incriminating evidence that is testimonial or communicative in nature (ie, testimonial communications). For example, the compelled act of producing a document is privileged if that act would prove that:
  • the document exists
  • the suspect possesses the document or
  • the document is authentic (ie, was created or written by the suspect).
However, the contents of a document are not protected by this privilege since the suspect was not compelled to create that content (Choice A).

Here, the grand jury compelled the suspect to produce any diary when it issued a subpoena duces tecum. The grand jury believed that the suspect might have kept a diary, so the suspect's act of production would prove that the diary exists, that he possesses it, and that it is authentic (self- incriminating evidence). As a result, the act of production is a privileged testimonial communication.

But the grand jury can still compel production of the diary over the suspect's assertion of this privilege if the suspect is granted either:
  • use and derivative use immunity - prevents the government from using self-incriminating testimonial communications (and any evidence derived from them) against the suspect in any way that could lead to a criminal prosecution (eg, to obtain a grand jury indictment, at trial) or
  • transactional immunity - protects the suspect from being prosecuted for any crimes associated with self-incriminating testimonial communications.
While testimony can be compelled by granting the suspect full transactional immunity, it is not necessary because the narrower use and derivative use immunity is the minimum grant of immunity required to comply with the Fifth Amendment (Choice C). Therefore, the grand jury can compel production of the diary if the suspect is granted use and derivative use immunity (Choice D).

Educational Objective: The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination protects suspects from compelled testimonial communications - eg, the act of producing a document that would prove its existence, possession, and/or authenticity. However, self-incriminating testimony can still be compelled if the government grants use and derivative use immunity.



选项正确率统计：A选项 38%，B选项 43%（正确选项），C选项 5%，D选项 12%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

Fifth Amendment 的反对自证其罪特权保护嫌疑人免于被强迫提供具有证言性质或传达信息性质的自证其罪证据（即证言性传达）。例如，如果强制交出文件的行为本身会证明以下事实，则该行为享有特权：
  • 该文件存在
  • 嫌疑人持有该文件或
  • 该文件是真实的（即由嫌疑人创建或书写）。
然而，文件的内容不受此特权保护，因为嫌疑人并非被强迫创作该内容（选项A）。

在本案中，大陪审团签发携带物证传票（subpoena duces tecum），强迫嫌疑人交出任何日记。大陪审团认为嫌疑人可能写有日记，因此嫌疑人交出日记的行为本身将证明日记的存在、其持有该日记以及其真实性（即自证其罪的证据）。因此，交出行为本身是一种受特权保护的证言性传达。

但是，如果嫌疑人被授予以下任一豁免权，大陪审团仍然可以不顾嫌疑人对此特权的主张，强制其交出日记：
  • 使用及派生使用豁免权（use and derivative use immunity） - 防止政府以任何可能导致刑事起诉的方式（例如，用于获得大陪审团起诉、用于审判），使用该自证其罪的证言性传达（以及任何由此派生的证据）来指控嫌疑人或
  • 交易豁免权（transactional immunity） - 保护嫌疑人免于因与该自证其罪的证言性传达相关的任何罪行而被起诉。
尽管通过授予嫌疑人完全的交易豁免权可以强制其提供证词，但这并非必要，因为范围更窄的使用及派生使用豁免权是满足 Fifth Amendment 要求的最低豁免授权（选项C）。因此，如果嫌疑人被授予使用及派生使用豁免权，大陪审团就可以强制其交出日记（选项B）。

教学目的：Fifth Amendment 的反对自证其罪特权保护嫌疑人免受强迫的证言性传达——例如，交出一份能证明其存在、被持有和/或真实性的文件之行为。然而，如果政府授予使用及派生使用豁免权，则仍可强制获取自证其罪的证词。

References

U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).

United States v. Hubbell, 530 U.S. 27, 43 - 44 (2000) (finding that the act of producing documents is a testimonial communication that can only be compelled by a grant of immunity).

Kastigar v. United States, 406 U.S. 441, 452 - 53 (1972) (holding that use and derivative use immunity is the minimum grant of immunity required to comply with the Fifth Amendment).

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law / Fifth Amendment
核心考点：交出行为原则
本题考察的是第五修正案（Fifth Amendment）中的反对自证其罪特权（Privilege Against Self-Incrimination）如何应用于文件传票（Subpoena Duces Tecum）。
关键区分：
第五修正案保护的是“被强迫的证言”（Compelled Testimony）。
1. 文件内容（Contents）： 通常不受保护。因为日记是嫌疑人过去自愿写的，政府现在并没有强迫他“写”日记，只是强迫他“交”出来。
2. 交出行为（Act of Production）： 受保护。虽然内容不受保护，但“交出文件”这个动作本身可能具有证言性质（Testimonial）。
为什么“交出行为”是证言？
根据最高法院判例（如 United States v. Hubbell），当政府不知道文件是否存在时，强迫嫌疑人交出文件，等于强迫嫌疑人承认以下三点：
📂 存在性 (Existence)： 文件确实存在。
✋ 持有权 (Possession)： 文件在我手里。
✅ 真实性 (Authentication)： 这些就是你们要找的文件。
在本题中，大陪审团只是听说嫌疑人“可能”（might）有日记。如果嫌疑人交出日记，就等于向政府提供了上述证言。因此，他可以行使第五修正案特权拒绝交出。
如何破解特权？(豁免权)
既然嫌疑人有权拒绝，政府若想强制获取日记，必须授予豁免权（Immunity）。
正确答案 B 的逻辑
使用及派生使用豁免权 (Use and Derivative Use Immunity)
根据 Kastigar v. United States，这是宪法要求的最低限度豁免权。
  • 它保证政府不会使用“交出行为”本身（或由此衍生的证据）来起诉嫌疑人。
  • 它不保护嫌疑人免受所有起诉（只要证据来源完全独立）。
因为这种豁免权已经消除了“自证其罪”的风险，嫌疑人就不能再拒绝交出日记了。
为什么其他选项错误？
❌
选项 A： 错误地认为只要内容是自愿写的就不受保护。它忽略了“交出行为”本身的证言性质。
❌
选项 C： 交易豁免权 (Transactional Immunity) 提供了更广泛的保护（完全免于起诉），但这并非宪法强制要求的。政府只需提供较窄的“使用豁免权”即可强制执行传票。
❌
选项 D： 私人日记并非绝对不可获取。只要解决了自证其罪的问题（通过豁免权），就可以强制交出。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧：
遇到 Subpoena Duces Tecum 的题目，先看政府是否知道文件确切存在（Foregone Conclusion）。
如果政府是在“钓鱼”（Fishing Expedition），嫌疑人通常有权拒绝，除非政府授予 Use and Derivative Use Immunity。

questions.question:
A man sought medical assistance for a gunshot wound to his leg in a hospital emergency room. He told a police officer at the hospital that he had been shot. The officer interviewed the man about the incident while the man was receiving medical treatment. At first, the man stated that he had been shot while attempting to buy drugs on a street corner. However, the discrepancies between the man's wound and his description of the shooting made the officer doubt the veracity of the man's story. The officer knew that the man was unable to leave the hospital due to his injuries, so the officer reminded the man that he did not have to talk with the officer. In response to further questioning, the man revealed that he had shot himself with his own gun.
The man had previously been convicted of a felony, so he was arrested and charged with illegal possession of a firearm by a felon. The man moved to suppress the statement that he had shot himself because he had not been provided with Miranda warnings.
Which of the following standards should the court apply to determine whether the man was in custody for Fifth Amendment purposes?

choices.a: Whether a reasonable person would have believed that he could terminate the interview.
choices.b: Whether it was reasonable for the police officer to believe that the man had shot himself.
choices.c: Whether the man believed that he could leave the hospital.
choices.d: Whether the police officer had probable cause to arrest the man.

questions.question:
A man was on trial for the murder of his former business partner. During closing arguments, the prosecutor made a remark about the man's failure to testify during the proceedings. The man's attorney promptly objected to the prosecutor's remark and moved for a mistrial. The trial judge overruled the objection, denied the motion for mistrial, and ordered the prosecutor to carry on with her closing argument. After considering the overwhelming evidence of the man's guilt, the jury returned a guilty verdict. The man's attorney has challenged the man's conviction on appeal, arguing that the trial court erred in overruling the objection to the prosecutor's remark and denying the man's motion for mistrial.
How is the court of appeals likely to rule?

choices.a: Affirm the conviction, because of the harmless-error rule.
choices.b: Affirm the conviction, because of the plain-error rule.
choices.c: Reverse the conviction, because there was reversible error.
choices.d: Reverse the conviction, because there was structural error.

Q85080

A man was on trial for the murder of his former business partner. During closing arguments, the prosecutor made a remark about the man's failure to testify during the proceedings. The man's attorney promptly objected to the prosecutor's remark and moved for a mistrial. The trial judge overruled the objection, denied the motion for mistrial, and ordered the prosecutor to carry on with her closing argument. After considering the overwhelming evidence of the man's guilt, the jury returned a guilty verdict. The man's attorney has challenged the man's conviction on appeal, arguing that the trial court erred in overruling the objection to the prosecutor's remark and denying the man's motion for mistrial.

How is the court of appeals likely to rule?

一名男子因谋杀其前商业伙伴而受审。在结案陈词中，检察官对该男子在诉讼过程中未能作证一事发表了评论。该男子的律师立即对检察官的言论提出反对，并请求宣告审判无效。主审法官驳回了反对意见，拒绝了宣告审判无效的动议，并命令检察官继续其结案陈词。在考虑了该男子有罪的压倒性证据后，陪审团作出了有罪裁决。该男子的律师已对该男子的定罪提出上诉，主张初审法院在驳回对检察官言论的反对意见和拒绝该男子宣告审判无效的动议方面存在错误。

上诉法院可能会如何裁决？
options:
A. Affirm the conviction, because of the harmless-error rule.
维持定罪，因为适用无害错误规则。

B. Affirm the conviction, because of the plain-error rule.
维持定罪，因为适用明显错误规则。

C. Reverse the conviction, because there was reversible error.
撤销定罪，因为存在可撤销的错误。

D. Reverse the conviction, because there was structural error.
撤销定罪，因为存在结构性错误。
data.explanation:
Fifth Amendment


Self-incriminationsecures right to refuse to testify against oneself
Grand juryrequires grand jury indictment for felony offense charged in federal court
Double jeopardybars multiple prosecutions for same offense
Due processprotects against unfair deprivation of life, liberty, or property
Takingsprohibits taking private property for public use without just compensation
The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination prohibits the prosecution from commenting on a criminal defendant's failure to testify at trial. However, a trial court's erroneous admission of such a comment does not result in the automatic reversal of a conviction on appeal. Instead, under the harmless-error rule, the appellate court should determine whether admission of the improper comment:

was sufficiently prejudicial as to require reversal or constituted only harmless error.

An improper prosecutorial comment is sufficiently prejudicial to require reversal if the comment contributed to the guilty verdict. Conversely, if the appellate court is convinced beyond a reasonable doubt that the comment did not contribute to the verdict, then the erroneous admission constitutes harmless error.†

Here, the trial court erroneously admitted a remark by the prosecutor regarding the man's failure to testify. But since there was overwhelming evidence of the man's guilt, the appellate court is likely to determine that the remark was not sufficiently prejudicial to require reversal (Choice C). Therefore, the appellate court is likely to affirm the man's conviction because of the harmless-error rule.

†The trial judge may attempt to cure potential error by immediately instructing the jury that the prosecutor's comment was improper and that the defendant has a constitutional right not to testify.

(Choice B) Under the plain-error doctrine, a defendant who failed to preserve a claim of error is still entitled to appellate relief if
  • the district court committed error under the law in effect at the time of the appeal,
  • the error was obvious under that law, and
  • the error affected the defendant's substantial rights.
Here, the claim was preserved when the man's attorney objected and moved for mistrial, so this doctrine does not apply.

(Choice D) An appellate court should automatically reverse a defendant's conviction if the trial court committed structural error - ie, error that affected the entire framework of the criminal trial and rendered it fundamentally unfair. However, reference to the defendant's failure to testify does not constitute structural error.

Educational objective: The privilege against self-incrimination prohibits the prosecution from commenting on a defendant's failure to testify at trial. However, an improper prosecutorial comment warrants a reversal on appeal only if it contributed to the guilty conviction.

选项正确率统计：A选项 68%（正确选项），B选项 7%，C选项 19%，D选项 5%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

Fifth Amendment


不得自证其罪的特权保证有权拒绝提供对自己不利的证词
大陪审团要求在联邦法院被控的重罪需经大陪审团起诉
一事不再理禁止对同一罪行进行多次起诉
正当程序保护个人免于其生命、自由或财产被不公正地剥夺
征收条款禁止在没有公正补偿的情况下为公共用途征用私有财产
Fifth Amendment 反对自证其罪的特权禁止检方对刑事被告人在审判中未能作证一事发表评论。然而，初审法院对此类评论的错误采纳，并不会导致上诉时定罪被自动撤销。相反，根据无害错误规则，上诉法院应确定采纳不当评论的行为是否：

具有足够的偏见性以至于需要撤销原判，或者仅仅构成无害错误。

如果不当的检方评论促成了有罪裁决，那么该评论就具有足够的偏见性，需要撤销原判。反之，如果上诉法院在排除合理怀疑后确信，该评论并未促成裁决，那么此错误采纳就构成无害错误。†

在本案中，初审法院错误地采纳了检察官关于该男子未能作证的言论。但由于存在该男子有罪的压倒性证据，上诉法院很可能会裁定该言论不具有足够的偏见性以至于需要撤销原判（选项C）。因此，上诉法院很可能会因为无害错误规则而维持对该男子的定罪。

†主审法官可以试图纠正潜在的错误，方法是立即指示陪审团，告知其检察官的评论是不当的，且被告人享有不作证的宪法权利。

（选项B） 根据明显错误原则，未能保留错误主张的被告人，如果出现以下情况，仍有权获得上诉救济：
  • 地区法院根据上诉时有效的法律犯了错误，
  • 根据该法律，该错误是明显的，并且
  • 该错误影响了被告人的重大利益。
在本案中，当该男子的律师提出反对并请求宣告审判无效时，该主张已被保留，因此该原则不适用。

（选项D） 如果初审法院犯了结构性错误，即影响了刑事审判的整个框架并使其根本上不公平的错误，上诉法院应自动撤销被告人的定罪。然而，提及被告人未能作证并不构成结构性错误。

教学目标：反对自证其罪的特权禁止检方在审判中对被告人未能作证一事发表评论。然而，不当的检方评论只有在促成了有罪判决的情况下，才能成为上诉撤销原判的理由。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Chapman v. California, 386 U.S. 18, 24 - 26 (1967) (applying the harmless error rule to an improper prosecutorial comment).
  • Barbara E. Bergman et al., 3 Wharton's Criminal Evidence § 3:22 (15th ed. 2020) (discussing improper comments or inferences regarding a defendant's failure to testify).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Procedure & Constitutional Law
核心考点：Griffin Rule

根据美国宪法第五修正案（Fifth Amendment），检察官禁止评论被告在审判中保持沉默（未能作证）的行为。这被称为 Griffin v. California 规则。

为什么选 A？

本题考察的是上诉法院审查宪法性错误时的标准。

✅ Harmless Error Rule (无害错误规则)

虽然检察官的评论确实侵犯了被告的宪法权利（Constitutional Error），但这并不意味着定罪会自动被撤销。

推理逻辑：

  • 前提：辩护律师在庭审时已经及时反对（Objected）并保留了异议。
  • 标准：对于已保留的宪法性错误，政府必须证明该错误在“排除合理怀疑”（Beyond a reasonable doubt）的程度上是无害的。
  • 应用：题目明确指出有“压倒性的有罪证据”（Overwhelming evidence of guilt）。这意味着，即使检察官没有那句不当评论，陪审团也几乎肯定会判被告有罪。

因此，法院会认定该错误未对判决结果产生实质影响，属于无害错误，从而维持定罪。

其他概念辨析
❌ Plain Error Rule (明显错误规则)

适用场景：当被告律师在庭审时未能提出反对（Failed to object）时使用。

本题情况：律师已经“promptly objected”（立即反对），因此不适用此规则。

❌ Structural Error (结构性错误)

定义：指那些从根本上破坏了审判公正框架的严重错误（如完全剥夺律师权、法官有偏见）。此类错误会导致自动撤销判决，无需进行无害分析。

本题情况：最高法院已裁定，违反 Griffin 规则（评论被告沉默）不属于结构性错误，必须进行无害错误分析。

💡 MBE 解题技巧

在处理上诉审查标准（Standard of Review）的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 有没有错误？（本题：有，检察官违宪评论）。
  2. 律师是否反对（Preserved）？
    • 没反对 ➡️ Plain Error（很难翻案）。
    • 反对了 ➡️ Harmless Error（政府需证明无害）。
  3. 证据强不强？
    • 如果题目说“证据确凿/压倒性” ➡️ 错误通常被视为Harmless，维持原判。

questions.question:
A suspect was taken into custody for questioning. After receiving Miranda warnings, which the suspect stated he understood, he was questioned by two detectives for three hours. The detectives told the suspect that the interrogation was about an illegal sale of automatic weapons. During this time, the suspect neither expressly waived nor expressly invoked his Miranda rights. Instead, he participated only sporadically in the conversation and responded to incriminating questions with silence.
Toward the end of the three-hour session, one of the detectives began to question the suspect about the recent murder of an arms dealer. The suspect was nonresponsive, so the detectives decided to pause the interrogation. As they were walking out of the interrogation room, one of the detectives asked the suspect, "Have you prayed for forgiveness for killing that man?" The suspect, tired from the hours of questioning, responded that he had. He then immediately told the detectives that he wanted to speak with an attorney. The detectives immediately terminated the interrogation and left the room.
If the suspect moves to suppress his admission about killing the arms dealer, how will the court likely rule on his motion?

choices.a: Deny the motion, because the interrogation immediately ceased after the suspect asserted his right to counsel.
choices.b: Deny the motion, because the suspect knowingly and voluntarily waived his right to remain silent by making the statement.
choices.c: Grant the motion, because the detectives failed to advise the suspect of the full subject matter of the interrogation.
choices.d: Grant the motion, but allow the prosecution to use the suspect's incriminating statement at trial for impeachment purposes only.

一名嫌疑人因受审问而被拘留。在收到其声称已理解的Miranda警告后，他被两名警探审问了三个小时。警探告诉嫌疑人，审讯是关于一起非法销售自动武器的案件。在此期间，嫌疑人既未明确放弃也未明确援引其Miranda权利。相反，他只是零星地参与谈话，并以沉默回应有罪指控的问题。

在三个小时的审讯快结束时，一名警探开始就最近一名军火商的谋杀案向嫌疑人提问。嫌疑人没有回应，因此警探决定暂停审讯。当他们走出审讯室时，一名警探问嫌疑人："你为杀了那个人而祈求宽恕了吗？" 嫌疑人因数小时的审问而感到疲惫，回答说他祈求了。他随即告诉警探，他想和律师谈谈。警探立即终止了审讯并离开了房间。

如果嫌疑人动议排除其关于杀害军火商的供述，法院可能会如何裁定其动议？
options:
A. Deny the motion, because the interrogation immediately ceased after the suspect asserted his right to counsel.
驳回动议，因为在嫌疑人主张其律师权后，审讯立即停止了。

B. Deny the motion, because the suspect knowingly and voluntarily waived his right to remain silent by making the statement.
驳回动议，因为嫌疑人通过作出该陈述，知情且自愿地放弃了其保持沉默的权利。

C. Grant the motion, because the detectives failed to advise the suspect of the full subject matter of the interrogation.
批准动议，因为警探未能告知嫌疑人审讯的全部主题事项。

D. Grant the motion, but allow the prosecution to use the suspect's incriminating statement at trial for impeachment purposes only.
批准动议，但允许检方在审判中仅为弹劾目的使用嫌疑人的有罪陈述。
data.explanation:
Incriminating statements obtained from a custodial interrogation may not be used against a suspect at a subsequent trial unless police provided procedural safeguards to secure the suspect's Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. Police safeguard this privilege by informing the suspect of his/her Miranda rights prior to a custodial interrogation (as seen here).

A suspect may then choose to specifically and unambiguously invoke a Miranda right - eg, by clearly and unambiguously asserting his/her desire to remain silent. Therefore, a suspect's silence in response to police questioning does not invoke Miranda rights, even if questioning was extensive. A suspect may also choose to expressly (eg, by signing a waiver form) or impliedly waive Miranda rights.

Waiver is implied when a suspect (1) has not asserted his/her Miranda rights, (2) understands those rights, and (3) engages in a course of conduct that indicates a knowing and voluntary waiver - eg, by making an uncoerced incriminating statement (as the suspect did here). Therefore, the court will likely deny the suspect's motion to suppress his admission about killing the arms dealer.

(Choice A) The suspect made the inculpatory statement before invoking his Fifth Amendment right to counsel and after initially waiving his right to remain silent. It is this - not the fact that the detectives immediately ceased their interrogation upon the suspect's request - that renders the statement admissible.

(Choice C) Police need not provide a suspect with the subject matter of the interrogation before administering Miranda warnings. Therefore, the detectives' failure to inform the suspect of the interrogation's full subject matter did not invalidate the suspect's waiver.

(Choice D) A voluntary and trustworthy statement taken in violation of Miranda is admissible to impeach a criminal defendant who gives contradictory testimony at trial. But an incriminating statement that does not violate Miranda is also admissible as substantive evidence.

Educational objective: Miranda rights may be expressly or impliedly waived. A waiver is implied when a suspect (1) has not asserted his/her Miranda rights, (2) understands those rights, and (3) engages in a course of conduct indicating waiver.



选项正确率统计：A选项 10%，B选项 70%（正确选项），C选项 4%，D选项 13%

在羁押审讯中获得的有罪陈述，在随后的审判中不得用于指控嫌疑人，除非警方提供了程序性保障以确保嫌疑人享有的第五修正案中免于自证其罪的特权。警方通过在羁押审讯前告知嫌疑人其Miranda权利来保障此项特权（如此案所示）。

嫌疑人随后可以选择明确无误地援引Miranda权利——例如，通过明确无误地主张其保持沉默的意愿。因此，嫌疑人以沉默回应警方讯问并不构成援引Miranda权利，即使讯问时间很长。嫌疑人也可以选择明示（例如，通过签署弃权书）或默示放弃Miranda权利。

当嫌疑人(1)未主张其Miranda权利，(2)理解这些权利，并且(3)从事了表明知情且自愿放弃的一连串行为时，即构成默示放弃——例如，作出了非胁迫下的有罪陈述（如本案嫌疑人所为）。因此，法院很可能驳回嫌疑人提出的排除其杀害军火商供述的动议。

(选项A) 嫌疑人是在援引其第五修正案的律师权之前，以及在最初放弃其保持沉默的权利之后，作出的有罪陈述。是这一点——而非警探在嫌疑人提出要求后立即停止审讯这一事实——使得该陈述具有可采性。

(选项C) 警方在发布Miranda警告前，无需向嫌疑人提供审讯的主题事项。因此，警探未能告知嫌疑人审讯的全部主题事项，并未使嫌疑人的弃权无效。

(选项D) 在违反Miranda规则的情况下获取的自愿且可信的陈述，在审判中可用于弹劾作出矛盾证词的刑事被告人。但是，一项不违反Miranda规则的有罪陈述，也可作为实体证据被采纳。

教学目的：Miranda权利可以明示或默示地放弃。当嫌疑人(1)未主张其Miranda权利，(2)理解这些权利，并且(3)从事了表明放弃权利的一连串行为时，即构成默示放弃。

References

  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 468 - 70 (1966) (listing Miranda warnings).
  • Berghuis v. Thompkins, 560 U.S. 370, 384 - 85 (2010) (holding that voluntary incriminating statement by suspect who has not invoked but understands rights constitutes waiver).
  • Colorado v. Spring, 479 U.S. 564, 577 (1987) (holding that a suspect's lack of awareness of an interrogation's possible subject matter does not invalidate the suspect's waiver of Fifth Amendment rights).
